The king, who had been clashing swords and struggling with Aaron, lightly pushed Aaron away and looked up at the sky. In the northern sky, a small white light was shining.
The king quickly understood the meaning of that light. He gritted his teeth in anger.
"Soldiers! Return to the castle! We must defend the castle."
The king quickly turned his horse around.
'Heaven helps us.'
Aaron, realizing the king had given up the fight, breathed a sigh of relief.
"Stop it! Give up the castle! The castle is doomed now!"
Aaron looked in surprise at the person who had spoken. It was Licia's voice.
"Insolent girl! How dare you speak to—"
For the king, abandoning the castle was akin to losing the war. Reacting to her voice, the king lunged at Licia with furious eyes, but Aaron blocked him again. The king clashed swords with Aaron once more. The moment Aaron received his sword, he felt as if his arm was being torn off.
"It will be as Dagmon said. The two cities will be completely destroyed. If you go into the castle now, you'll only die a dog's death. You and your soldiers alike."
Aaron said cynically.
"There are still people inside the castle. I am the king."
"So you do care about your people, after all."
"What did you say!"
The king, overcome with rage, lost his composure. Thanks to his loss of reason, Aaron was able to parry his sword a little more easily, which was Aaron's intention.
Aaron's stamina was almost at its limit. The king's sword had already grazed Aaron's body several times, inflicting wounds here and there, though none were fatal. Aaron thought he had to escape this situation somehow.
"Fighting me with your sword might actually be the way to preserve your life."
Upon hearing Aaron's words, the king's expression subtly shifted.
"This fellow. He's deliberately trying to buy time..."
As if realizing he had been tricked upon hearing those words, the king finally disengaged from Aaron and turned his horse around.
"All soldiers, gather at the castle!"
The king ordered all soldiers to return to the castle. Aaron knew that if he made it seem like he was buying time, the king would return to the castle. And that if he went there, he would die... But if he had continued to clash swords with the king, it would have been Aaron's life that was in danger. Watching the king's retreating figure as he withdrew his troops, Aaron thought.
'It seems I'll be the one who killed Dagmon's father...'
The light, which had appeared as a mere dot in the sky, had now grown to the size of a fingernail.
"Aaron!"
Licia cried out Aaron's name. At first glance, it might not have been obvious, but listening closely, one could tell her voice was filled with anger.
"Phew... That was close. If the battle had continued like this, we wouldn't have survived. It's better this way."
Aaron said with a relieved expression and then led the people.
"Everyone, keep moving forward. A huge explosion will occur in a few minutes. It will be safest to be as far away as possible."
However, Licia jumped out of the carriage and approached Aaron with an enraged face.
"Aaron! How could you do that?"
Licia shouted loudly.
"What?"
"Why did you let Dagmon's father go to the castle?"
"Well..."
Aaron was speechless. He wanted to say that he would have died if he hadn't, but Aaron couldn't bring himself to utter those words.
"I'm going to go get him!"
Licia climbed back into the carriage, sat on the driver's seat, and grabbed the reins.
"What are you doing, Licia!"
"Let go! I'm going alone!"
Licia drove the carriage with all her might. Although she didn't know how to drive a carriage, she had seen it done and spurred the horses on.
Aaron quickly spurred his horse to chase Licia's carriage. Aaron's horse was exhausted from running on the battlefield for a long time. So, catching up to Licia's carriage, pulled by two horses, was no easy feat.
"Licia! Licia! Listen to me!"
Aaron desperately called out to Licia, but the angry Licia drove the carriage without looking back. In fact, the distance between them was growing. Aaron began to shed his heavy armor, piece by piece.
First his helmet, then his armor, chest plate, and even his iron boots...
Aaron realized anew how difficult it was to take off each of these heavy items. Before long, he was wearing no armor except for his father's sword. Only then, with a lighter Aaron on its back, did Aaron's horse gain speed faster than the carriage. Aaron rode his horse right up next to Licia's carriage.
"Licia! Licia! I said listen to me!"
Aaron shouted urgently.
"Hmph. No need to listen. Not to someone like Aaron."
Licia ignored his voice.
Before long, the king's rear guard began to appear. Aaron grew anxious. Aaron looked at Licia with a piteous gaze and said.
"You fool. You'll die before you even reach the king."
But Licia replied without even looking at Aaron.
"Whether someone dies or not. Wasn't that what you wanted?"
"What are you talking about!"
Aaron moved closer to transfer to the carriage. Aaron grabbed the end of the carriage and jumped with all his might. Aaron tumbled into the back cargo compartment of the carriage. He succeeded in getting onto the carriage properly, but due to the force of his jump, he hit his waist on the corner of a piece of cargo inside the compartment.
"Ugh..."
He endured the pain and stood up.
"Licia. I was wrong, so please stop this."
Licia, startled by the voice coming from right behind her, unconsciously turned around and looked at Aaron.
"No... How..."
Licia was most surprised that Aaron had gotten onto the carriage.
"Licia! Look straight ahead!"
Aaron spotted a large rock in the carriage's path and shouted.
"Kyaa!"
Only then did Licia try to change the horses' direction, but the carriage only shook violently. Realizing it was too late, Aaron quickly grabbed Licia and jumped out of the carriage.
The carriage made a loud noise, its wheels flew off, and it overturned, severely damaged. Aaron barely escaped the carriage by a hair'

"Dagmon... I truly never expected this. For you, whom I trusted most, to betray your father..."

The king, armored, stood on the high rampart, watching the battle on the southern wall with disbelief, filled with anger and bitterness. The battle had begun yesterday at dawn. The rampart of the southern wall was already half-burnt from magic attacks, and smoke still billowed into the sky.

A minister came to the king to report.
"The tide is slowly turning in our favor. The enemy seems to be planning to buy time by fleeing into the southern valley."
"The southern valley? Do the enemies intend to meet their end there? Or do they have other reinforcements? Instruct them to strengthen the front lines and not to lower their guard in the rear."
"Your command will be obeyed."
"And how is the Light Magic progressing? If they are relying on the Light Magic of the Ceres Kingdom, we must complete that spell first."
"The Light Magic has consumed more magical power from the mages than expected, but it is progressing smoothly. It is almost complete."
"Hurry as much as possible. Dagmon has outsmarted us. He can attack with Light Magic from the Ceres Kingdom while his forces stall and hold out in the southern valley. We cannot lose the victory we have almost secured."
"Rumors about the Light Magic have spread, causing great unrest among the city residents, and they are fleeing the castle."
"Control all exits and kill anyone who tries to escape."

The king said this as if it were nothing. However, the minister's voice was different.
"Rumors have already spread among the residents that this city will be destroyed, and most of the army is engaged in battle, making it difficult to control the residents. Many residents have already begun to flee through each gate, and the southern gate, in particular, is so crowded with people that our army is struggling to fight. This is causing unrest not only among the residents but also among our fighting forces. If this continues, public morale and military morale will fall into uncontrollable chaos. There are already casualties from the battle, but many of our soldiers are getting entangled with residents, leading to more casualties. If this continues, it will become even more severe."
The king covered his face and cried out.
"Damn it! Dagmon, you bastard. Then what do you want me to do!"
"Perhaps Your Majesty could personally calm the residents and lead the soldiers to fight..."
The king thought for a moment and then replied.
"Very well. I will do so. Prepare a statement for the residents and my words."

"Lishia! Lishia!"
Aaron entered the southern valley camp, shouting Lishia's name. His body was covered in dirt and sweat, clearly exhausted.
"Aaron! Why are you only just arriving? Why are so many wounded coming? Explain this. These aren't soldiers."
"Things turned out that way. More importantly, how are the battle preparations here?"
"Battle preparations? Are we fighting here too?"
Lishia asked back, surprised.
"I told you last time. The final operation is to buy time at this entrance. Soon, Sueb's last unit will retreat and enter. And we will regroup our forces here and buy time."
"I've done as you asked, half-believing, but here? There's nowhere else to run. Holding out against the Laodicean army here is inviting death."
"We entrusted our lives to Dagmon from the beginning."
"Did Dagmon really know things would turn out like this?"
Lishia's face clearly showed disbelief and a sense of betrayal.
"I don't know. But he must have had something in mind. Seeing as he's accepted the sacrifice of so many people."
"Dagmon really..."
Lishia still looked disbelieving.
"Let's get ready before Sueb arrives."
Aaron urged Lishia. Just then, a soldier rushed to Aaron with a message.
"General Aaron! Captain Sueb says the retreat will be faster than expected. Enemy forces are being reinforced, and the chaos within the castle is reportedly calming down."
"Unfortunately for us, the king isn't a fool, it seems."
Aaron said, looking troubled.

When Dagmon opened his eyes, it was already midday.
"Oh... where is this?"
He had woken up in an underground dungeon. A palm-sized ray of sunlight streamed through the small window of the cell, and they were seated haphazardly, leaning against the wooden built-in bed in the cell.
It was damp, cockroaches scurried about, and the floor was almost submerged in water. Dagmon's hands were tied behind his back, and Sera, also bound, was leaning against Dagmon's chest, still unconscious.
"Sera?"
Dagmon called Sera's name with a worried voice.
"Mmm..."
Contrary to Dagmon's worry, Sera slowly regained consciousness.
"Where are we?"
Sera must have realized she was leaning against Dagmon's chest upon waking, but she didn't try to change her position.
"Was it Arie? That girl. She, unfortunately, betrayed Sera."
"No way... that can't be."
"It's true. She was the one who attacked me."
"It's true she's a tomboy, but she's not the kind of girl to betray me."
Sera said, her voice indicating she absolutely couldn't believe it.
"You never know what's in people's hearts. Anyway, this is a big problem. Eventually, even if we're tied up, the summoning spell to the Laodicean Kingdom will happen automatically, but our plan will be ruined. By now, the battle must be in full swing in the Laodicean Kingdom. If this continues, both cities will be annihilated."
Sera asked cautiously, in a small voice.
"....Then, will this castle be destroyed too?"
"It might be, if the timing of our summoning isn't just right."
"My mother too?"
Sera looked up at Dagmon and asked, as if it were a sudden question. Dagmon also looked at Sera, who was leaning against him. Dagmon was surprised when he saw her.
Her eyes no longer looked strong like they used to. Perhaps due to the loneliness of being alone without Elon or Sibiya, she now looked infinitely fragile.
"I don't want to be alone anymore. Even Arie... I never thought..."
Sera suddenly lowered her head. Dagmon read Sera's thoughts and was suddenly speechless. Dagmon wanted to comfort Sera, feeling pity for her, but no good words came to mind suddenly. Her appearance just came to Dagmon as a great pain, like his own sin.
"........."
Sera, mentally exhausted, now seemed to completely rely on Dagmon. Dagmon forced a smile and encouraged Sera.
"Don't worry. There will be a way out. I will never leave you alone, so don't worry."
He hooked his fingers, searching for equipment in his sleeve. But then he made a troubled expression.
'Damn it. Anania has already searched our bodies...'
Just then, the sound of splashing water was heard.
"Someone's coming. Pretend to be unconscious."
Sera and Dagmon closed their eyes again. But the voice they heard was a girl's call.
"Princess. Princess."
He had heard that voice before. Dagmon opened his eyes and looked at her. She stood outside the cell, her skirt pulled up to her knees so her clothes wouldn't get wet in the cell's water. The little mage named Arie.
"Arie?"
Sera's voice still held affection rather than hatred for being betrayed.
"Yes. It's me."
"Did you really? Me..."
"Hehe. No. I'm sorry about yesterday. Did you think I would abandon you, Princess?"
She chuckled lightly, reading Sera's thoughts, and replied.
"B'ol (practical heat magic)."
As she chanted the spell at the cell door, it clicked open lightly. She untied Sera's hands and said,
"We can't defeat General Herodion within this palace with just our strength. I did it because I was afraid you might lose your life, Princess."
"So that's what it was. By the way, what about the Light Magic?"
Dagmon interjected, sounding relieved.
"It's been delayed a bit, but it will be completed soon. Probably by evening. And the target, as you might have guessed, is the city of Laodicea."
"My mother?"
This time Sera asked.
"It will be difficult to rescue the Queen. She's too close to Anania's office. Anania is enjoying the Queen's suffering. I feel sorry for the Queen. She's already become a wreck because of Anania's medicine. From what I sense, she doesn't have much longer to live anyway."
"My mother...?"
That news was quite a shock to Sera.
"Hurry and follow me."
However, Arie, as if this matter was more urgent, spoke in a slightly irritable voice, leading the way and urging Sera. Dagmon looked at Sera. Sera's face looked half-dazed. Dagmon had no memory of his mother, who had died giving birth to him. But he knew better than anyone the shock of losing a loved one.
"Sera?"
Dagmon called Sera's name with a worried voice.
"Ah... I have to go."
Sera again tried to act composed, as if not to be a burden.
Arie guided them. Thanks to Arie using Svanya (hiding magic), they could pass soldiers quite easily. However, important doors had soldiers with a bit of magical power stationed there, so they couldn't get through with hiding magic.
"Arie? Where are we going?"
Sera asked, following Arie.
"My secret passage."
After walking for a while, she entered a place within the castle where a forest grew thick. Following Arie, they found a magic circle drawn in the middle of the forest.
"This magic circle is connected to the magic circle in the forest outside the castle. Using this, we can easily escape. I made it to escape."

I've been putting it off, but I think the time has come."
"Wait. What about light magic?"
Dagmon asked, flustered.
"It has nothing to do with me anyway. And, Princess, forget about the Queen. It's already too late. Those events were already destined to happen. There's no need to feel sorry for things that are beyond our power."
She spoke with a coldness that was unbelievable for a child.
"Do you even know how many people will die?"
Dagmon asked Arie.
"About 10,000 people from both countries combined. But everyone dies once anyway." Arie turned her head and said simply. Then she continued without hesitation.
"Prince, what did you think you could do?"
Arie's piercing question somehow struck Dagmon's heart. Dagmon couldn't answer and looked into Arie's eyes. Arie's eyes looked like a deep lake. In front of her lake-like gaze, which seemed to reflect everything, anyone would instinctively speak the truth.
"Your plan was surprisingly meticulous. If you lived according to your will, I lived according to fate. Fate often deviates from one's will and plans. You must have experienced that fact as much as I have, haven't you? Sometimes, you have to do things even if you don't want to. Didn't you expect such an outcome anyway, Prince? If not, why did you send Aaron and the villagers to the southern valley?"
Dagmon was startled. She asked as if she knew everything precisely.
"No? How do you know all that?"
Sera asked, surprised.
"I can see everything. The movements of this world... This is also my destiny. My shackles given by God."
"Then you knew we would come here?"
"No, I didn't know. What I just told you was a revelation I received yesterday. Let's stop talking and go. There are things even a prince and princess cannot do. The wheel of fate is already turning."
"But Mother!"
Sera cried out in despair.
"The Queen will pass away this evening, not by a light spell."
"Hmph. Then I'd rather stay by Mother's side and watch her pass."
Sera burst into tears.
"Princess, that is not your destiny. You must leave with the Prince. That is your duty, and my duty is to send you out of the castle."
Somehow, her voice contained an irresistible power, and Sera couldn't move a single step.
As Arie activated her magic, a magic circle identical to the one drawn on the floor appeared in light, and soon that magic circle swallowed Arie, Dagmon, and Sera.

Inside the walls of Brugia, the capital of the Kingdom of Ceres, was bustling with many city dwellers. In the middle of that street was a large road leading to the castle, and a single handcart was moving slowly down the middle of it. The cart was piled high with fodder for horses, and a small, black-skinned, white-haired old man was pulling it with difficulty. On the cart sat a country girl with braided blonde hair, wearing a straw hat, talking about something with the old man who appeared to be her father.
The cart gradually approached the castle gate, and eventually reached the front of it.
“Stop!”
The soldiers guarding the castle gate began to inspect the cart.
“What is in this cart?”
A soldier stopped the cart and asked.
“It’s fodder for horses.”
The old man replied.
“Just fodder?”
The soldier looked at the cart as if he couldn't believe what he saw right in front of him. All the while, his gaze kept darting to the maiden on the cart.
“Alright. You may enter.”
The old man struggled to pull the cart inside. Just then, the soldier blocked their path again.
“Wait. That maiden must stay here.”
“Huh? What do you mean?”
The old man asked in a flustered voice.
“The responsibility for transporting the fodder lies only with you. Whether she's your daughter or not, that woman has no responsibility for the transport, does she? We cannot simply let her into the palace.”
As he spoke, the soldier leered at the maiden, scanning her up and down. The maiden hid her face with her straw hat, avoiding the soldier's gaze.
“Soldier. Even so, my daughter is my daughter. If that's the case...”
The old man spoke as if resigned, then rummaged through the hay bales in the cart and pulled something out. What he held in his hand was a bottle of liquor.
“Actually, this cart is going from Lord Huria, the landlord of Kolgus province, to Lord Anania. And this maiden is General Herodion's personal servant...”
Only then did the soldier look surprised, then cleared his throat as if nothing had happened...
“Oh? Ahem. Ahem. Well then, why didn't you say so earlier?”
“Still, since you've gone to the trouble, I'll give you a bottle of precious liquor.”
“You really don't have to...”
The soldier waved his hand in refusal, but his eyes were actually fixed on the bottle of liquor with a longing look.
“Don't refuse, please take it.”
The old man practically pushed the bottle into the soldier's hand, then quickly pulled the cart into the castle.
After entering the castle for a while, the cart stopped in a place where people couldn't see them.
“Where is Kolgus province, and who is Huria?”
The maiden jumped down from the cart and asked. At that moment, the straw hat she was wearing fell to the ground. She was Sera.
“I don't know either. I just made it up.”
The old man's voice was not his own. He peeled off the beard from his face.
“Dagmon's disguise skills are amazing. To even change your skin color. And that voice was so funny.”
As Dagmon wiped his face with a towel, the wrinkles disappeared, and his original coppery skin color returned.
“Thanks for the compliment. By the way, where in the palace do they usually perform magic?”
“There's a large room in the basement on the west side of the palace.”
“Eek, someone's coming.”
They quickly hid themselves among the bushes. A sentry passed in front of them.
“The security is stricter than I thought. It seems best to wait until it gets dark...”
“Mother must be somewhere in that tower over there...”
Sera gazed at the tall tower, which the deceased Sibiya had mentioned, visible through the bushes, and murmured to herself.
“Sera. Don't worry too much. Once this is resolved, I'll figure something out.”
“Can you really do that?”
“I promise.”
Dagmon smiled at Sera, who was asking questions like a child.
“But it won't be easy...”
Sera turned away from Dagmon's gaze and said in a small voice.

It was a dark night. A guard from the nation of Laodicea was patrolling the city walls, whistling cheerfully. Normally, two people would patrol, but for some reason, one of them hadn't shown up today. The thought that he was probably sleeping soundly somewhere made his blood boil.
"Ugh. What am I doing all alone?"
Just then, a dark shadow suddenly appeared in the darkness over there.
"Who's there!"
The soldier, tense, aimed his spear and shouted. But there was no reply. Moreover, normally, soldiers from nearby outposts would have reacted immediately upon hearing his voice. He felt a sense of unease. He immediately ran towards the drum on top of the south gate, which was used to signal an invasion. The faint light of the lamp hanging by the drum on the south gate grew closer and closer. Shadows of several soldiers were visible around the drum.
"Hey~!"
He signaled to them. They spotted him. Thanks to that, he felt a little relieved. Just then, one of them drew his bowstring. Seeing that he was dressed as a soldier of Laodicea, the soldier thought he must have seen something else. An arrow flew with a sound of cutting through the wind. Even then, he didn't realize it was an arrow aimed at him.
The arrow cleanly pierced his neck. He couldn't even scream. His vision went black, and he fell forward.
Sueb descended from the south wall and went to Aaron, who was with the mercenary group waiting at the base of the wall. In the middle of the command post, set up with a makeshift tent, Aaron greeted Sueb warmly.
"Did it go well?"
"The gate is completely secured."
"So, the war is really starting."
"We were waiting for the prince too, but I never imagined our first opponent would be the Laodicean army."
"The soldiers of Laodicea are also citizens of Dagmon, so making such a decision must mean they're ready to take responsibility for it. All we can do is trust Dagmon."
"Then, give the next orders."
"The disguised soldiers are well-positioned, right? Now all that's left is to escort the refugees. How many refugees are in the first group?"
"About 400 will be leaving tonight."
"We'll have to be careful... really..."
"Is there enough food?"
"Well... only enough for about 1,000 people for one day..."
"That was expected anyway. At most, it's three days. Provide ample food for those who can fight, and distribute minimal rations to everyone else. Please take care of it."
"Don't worry. It was quite a while ago, but our mercenary group isn't an easy unit to deal with."
Sueb replied with a confident voice, as if saying, "Leave it to me."
"I should go out and check on the unit's battle readiness."
Aaron stepped out of the tent. But he felt uneasy because Lisia, who usually followed him everywhere, wasn't around.
"Lisia. Where did she go now?"
He spotted a group of soldiers getting their gear ready.
"Have you seen a wizard with long, straight hair, who looks about sixteen or seventeen?"
Aaron asked them about Lisia's whereabouts.
"Ah, you mean Lady Lisia? Please check the supply wagon over there."
A soldier replied to Aaron.
"Since when did Lisia become Lady Lisia?"
Aaron tilted his head at the soldier's answer and went in the direction the soldier had indicated. Several soldiers were peering into a supply wagon.
"What are you doing!"
The soldiers jumped in surprise and backed away from the wagon. Aaron looked into the wagon they had been staring at. Inside, Lisia was sound asleep, with nothing else remarkable.
'What on earth were they looking at?'
"Hey! Lisia! Wake up!"
"Mmm... what? It's not morning yet."
Lisia rubbed her sleepy eyes, got up, checked that it was still dark outside, and grumbled.
"What time is it for sleeping? Everyone is busy preparing for battle. You go to the south valley where the refugees will be and help them out..."
"Can't I go tomorrow?"
"Lisia... you really are something."
"Alright. I'll go, won't I?"
Lisia glared at Aaron with an annoyed look, then got up and stepped out of the wagon.
"You're not the only one having a hard time, you fool."
"I get it. Stop nagging."
"I'll assign a few soldiers to you, so go ahead. Hey, you there, you there!"
Aaron picked out a few soldiers nearby.
"Go with Lisia to the south valley where the people will be, and help set up defensive positions and a camp."
"Understood."
The selected soldiers replied happily.
Aaron watched Lisia and the soldiers head towards the south gate with worried eyes. Aaron was honestly suspicious of those soldiers, especially after what happened earlier.
"I feel uneasy somehow."
Aaron muttered to himself.
"If you're worried about Lisia, there's no need to worry if our unit members are with her."
Sueb, who had arrived unnoticed, spoke to Aaron.
"When did you get here? Is it because you're a famous mercenary captain? I didn't even sense your presence. The soldiers were staring at Lisia while she was sleeping."
"Hmm... really? Well, that could happen. But those guys will protect Lisia with their lives."
"What do you mean by that?"
"Earlier, the soldiers decided on a new symbol for the unit. Lisia has become the new symbol of the unit among the soldiers. Originally, mercenary units had a custom of choosing a symbol to represent the unit, and Lisia was chosen as the symbol almost unanimously."
"A new symbol? What's that all about? They're not going to sacrifice her or anything, are they?"
"Haha. Put those worries aside. The name 'Sueb Mercenary Group' is my name, but it also means 'Wolf Mercenary Group'. We used to raise a young wolf in the unit... but we lost it along with half of our unit members in a battle three years ago. So, we needed a new symbol before this battle. That's why we chose Lisia. She's young, beautiful, and she even provides healing. So now, it's not the Sueb Mercenary Group, but the Lisia Mercenary Group."
"Hmph... The Lisia Mercenary Group. The name is funny, and it's a really strange custom."
Aaron looked at him, laughed, and replied. However, he just gazed in the direction where Lisia and the soldiers had disappeared and spoke in a low voice.
"It might seem that way. In battle, you need something to believe in unconditionally. Having something to protect gives you the will to fight. That's Lisia. Many soldiers believe we lost the battle three years ago because we lost our guardian wolf. This time, they're determined to protect the symbol with their lives. They will protect Lisia to the very last man."
"Don't say such terrible things. We won't be defeated that easily."
Aaron replied in a bright voice.
"That's right. It's our debut battle after three years, so we should make it spectacular."
Sueb laughed and clapped Aaron on the shoulder.
"Anyway, our unit will be borrowing the captain's girlfriend for a bit."
As Aaron's ears instantly turned red, Sueb laughed even louder.
"I thought you were a hero, but you're just a shy boy."

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode 7
contentEn:
Dagmom decided to meet with the Elder Minister first to seek advice. As Dagmom waited in the palace reception room, an elderly man soon appeared in a hurry.
“Your Highness. It has been a long time indeed. What are these soldiers you’ve brought with you?”
He respectfully paid his respects to Dagmom as a prince and asked.
“They are the soldiers my brothers left me. My eldest brother returned safely, didn’t he?”
“Yes, he returned safely. But there’s news that the second prince has passed away…”
“I know.”
“It’s been almost three years. Have you been well, Elder Harsa?”
“Well, there’s not much to be well about. I do everything I can for this country, but… I am very glad that Your Highness has returned to the palace. His Majesty said he would not hold you accountable for what happened three years ago.”
“Even if Father doesn’t hold me accountable, it doesn’t change the fact that it was one of my mistakes. Instead, I have a favor to ask.”
“What is your request?”
“What my eldest brother brought back is a spell of light. A high-level attack spell, at that.”
“Did such a spell truly exist? The war will soon end in victory, then.”
The minister showed a joyful expression, but Dagmom’s face was not bright.
“That… there will be severe casualties. In both nations.”
“The Ceres Kingdom also obtained that spell.”
“What? Is that true? Oh dear… this is a serious matter. It seems that after the war that annihilated the civilizations of light and darkness, the most people might die again.”
“We must stop that. Can you persuade my father?”
“That would be impossible for me… Perhaps Your Highness should step forward…”
“I’m already treated as a discarded child. My name is probably on the list of suspected rebels.”
The old man shook his head repeatedly and replied courteously.
“Is that so? Nevertheless, His Majesty awaits Your Highness. That’s why he said he wouldn’t question your mistakes.”
“If we make a mistake, the capitals of both nations might completely disappear.”
“What? What are you talking about?”
The old man asked with an even more astonished voice.
“The destructive power of that spell is enough to obliterate an entire large city, and it can be dropped anywhere desired. The Ceres Kingdom will complete the spell within three days. There isn’t much time left. We’ll be almost at the same pace… The time it takes for the spell to fly here is about 10 hours at the shortest, and up to a day at the longest. If there’s a period between firing one shot and the next, the first targets will naturally be the capitals of both nations. If that happens, both capitals will vanish.”
“In that case, we must quickly get His Majesty to evacuate.”
“What about the many common people outside? How can you say such a thing?”
Dagmom asked with a sorrowful voice.
“Initially, they might fire one or two shots with only the mages in the capital, but in the end, if they mobilize all the mages of the nation on the battlefield… our civilization might truly be destroyed.”
“Then what do we do?”
“I came here to stop that.”
Dagmom said with a grim voice.
“By what method?”
“I came here to seek advice myself.”
“Telling His Majesty this would be like preaching to a brick wall. He’d undoubtedly thunder, asking if we would just stand by and watch our Laodicea Kingdom be destroyed by the Ceres Kingdom. His Majesty’s will is that offense is the best defense. The only time we wouldn’t attack is when we are certain the enemy has been neutralized. The best course of action is to make sure the Ceres Kingdom cannot use that magic, and then convince His Majesty of that.”
Dagmom said with a voice full of exasperation.
“He’s truly stubborn. Father… How many people can be teleported round-trip to the Ceres Kingdom’s capital right now?”
“About two people. You know well that we cannot precisely teleport to the Ceres Kingdom’s capital, right? And that round-trip teleportation magic automatically summons you back after a certain amount of time…”
“Anyway, there’s no time. At most, we have about two days left.”
“Who are you planning to send? And by what means will you prevent the Ceres Kingdom from using their magic?”
“I will go myself. The other person is someone who knows the geography there well.”
“You’ll go yourself? What if you get hurt?”
“Am I not already a dead man in this royal palace for the past three years?”
“No, you are not. There are still loyal subjects who await Your Highness. Including myself, of course. And have you met Sueb? He is still waiting in Laodicea.”
“Don’t flatter me. It’s good to hear Sueb is still waiting for me.”
Dagmom patted his shoulder and replied with a smile.
“Then, I hope Your Highness returns without a single scratch.”
“Don’t worry. There won’t be a corpse teleported back. More importantly, as a precaution, tell Father about this and have him leave this city.”
“It will be difficult for me to persuade His Majesty. Moreover, after returning after three years, do you not intend to see His Majesty’s face even once?”
Dagmom hesitated for a moment, then replied.
“Very well. I will see him.”

Dagmom hurried towards his father. Time was of the essence for him.
However, all he received was a message to wait in his father’s secretary’s reception room.
“Damn it… time is critical…”
The castle of the Laodicea Kingdom was sturdily built. Beyond the high, sturdy walls, which made it look more like a fortress than a castle, there was a city wall, and within that wall lived many people. Dagmom quietly looked down at the city below.
On one side, there were markets and houses… children playing in the streets, people haggling over goods; many people were visible. They all seemed unrelated to the war, even amidst it.
In the middle of the market where these people gathered, a person with one leg missing was seen walking with difficulty, leaning on a cane. He hadn’t noticed it at first, but surprisingly, disabled people were visible everywhere in the streets. It wasn't entirely unrelated after all. It was obvious that among them, countless people had lost limbs, property, and loved ones because of the war. Dagmom was clearly aware of that fact.
Just then, Dagmom heard the sound of a door opening behind him. It was his father.
The king silently closed the reception room door.
“It’s been a long time, Dagmom. I said I wouldn’t hold you accountable for the defeat, so why did you run away?”
“I felt I could no longer run, so I came here.”
“Yes. That’s fortunate. Anyway, welcome. We must have dinner together tonight.”
A smile appeared on the stern king’s face.
“I have business to discuss rather than dinner. It’s about the spell of light.”
As Dagmom began to speak, the king cut him off.
“I know. That you found the spell. I secretly think highly of you for it.”
“That’s not it. Please abolish that spell!”
Dagmom demanded adamantly.
“What are you saying, returning after three years?”
The king asked, as if he couldn’t believe Dagmom’s words.
“That spell might once again plunge the world into ruin. The capital of the Ceres Kingdom, Brugia, and this city, Laodicea, will be the first targets.”
“As you know, that cannot be. Not until we lead the war to victory. Especially if the Ceres Kingdom possesses the same spell. We cannot delay. We might just sit back and suffer, mightn’t we?”
“The probability is fifty-fifty.”
“We will win that half. And if the power of that spell is real, we will lose if we don’t act.”
“That’s not it. The half is either only two cities are destroyed and it ends, or the entire land of Dragonia is destroyed.”
“Don’t mock your father! The kingdom’s mages never told me such a thing!”
The king shouted in an angry voice.
“They must have been afraid of you, Father.”
Dagmom’s voice was still calm, but it was easy to tell that it contained the same anger as the king’s.
“Don’t worry. We will win this war. I thought you had finally come to your senses after a long time, but you still haven’t.”
“Whether we win or lose is of no interest to me. We must not forget what is more important than victory.”
“What! Are you even a prince of this country, saying such a thing!”
The king truly shouted in a voice filled with rage.
“All I care about is how many sacrifices this war will cost before it ends.”
“You coward!”
“Must you defeat the Ceres Kingdom in such a way? Even using such a terrifying ancient spell?”
“The stronger the weapon, the better.”
“Blood only calls for more blood.”
Dagmom refuted his father’s every word.
“Dagmom, are you truly going to act this way? Yet, I trusted you the most among my sons… I’ve even heard rumors that you are plotting rebellion.”
“Rebellion is an absurd notion. I have no interest in this country.”
“So what do you want me to do! This war, at the very least, cannot be lost!”
“If you promise not to use that spell, I have devised another weapon.”
Only then did the king show some interest and lower his voice slightly.
“What kind of weapon is it?”
“That weapon is… first, please make a promise.”
“What promise?”
“To abolish that spell…”
“As long as the Ceres Kingdom has that spell, I cannot do that.”
The king said firmly.
“I will make sure the Ceres Kingdom cannot use that spell.”
“They might have already started making the spell, just like us. What do you intend to do?”
“As you already know, that spell is not completed in a short time. At least ten high-level mages will be needed. However, like us, they won’t have many combat mages stationed in the capital, and…”

"If I can break the spell they are making, and kill or capture some of those mages, they will have to delay its completion for at least a month while they summon mages from other regions. Then, I will bring you victory within a month."
"Can you truly do that?"
The King said, sounding unconvinced.
"I promise you. I have learned from our previous defeat."
"But how will you send someone to Ceres within that time?"
"I will cast a teleportation spell. Although it will only last a few days... And, just in case, please evacuate everyone inside the castle to outside the castle walls."
"Then I cannot keep that promise!"
The King immediately refused.
"I cannot allow you to go, and the tens of thousands of people inside the castle certainly cannot be moved."
"If something goes wrong, the city of Laodicea itself could disappear."
Dagmon said in a pleading voice.
"Very well, then. I will halt the creation of the spell for just two days. It will take two more days to restart the spell, so the Kingdom of Laodicea will launch the spell four days from now. If you inform me within that time that you have neutralized Ceres’s magic, I will stop."
"Understood. I will make it happen within four days. Then, I’ll take my leave."
Dagmon tried to leave the audience chamber quickly, as if avoiding his father.
"Is this how it is after three years?"
From behind Dagmon, his father’s resentful voice was heard.
"Hasn’t it always been this way?"
Dagmon replied with a bitter smile as he stepped out of the audience chamber.

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode
contentEn:
Sara sat in the shade of a tree at the village entrance, burying her face and weeping continuously.
‘Now I'm all alone... Sibiya and Elron are dead... I killed Sibiya and Elron. They all died because of me... because of me...’
She cried like that for a long time. In the distance, the chirping of birds could be heard, and the weather was bright and sunny, seemingly oblivious to Sara's feelings, just smiling.
Licia tried to comfort her, but Sara asked to be left alone and continued to cry until she had no strength left. Eventually, she fell asleep right there.
Sara had a dream. In her dream, Sibiya and Elron were smiling. Sara was only upset, wondering why they were smiling when she was so heartbroken, and so she cried again in her dream. She didn't know how long she had cried like that.
Then, she was awakened by someone shaking her. She quickly sat up and saw that the sun was already setting over the western mountains, and it was Dagmon who had woken her. Behind him, the well-ordered soldiers of the Kingdom of Laodicea stood in lines, and Dagmon, dismounting from his handsome horse, was shaking Sara's shoulder to wake her.
“I was worried, but I'm glad you're safe. Why on earth are you sleeping in a place like this? And why are you crying so much? Did you have a bad dream?”
Dagmon spoke to Sara as he usually did, but his appearance was definitely different from normal. He was wearing the armor of an officer of the Kingdom of Laodicea, and a sword with an emblem symbolizing a prince gleamed at his waist.
Seeing him like that, the fact that Dagmon was a prince felt fresh and new. He certainly looked like a prince. As Sara saw him, she remembered what Sibiya had once said to her.

It was when she had returned, covered in dirt, after getting into a fight with the boys in the palace. Sibiya wiped the dirt from young Sara's face and her wounds, saying to her:
“Princess! Can't you act like a princess? A prince should act like a prince, and a princess should act like a princess!”
“They started it first!”
Sara exclaimed with a grumble. Beside her, Elron chuckled and said to Sara:
“Princess. Was that really true?”
Elron asked, as if confirming the truth.
“Yes, it was.”
Sara replied primly.
“Alright. How many did you fight?”
Sibiya asked as she wiped her wounds.
“Ouch! Be gentle. Five boys.”
Sibiya asked again, surprised.
“You knocked all five of them down?”
“Of course. Though Elron helped a little.”
Sibiya looked at Elron. Elron avoided Sibiya's gaze and just pretended to be busy with something else. Sibiya found his behavior amusing. She knew Elron had helped Sara.
“All done. Really. You're such a stubborn princess, aren't you?”
After wiping Sara's face clean, Sibiya playfully tapped Sara's head and said.
“You~ can you hit the princess's head?”
Sara said with a grumble.
“I have committed a grave sin. Please have mercy~”
Sibiya replied playfully.
“Alright. Since you treated my wounds, I'll let it slide this once.”
Sara smiled brightly.

As old memories resurfaced, Sara felt like she was about to burst into tears again.
‘Is that what it means to be princely? Then... me...’
Sara started to sniffle again. Dagmon was flustered by her appearance. It was the first time Dagmon had seen Sara show such vulnerability. Dagmon, surprised, hesitated about what to say, then stopped, took off his outer garment, draped it over Sara's shoulders, and helped her up, saying:
“The others are at the village inn, right? It'll get cold soon when evening comes. Let's go in. What on earth happened?”
Sara, still silent, followed Dagmon. She was so exhausted that her steps faltered. She didn't know how many times she leaned on Dagmon.
“I... I'm sorry.”
Sara apologized to Dagmon.
“No, it's alright.”
“Elron... he's dead.”
Sara said briefly in a weak voice, and Dagmon's face instantly hardened upon hearing her words.
“So... so... yes. *sob*”
“I see... such a thing...”
Sara tried to walk on her own again but stumbled and almost fell, only to be caught by Dagmon. Dagmon found her utterly pathetic.
“So that's what happened....”
The group was seated around the table, and Dagmon, after hearing the full story, had a devastated look on his face.
“I've lost one of the greatest generals I've ever known.”
Dagmon looked at Sara. Sara was still immersed in sorrow, saying nothing.
“Was the situation that bad? To the point of requiring Elron's sacrifice...”
Aaron, sitting opposite Dagmon, nodded silently.
“It truly has become the worst-case scenario.”
“No! Aaron must have killed him! Elron! He could have been brought back!”
Suddenly, Sara screamed.
“Don't talk nonsense! Do you think Aaron wanted that to happen?!”
Dagmon, uncharacteristically, snapped at Sara.
“Leave Sara alone.”
Aaron stopped Dagmon.
“Elron died for us, but especially for Sara. He loved Sara...”
“Huh?”
Dagmon asked, sounding puzzled. Then, Dagmon's expression quickly changed to one of understanding, and he looked at Sara once more. Sara avoided Dagmon's gaze, stood up, and was already stomping and running up to her room.
“Anyway, it's a relief that the Spell of Light wasn't handed over to Herodion.”
Aaron said, sounding somewhat relieved.
“Unfortunately, Herodion has obtained the Spell of Light.”
Then Dagmon said with a miserable expression.
“What? What do you mean?”
“My second brother's body was found. And my second brother had my notebook, but it wasn't on the body.”
“What? If the spell has fallen into their hands, that's a big problem...”
“And my eldest brother seems to have returned safely to the castle... and he also reportedly possesses the spell.”
“Things have gotten ridiculous... I had intended to just eliminate him and bury the spell, fearing its power would be too absurd...”
“The power of the spell is quite formidable. According to my research, originally only people of light could use it, but if multiple mages gather and take some time, they can also use it. Its range is almost unlimited, and its power is said to completely annihilate a city. And it is known that the civilizations of light and darkness were mutually destroyed because of it.”
“Enough. It doesn't matter. Not to me... My goal is simply to defeat Esbaal. Then this wretched fate of mine will also end.”
“But many people will die. Perhaps our civilization will also be annihilated, just like the civilizations of light and darkness...”
“Don't talk such dreadful nonsense. At least only one side can use it. Anyway, that spell isn't known by all mages now, like it was during the war of light and darkness. Only the side that launches a preemptive strike will survive. And, in fact, the war might end quickly. I just hope Anania doesn't get her hands on that spell first. Fortunately, Brugia, the capital of the Kingdom of Ceres, is far from here. The Kingdom of Laodicea will likely be reached before Herodion, who has the spell.”
Then Dagmon replied in an agitated voice.
“Don't talk so lightly! Even so, my father and brothers are in the castle, and Sara's father and mother are there too! Moreover, if the Kingdom of Ceres uses migratory birds heading

"You must be overwhelmed because of Ron..."
"It's okay. He's stronger than he looks."
Aaron smiled faintly at Dagmon.
"And, seeing how well you handled things, I see potential in you as a king."
"Huh?"
Dagmon asked, puzzled by Aaron's words.
"At least, you seem more suited to be king than the first or second."
"Don't say such things. I have many shortcomings."
Dagmon said, as if telling him not to joke.
"Tomorrow will be busy again, so please get some rest."
Dagmon said this to Aaron in a chiding tone, then stood up and started to leave the inn. Then Licia, puzzled by Dagmon, asked.
"What about Dagmon?"
"I need to go sleep where the soldiers are."
Aaron stood up, smiled at Dagmon, and gave him a thumbs-up. Dagmon saw this and also gave a thumbs-up. And then Aaron slowly went back up to his bedroom.

{{IMG:1}}
As Aaron's group entered the precarious cliff path, the Ceresian cavalry could no longer approach. Thanks to this, they were able to avoid the gap narrowing, as the cavalry had to dismount and pursue them on foot. However, the distance was still not widening.
Instead, it was slowly getting closer. Elon, checking behind him, was almost walking backward as he ran, worried that they might be within arrow range and shoot.
The snowflakes were getting thicker. For some reason, Elon kept recalling old memories, whether because of the white snow or the desperate situation. Memories of his childhood with Sera. Anania, who had destroyed his happiness. The thought that Anania was responsible for the state he, Sera, and the Ceres Kingdom were in made him uncontrollably angry.
Just then, with a whoosh, he saw an arrow cutting through the wind and flying straight towards his head through the white snow. It was a narrow cliff path, and the snow made it hard to see, but a quite skilled archer had shot an arrow at them. Elon, who had been dazed, quickly snapped out of it and barely dodged.
The arrow that grazed Elon's ear tore Sera's clothes and grazed her arm. Elon knew how deadly that poison was. Elon, startled, grabbed Princess Sera.
"Princess!"
"I'm fine. This much is..."
Sera replied as if it were nothing, as the wound didn't look serious, but Elon quickly tore off the sleeve of Sera's arm and urgently sucked out the poison with his mouth.
"Anania's poison is lethal."
"Thank you. Every time."
Sera replied shyly.
"Go on! Aaron!"
However, instead of replying, Elon shouted to Aaron, worried that the distance would narrow further.
"I can't!"
Aaron also stopped walking after seeing the scene. The wind was getting stronger. The fine snow had now turned into large flakes.
"If we stay here, everyone will be in danger!"
Elon urged Lisia and Aaron.
"That goes for you and my sister too!"
Lisia also shouted, sounding worried.
"It's fine, let's go!"
Elon, having just finished sucking out the poison, urged the group again.
"Be careful! The path is very slippery because of the snow!"
Aaron warned the group. In fact, Aaron, who was at the very front, had almost stumbled several times. From behind, a long scream from one of Anania's soldiers echoed down the cliff and faded away. Aaron felt a chill down his spine at the thought that they might share the same fate.
Lisia clung tightly behind Aaron, like a frightened rabbit, stepping exactly where Aaron stepped, and Sera was barely moving forward, protected by Elon.
'Whoosh! Whoosh!'
The frequency of arrows flying had increased. It seemed the distance was narrowing.
"Tch. They can't see well because of the snow, but they're shooting well."
Elon grumbled, deflecting an arrow with his sword. Aaron thought that on such a narrow path, the person at the very back was most likely to be hit by an arrow, so he decided he should go to the back.
Elon was guarding the rear. Of course, Aaron didn't distrust him. However, he felt an ominous shadow on Elon's face, perhaps due to the after-effects of sucking out the poison earlier. Aaron, having experienced long journeys and battles, had developed such instincts and knew that feelings should not be ignored.
"Elon! Let's switch positions!"
"What are you talking about! Do you not trust me!"
Elon shouted back, unwilling to back down.
"It's not that..."
"What do you mean by that!"
"I just have a bad feeling."
"What's with the 'feeling' talk? Just lead the way properly! Our fate depends on you."
Sera understood what they were talking about. The very back was clearly dangerous.
"Then, I'll go to the back."
"Princess Sera!"
Elon tried to stop Sera, but Sera disliked asking anyone for permission.
"I said I can do it."
She stepped forward, trying to go behind Elon. The moment she moved past Elon's large frame, an arrow was seen flying through the blizzard towards Sera. Elon pulled Sera back, having no time to dodge the arrow. He quickly embraced Sera and turned his body.
'Thud!'
The arrow struck Elon squarely in the back. Sera, held in Elon's arms, could only watch the scene with wide, startled eyes.
"Damn it! You fool! Lisia!"
Aaron quickly called Lisia, but Lisia's reply was despairing.
"I used up all my magic power summoning the spirit! I didn't think something like this would happen..."
Lisia whimpered, as if blaming herself for the sudden situation.
"It's okay. It's not your fault. And Elon isn't someone who'd fall from one arrow."
Aaron stroked Lisia's head once, then quickly moved to the very back. Aaron supported Elon.
"Aaron, it's fine. It's nothing. You just take care of the front."
"What are you talking about? I said that to Lisia, but you know best that it's a critical injury."
"This. I've made quite a spectacle of myself."
Elon smiled and leaned on Aaron.
'I hate it most when my ominous feelings are right.'
Aaron's ominous feeling hadn't gone away, but he didn't say anything, not wanting to make the group anxious, but he felt somehow stifled inside. He had felt this way in the past too.
"Lisia! You lead the way!"
Aaron quickly ordered Lisia to take the lead.
"How can I?"
Lisia replied with a voice full of fear.
"Then, who will?"
When Aaron shouted, Lisia finally replied in a barely audible voice.
"Alright..."
Lisia, thinking it was her responsibility for having used up all her magic power, mustered her courage. Leading the way on a narrow cliff path in a blizzard where one couldn't see an inch ahead was truly something she didn't want to do. But she had no choice.
Sera stood by, at a loss, worrying about Elon. It was Sera's unnecessary action that had caused Elon to be hit by the arrow. Surely, if Elon had been alone, he would have dodged the arrow or taken appropriate measures. Seeing Sera's flustered expression as she thought this, Aaron couldn't say anything either. Aaron knew well that if he said even a single word, as he usually would, Elon wouldn't stand for it.
Elon, seeing Sera at a loss, spoke to her.
"Princess, I'll be fine."
"Elon. Are you really okay?"
"Don't worry. I won't die and leave the Princess behind. I am your escort knight. My mission isn't over yet. If I were to die from one or two arrows like this, I wouldn't be qualified as a knight."
Elon showed a relaxed demeanor.
"Aaron, is Elon really okay?"
Sera asked Aaron, truly worried about Elon. But her voice had lost its composure. However, Aaron didn't answer. Arrows continued to fly, but Aaron focused all his efforts on supporting Elon and blocking the arrows. This was an extremely difficult task for Aaron as well.
"I'm sorry, Aaron. You don't have to do this..."
Elon said apologetically.
"Helping me means staying quiet. And move as much as you can to make it a little less difficult for me."
Elon spoke to Aaron, who was supporting him, in a voice quiet enough not to be heard by the others.
"Aaron. Do you know about the poison arrows of Anania's Royal Guard?"
Elon asked cautiously.
"....Damn it.. I know.."
Aaron paused before answering, then spoke in a displeased tone.
"Then. Leave me behind."
"Don't talk nonsense! Sera lost Sibiya to that arrow, and if I lose you too, I might go crazy! I have no desire whatsoever to leave you behind."
"The Princess isn't that weak."
"Honestly. I don't like your tone. Treating a girl younger than you with such deference and respect... She's just a princess in name. Do you really need to do that?"
"That's why I do it even more."
Elon's voice was a little weaker.
"What a strange fellow."
The moment Lisia rounded the cliff corner, she had no choice but to stop dead in her tracks. There was a small clearing blocked by a large cliff, and only a small cave entrance ahead.
"Lisia, what is it? Why did you stop?"
Aaron caught up and asked. But he too understood the situation and asked no further questions.
Aaron's anger towards Anania surged.
"Damn it!"
"Aaron. That small cave leads to the foot of the mountain."
Elon said, breathing heavily, looking at the small cave.
"What do you mean?"
Aaron asked Elon.
"Dagmon said that in the village below this mountain, they preserve food with the cold air coming down from the mountain... That cave must be the one that leads to that village. Do you see the melted snow only at that cave entrance? That must be because of the warm air blowing up from below."
Elon continued speaking with difficulty.
"Are you sure about that?"
"Of course, it's a guess. I only heard about it. A Ceresian soldier wouldn't know much about Laodicea, would they? Still, we have no choice. If push comes to shove, we can just kill all those soldiers in that cave."
"Indeed, we have no choice. But I don't have the confidence to stop that many soldiers."
Aaron chuckled lightly, agreeing.
"Yes. I knew you'd say that, Aaron. Leave me here now. I'll try to hold them back for a while."
"What are you talking about? We have to go together."
"Aaron. You know well. I'm done for. In a place like this, I can hold back the soldiers for a while. And if push comes to shove, I'll block the cave entrance. Even if it's a dead end, it will buy us time until Lisia's magic power recovers."
Elon spoke to Aaron as an adult would admonish a child. Aaron was momentarily speechless, thinking of other methods. But he realized that this was the best option.

"Damn it. How did things end up like this?"
"You have a mission. And I, too... My mission is to protect Princess Sera until the very end."
"I don't understand at all. Why was someone as capable as you with Princess Sera? Honestly, Princess Sera's position must have only been a hindrance to you."
"Don't say such things. The princess might hear you."
"I'll leave you here as you wish. But tell me just one thing. Otherwise, I'll take you with me."
"What on earth do you want to know, my friend?"
Elron said, gasping for breath.
"Your feelings... for Princess Sera. Without that, I can't understand the relationship between you and Princess Sera. It's not a short period of just over ten years."
"It's just as you think. Perhaps it was pity at first... Stop talking nonsense and go!"
"Then... I have no choice. You were the bravest, and also the most foolish man I've ever seen."
Aaron said, letting go of Elron's arm.
"Why am I foolish?"
"You figure that out."
Aaron smiled lightly at Elron.
"We're going into that cave."
Elron said to Licia and Sera.
"Really? If it's blocked inside, we'll be trapped."
Licia asked, as if she couldn't believe it.
"There's no other way. At least inside there, we won't have to worry about arrows. Licia, keep leading the way."
"No!"
Licia was as afraid of leading the way into the dark cave as she was of the soldiers chasing them from behind.
"Licia!"
When Aaron called Licia's name, Licia's heart skipped a beat. Licia gave Aaron a pleading look, but for some reason, Aaron's eyes were firm. Licia turned her head again, knowing she had no choice.
"Fool..."
Licia carefully created a lantern spell with the little magic power she had left, then cautiously entered the cave. Licia was truly terrified. Looking back, Sera was following with a frightened expression, and Aaron was following, supporting Elron.
'Licia. You must be brave.'
Licia grabbed her sister Sera's hand, who was following behind, and once again steeled her resolve, moving forward.
However, the darkness, beckoning and gaping open as if inviting them in, terrified Licia. When she was alone in the dark, it always felt like someone was whispering to her, so darkness had been Licia's greatest fear since childhood. But now, perhaps because her friends were beside her, she felt a little relieved that she heard no sounds.
Licia felt that if she looked back, she would only become weak again, so she didn't turn around and just looked straight ahead. Thinking that Aaron was behind her somehow made her feel secure.

Dagmon, entering the battlefield, seized a riderless horse, whose owner was unknown. On the outskirts of the battlefield, he spotted a young general who had fallen from his horse and was on the verge of being killed by several Ceresian soldiers. Without hesitation, Dagmon charged towards him. The Ceresian soldiers, caught off guard in the chaotic and fleeing Laodicean army, lost their lives to Dagmon's sword.

"Thank you."

The general, whose life had been saved, expressed his gratitude.

"I am Prince Dagmon, the third son of Laodicea. What happened to your subordinates?"

The general, startled, saluted Dagmon and replied with an apologetic tone.

"I apologize. The senior unit issued a charge order, but our unit, being non-combatants, was almost completely annihilated."

"I don't blame you. What about the combat units?"

"The combat units seem to be escorting the two princes and retreating behind the front lines."

"So, are non-combatants currently facing the enemy?"

"That's right."

Upon hearing that, Dagmon's anger flared.

"I apologize to you, who barely escaped with your life, but from now on, you will accompany me to the heart of the battlefield and guard me. And, gather all your unit members who survived or are fighting on the front lines. From now on, I will command the unit. And I will take responsibility, so you command my brothers' units."

"Understood. I will follow Prince Dagmon's words."

The general's face brightened at Dagmon's words, and he replied vigorously, then used one of the magic tubes he carried. A blue beam of light shot up into the sky, and the Laodicean soldiers entangled in battle on the field understood the meaning of that light in the sky, and the soldiers of that unit gradually began to retreat.

General Herodion, who was confident of victory, suddenly felt that the formation was moving strangely. After the blue magic light appeared, the soldiers' movements changed. Soon, another beam of light rose. The vanguard unit commanded by the two princes was already in the rear, but another beam of light, signaling an operation to the unit, rose from a closer, different direction, and the drumbeat of the Laodicean army also changed.

"It can't be those two foolish princes... Who is it?"

Herodion surveyed the formation from which the light beam had risen. By then, the Laodicean army there was re-establishing its defensive line. Taking out his telescope, he observed the enemy lines forming a defensive position, and a young man, not particularly large in stature, caught his eye, riding a horse and commanding the soldiers.

"Tch. It's Dagmon. He's a bigger fish than those two fleeing princes. I'll have to catch him myself."

Herodion gathered the swiftest and best-trained soldiers of Ceres and personally rode towards Dagmon. The Laodicean army's defensive line was well-organized, but since it was mostly composed of non-combatants, it seemed possible to break through by concentrating an attack on one side. Dagmon was trying to retreat his unit as quickly as possible while forming the line, but in terms of mobility, he was a step behind the well-trained Ceresian soldiers.

Just as Herodion was thinking that he could break through the defensive line and capture Dagmon with a little more attack, he spotted Aaron's group fleeing in the distance. It was almost certain that he wouldn't be able to stop Dagmon from retreating and escaping unless he commanded directly, but for Herodion, the "Light Spell" was more urgent.

"Damn it! I can't let them get away. 3rd and 4th platoons of the direct company (approx. 30 men per platoon)! Follow me!"

Herodion divided his soldiers and pursued Aaron's group. With Herodion gone, the enemy's movements changed slightly. However, even so, there was no chance of victory, but it seemed sufficient to withdraw the troops and regroup. Saving even one more soldier was his responsibility. Soon, Dagmon's soldiers, with only a few combat soldiers covering the rear, mostly managed to withdraw from the battlefield and retreat, joining their two brothers' combat units. Seeing this, the enemies, perhaps fearing casualties, stopped pursuing the larger Laodicean army and regrouped. Dagmon had the battle-weary soldiers regroup and set up camp. Instead, he called the unit commanders who had been on escort duty for his two brothers and had them stationed in the direction of the enemy lines, then reorganized the battle formation.

"Dagmon! What are you doing! Why did you withdraw the troops!"

The two princes came to the command tent and shouted in angry voices.

"If we had left them, our soldiers who fought Herodion would have been annihilated."

"What are you talking about! We had so many troops!"

"Not so many now."

Dagmon cut them off. At his words, the two princes could not continue.

"Did you find the Light Spell?"

The second brother asked, seemingly embarrassed. Dagmon's mood soured at the mention of the spell even on the battlefield. However, he was not in a position to say anything to them. Dagmon, already angry with his brothers, decided not to care what they said.

"I am not obligated to answer. I'm tired, so I should get some sleep in my tent."

Dagmon ignored the two princes and walked out of the command tent.

"That!"

The eldest, Goseba, clenched his fist and was about to rush at Dagmon. Then, the second prince, Sakgae, blocked the eldest prince.

"Why are you stopping me!"

The eldest shouted in a voice full of rage. The second prince gave the eldest prince a meaningful look. The second's eyes were fixed on the small notebook tucked into Dagmon's waist as he turned and walked out. Soon, the eldest also caught on and approached Dagmon.

"Alright! Dagmon. Then we will officially give you command."

Dagmon, who was about to leave the tent, stopped. It was the most welcome news he had heard so far. While the soldiers followed Dagmon's command, they were afraid of disobeying the official commanders, the first and second princes. If the two stepped forward, it could change the atmosphere among the soldiers.

"Really? Brothers?"

Dagmon wondered what had suddenly changed his brothers' minds, but he turned around and asked with a bright face.

"Really."

The eldest showed a false smile. The two princes approached Dagmon. Just as Dagmon let his guard down, the second brother suddenly snatched the notebook from his waist. Only then did Dagmon realize their true intentions.

"Brother! What are you doing? Give it back!"

"What is this?"

The second brother had no intention of returning the notebook and flipped through it.

"This is it. What you've been investigating about the Light Spell all this time..."

The second brother spoke as if he already knew.

"They are useless things. Please give them back!"

Dagmon shouted in a voice full of indignation.

"Brother! I found it. The Light Spell is written here."

When the second Sakgae spoke in an excited voice, the eldest said,

"We will take that notebook to the imperial palace according to His Majesty's command."

"You can't go!"

Dagmon quickly blocked their path and drew his sword.

"What? Are you going to kill me? You usurped the command given by the king, and now you're obstructing the mission given by our father and going to kill your brothers? This is clear rebellion. Kill me if you dare. The entire Laodicean army will now pursue you."

The eldest spoke with a sneer at his sword.

The eldest, Goseba, pushed aside the sword aimed at him with two fingers and walked out of the tent, but Dagmon could not stop him.

"Let's go back to the imperial palace, Sakgae."

"Ah. Yes, brother."

Sakgae followed Goseba with a sly smile. As the eldest was about to leave the tent, he suddenly remembered something and said to Dagmon,

"Oh. And, let me tell you something. Father said you would not be held responsible after the defeat. However, you did not return to the imperial palace and have already broken many national laws. Thanks to that, you are now on the list of rebels."

Dagmon resented his irresponsible and despicable brothers, but there was nothing he could do.

"Alright. Please don't inform the imperial palace that the soldiers followed my command. If you're going to hold someone responsible, it's all my fault."

"Good. You've worked hard to find the Light Spell, so I'll grant that request."

Dagmon was furious, but all he could do now was protect his soldiers. At his words, the eyes of the generals watching the situation around them stirred with a mix of anger and apology.

The two brothers rode their horses and began to descend the mountain.

"No matter how I look at it, that guy seems stupid. Don't you think so?"

"He must have become a fool from being engrossed in books since childhood. Anyway, stop for a moment."

The eldest, Goseba, who was riding, stopped his horse as if he had thought of something. Sakgae also stopped his horse, following his brother.

"Wouldn't it be better if we, just in case, didn't go together like this, but instead, both of us took the Light Spell with a time difference?"

The eldest spoke cautiously.

"What are you talking about, brother?"

"Ceres is also after this spell. The Light Spell is important. What if we get attacked while going together? It would be a disaster, wouldn't it? Even if one person can't deliver it, if two go, at least the remaining one can deliver the spell."

Then the second brother stared at the eldest.

"You're not planning to kill me and steal the credit, are you? I'm the one who found and took Dagmon's notebook."

"What are you talking about! Kill my beloved brother? If I wanted to kill someone, I would have killed Dagmon long ago. Besides, I'm about to become king."

The eldest denied it with disgust. In truth, the eldest had such intentions, but the second brother was not as foolish as the eldest thought.

"Alright. I'll write it for you."

He took out a piece of paper and copied the spell and text from the notebook.

"Here it is."

The second brother handed the note to the eldest.

"It's the same as the notebook, right?"

The eldest asked, as if he didn't trust him.

"Look! Look!"

The second brother held out the notebook.

"I see."

The eldest, after comparing it with the notebook, felt relieved and handed the notebook to the second.

handed it over.
“Then, who should go first?”
“Brother, you go first.”
The eldest, who had intended to go first and claim the credit for himself with their father, was unexpectedly pleased by the second son's willingness to do as he wished. It wasn't that the second son couldn't read the eldest's mind.
However, the eldest coveted Dagmon's notebook, filled with numerous spells and wondrous things, even more than he desired the credit for that spell for himself. Just as the second son was contemplating a way to get his hands on Dagmon's notebook, the eldest's words were welcome news.
If the eldest brother delivered the spell to their father, he (the second son) would simply take the notebook.

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1, Episode 60 - Agol's Wind
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
"Is that it?"
Lishia pointed at the mountains that soared so high they seemed to pierce the sky. Dagmon nodded silently. The white mountains in the distance stood against the blue sky like a painting. Lishia stared at them with wonder.
"Is there snow piled up on top of that place?"
"They call it perennial snow. Snow that hasn't melted for hundreds, no, thousands of years, is piled up there. From here, it looks beautiful, doesn't it? But it's not an easy mountain, as beautiful as it looks."
Dagmon kindly explained.
"It's pretty, but just looking at it makes me dizzy. Seriously, it's going to be tough. I hate high places."
Aaron complained.
"If we had time, it would be nice to look around. Still, this place has many unique things that Laodicea doesn't. It's the only place in Laodicea where you can see snow. I don't know if it was artificially made by someone long ago, or if it formed naturally, but there are dozens of ice caves extending from the mountaintop to the base, where people living at the base store food. In that village, they even sell something called ice cream made with milk and cheese, and the taste is incredible."
"Dagmon, you know we don't have time for sightseeing like that..."
Serah looked at Dagmon and said.
"I was just explaining that such a place exists. Still, it's one of the most famous tourist attractions in Laodicea."
"In this time of war, who has the leisure to go sightseeing? It must be some group of people with warm backsides, no doubt."
Aaron shot back coldly, glancing at Dagmon.

Before they knew it, the group had climbed onto the ridge of Mount Agol and were walking through a pure white snowfield. The sun was shining down from the sky, and the white snow sparkled with its light, making it so dazzling that onlookers couldn't look directly at it. However, unlike the seemingly warm sunlight, the air felt biting.
"It's really cold..."
Lishia complained, pulling her collar tighter. They had prepared thoroughly before climbing the mountain, but the cold was truly unbearable.
"Still, it's a good thing the snow isn't blowing. The weather changes easily in places like this."
Aaron said, as if it was at least a relief.
"Are we still far?"
Serah asked Elon.
"Well, we'll have to walk for a few more hours, Princess. Please tell me if you're tired."
"Dagmon!"
Just then, Lishia's voice was heard calling Dagmon from behind.
The group looked at Dagmon. He had fallen far behind the group at some point and was staring at something in the middle of the snowfield. Aaron thought he might have discovered something, so he walked through the sinking snow to Dagmon.
"This is..."
Dagmon was examining the snowfield.
"What is it, Dagmon?"
"Someone else is here besides us."
"Footprints? Why are there so many footprints in such a rugged mountain?"
"They are soldiers of Laodicea."
"How do you know that?"
"These boots are exactly like mine."
Dagmon showed his own footprints.
"They lead over that ridge. I'll go take a look."
Dagmon left Aaron behind and strode off, following the footprints.
"Hey! Dagmon, don't go alone!"
"Don't worry. You all go ahead."
"That guy, he's sometimes so unpredictable."
Aaron, resigned as if he couldn't stop him, returned to the rest of the group.
"Where's Dagmon going?"
Lishia asked.
"To the restroom."
"Don't joke."
Serah hit Aaron's head with her sword sheath, saying dismissively.
"There are footprints of Laodicea soldiers, so he's following them."
"Laodicea? We need to be on high alert."
Elon tensed up.
"Do you still think you're a general of Ceres?"
Aaron asked, seeing his reaction. Elon then made a realization and replied.
"That's right. Yes, I'm not in a position to be, but at least it doesn't feel good."
"Anyway, he told us to go ahead. Dagmon will handle it well. He may look like this, but he's a prince. Don't worry."
Aaron urged the group to quicken their pace.
"Will Dagmon be okay by himself?"
Serah asked with a worried voice.
"That guy's got a lot of experience wandering around. He certainly doesn't fit in with the king. More surprisingly, Serah, you're worried about Dagmon?"
"What's wrong with me worrying about Dagmon!"
"You once tried to kill him... Well, you tried to kill all the men here except Elon. Is it a phobia of men?"
"That's enough!"
"Stop these childish fights!"
Elon stopped Serah.
"He started it!"
"Sister, just bear with it. Aaron always likes to get on people's nerves."
Lishia chimed in.
"When did I ever!"
This time, Aaron said, as if wronged.
"That's true. I never thought Prince Dagmon's absence would be felt so strongly. Who's going to stop you?"
Elon agreed.
"Let's just go quickly. Beyond that ridge is Agol Valley. It won't be cold there."
Aaron, having nothing more to say, quickly changed the subject and started walking.
"Still, I'd rather be cold than in Agol Valley."
Elon sighed and followed Aaron.
"What do you mean by that?"
Lishia asked Elon.
"As far as I know, that place is truly barren. It used to be an active volcano, and they say it's hard to approach because of the sulfur smell. It's literally like hell."
Lishia had never seen a volcano or smelled sulfur, so she tilted her head as if she didn't understand what he meant, and just followed along, but she vaguely understood that it was an unpleasant place.
"That's absurd!"
Dagmon slammed his hand on the desk in the tent and shouted.
"It's absolutely necessary for our war!"
One of the two young men dressed as generals standing before Dagmon replied.
He was Goseba, the eldest son of Laodicea and Dagmon's older brother.
"Such a war will only result in the depletion of both nations' power! Ceres is already crumbling. Our further involvement will only lead to more deaths among our people. Moreover, to use the power of light in war! Without even knowing what that power is!"
"Dagmon, just be quiet! You just need to bring us that spell!"
Another young man said. He was Zacchaeus, Dagmon's second older brother. Seeing Zacchaeus, Dagmon recalled events from several years ago and felt even more displeased. Though it had been a long time since he'd seen his two brothers, they had become unpleasantly fat, and their eyes seemed even more filled with greed than before. Dagmon felt disgust rather than joy towards his two brothers.
"I refuse!"
"Then, the Ananias Royal Guard of Ceres on the other side might seize that spell."
"Huh? What do you mean?"
"There's a battalion-sized Ananias Royal Guard on the other side. They're here with the same objective as us!"
"Damn it! Then we shouldn't be just sitting around!"
"What do you mean, 'sitting around'?"
"Are you saying we should leave the elite soldiers of Ceres who have entered Laodicea's territory alone?"
"We are also observing their actions. Until we find the spell of light."
"If you find it, both nations will be ruined! Do you know how the civilizations of light and darkness were destroyed? Moreover, with a formation like this, it's obvious we'll lose!"
"What? Are you questioning our qualifications as generals?"
The eldest brother flared up.
"I'm not questioning, I'm saying you're wrong. They are elite soldiers. We, on the other hand, are just a disorganized rabble, easily detected by our footprints, and our current formation and position are poor. If we engage like this, we will only suffer heavy losses."
"What! What do I know, who only wandered outside! What do you know about war! We've led soldiers on battlefields! And we are a division-sized force! We have four times their numbers!"
The second brother also lost his temper, unable to bear it.
"It must have been a battlefield in name only. The soldiers are pitiful. War isn't just about numbers."
Dagmon smiled with a sneer. At that, the displeased eldest brother, Goseba, shouted.
"So, did you go to the front lines and drive those pitiful soldiers to their deaths? I don't know why a defeated general has so much to say."
"That is..."
Dagmon couldn't find an excuse to answer that remark. It was true that many soldiers had lost their lives because of him. And after that, he had no intention of leading an army again. However, that didn't mean he deserved to hear such words from his brother. Dagmon was angry, but he knew well that further discussion would only make him look foolish. Dagmon suppressed his anger and left the command post without a word of farewell. As Dagmon exited the command post, he tapped a soldier inside the tent on the shoulder and said.
"If the battle starts and it looks unfavorable, escape along the southern ridge."
His voice was heard by his two brothers inside the command post. Inside, the eldest, Goseba, was unable to contain his rage at the insult Dagmon had given him.
"That guy..."
"Calm down, brother. He's still young."
The second brother, Zacchaeus, tried to soothe the eldest.
"When he returns to the palace, I'll have to give him a good education. He seems to be getting too big for his britches just because His Majesty favors him a bit."
The second brother also muttered to himself.
Dagmon quickly exited the command post, crossed the Laodicean camp, and intended to return to Aaron's group. He needed to quickly inform them that the armies of both nations were pursuing the spell.
"Prince Dagmon!"
Just then, a man approached Dagmon and grabbed his sleeve. Dagmon looked at him with surprised eyes. He was a soldier who looked much older.
"Oh? Did you volunteer too, grandfather?"
"Volunteer? About half of us were hastily conscripted from nearby villages and cities. Military service..."

"We've paid our taxes diligently. What is this sudden turn of events? What on earth is going to happen to us? Moreover, we've heard rumors that the army we're supposed to fight is Anania's personal guard. Is that true?"
"........."
Dagmon was speechless. His fists clenched tightly. However, in this state, there was nothing he could do for them.
"Just... have faith. Surely, there will be a good outcome."
