Dagmon replied curtly, shook off the old soldier's hand, and hastened his steps back towards Aaron and his companions. Dagmon clenched his fists tightly and gritted his teeth. He began to despise himself again for being unable to do anything. The wind blowing through Agol, under a sky so clear it felt chilling, seemed unusually cold.

Aaron, who had rushed into the forest, began to call out for Lisia. However, the only response he received was the sound of birds startled by the unwelcome noise and flying away.
“Lisia!”
Aaron continued to run, shouting Lisia's name.
He hadn't eaten anything since morning, and had been running around calling Lisia's name. Even with Aaron's excellent stamina, searching for someone all day without eating was taking a toll on his body, and his voice began to sound hoarse.
Aaron went deeper and deeper into the forest, which grew so dense that no light could penetrate it. It felt as if he were in a cave rather than a forest. When Aaron shouted Lisia's name, the deep forest echoed her name back to him. Aaron had lost his sense of direction.
“Lisia~~~~! Lisia~~~~~~~! I was wrong! Come back!”
Aaron, no longer knowing which way to go, suddenly stopped and screamed with all his might. His voice was filled with despair.
It was an apology to Lisia, his true feelings. And, it was his clumsy confession of love. But still, there was nothing to be heard from the darkness. Aaron began to sob uncontrollably.
“Lisia~ please… come back…”
Unable to bear it any longer, Aaron knelt and pounded the ground.
“God of Dragonia! God of Light! Please return Lisia to me! How can you be so cruel! To burden a human with a destiny called a legend at will! How can you do as you please! Please return Lisia! Even if it's not the God of Light. Whether it's the God of Darkness, or the God of Dragons! Please…!”
Aaron cried out to the sky, which was obscured by trees and received no light, while still on his knees. But again, all that returned was the forest's echo, silence, and darkness.
“Ughhh~!”
Aaron whimpered softly. He couldn't hold back the tears and sorrow that welled up. It was resentment towards fate… and sorrow for being unable to do anything.
Just then, Aaron heard a loud noise. He instantly stifled his cries. It was difficult to suddenly stop crying, but he had to hear that sound somehow. He even held his breath, listening intently to the sound.
Aaron soon reacted to the sound, stopping all movement at once and springing to his feet.
It was a familiar sound. It was definitely not Lisia's voice, and it was a small sound, but it was a sound that could lead him to Lisia. Shagya's cry! The sound echoed faintly in the dark forest.
Aaron closed his eyes to concentrate after hearing Shagya's sound. As a hunter, he knew well that in a place with such strong echoes, blindly heading towards a sound would only lead him astray. Soon, Shagya's almost-scream-like cry echoed again, bouncing off the dense thickets. Aaron suddenly opened his eyes wide and began to run furiously in the direction from which the sound had come.
Even when thorn bushes blocked his path, Aaron cut through them without hesitation to avoid losing his direction. His arms were torn and scratched in many places. However, Aaron's expression was surprisingly bright with the glimmer of hope that he might find Lisia, and just as he wished, Shagya's sound grew closer.
When Aaron arrived, Shagya was threatening the monsters beside the fallen Lisia. However, the monsters didn't seem particularly scared. This was because Shagya's flames had no effect on their thick, rough skin, and they were even herding the small dragon with hunting tools, as if trying to capture it alive. Shagya was almost caught.
But what angered Aaron more was one of the creatures half-uncovering Lisia's chest and caressing her.
“Lisia!”
When Aaron called Lisia's name, the monsters spotted him and grinned hideously. Aaron tried to draw the sword at his waist. However, he instantly tensed up. He had forgotten to bring his sword in his haste to leave. All he had was a dagger he wore at his ankle, used for skinning animals.
Aaron first charged with terrifying momentum, colliding with the creature that was assaulting Lisia. He managed to push it back and knock it down, but it felt like hitting a rock.
‘Disgusting creatures!’
At the same time, Aaron immediately pulled out the dagger from his ankle, gripped it tightly, and forcefully plunged it into the creature's belly. However, the sensation in Aaron's wrist was unexpected. The dagger penetrated to a certain extent but then stopped.
‘Damn it… they're armored with leather under their ragged clothes!’
Aaron rolled sideways with a chilling sense of danger. The creature that had been holding Shagya behind Aaron gave up on Shagya and brought its hand-axe down towards Aaron. Aaron narrowly dodged it, and only the creature pinned beneath him had its arm severed by its own comrade. The monster's desperate scream echoed through the dark forest.
Aaron quickly stood up and gripped his dagger. Then, he looked at the fallen Lisia. He couldn't even check if she was alive, thinking that if he showed even a slight opening, these creatures would kill him. However, he could confirm that Lisia was alive by the groaning sounds she made.
‘This girl… she must be really hurt. But how do I get out of here?’
The monster with the severed arm screamed in pain, rolling on the ground. Its desperate cries echoed through the forest.
One monster swung its axe, decapitating its comrade who was writhing in pain from the severed arm. Instantly, the monster decayed and turned to dust. The forest, which had been filled with the monster's screams, fell silent again in the dark. Aaron was threatening them with his dagger to keep them at bay, but he knew that once they realized his dagger was useless against their armor, they would charge without hesitation. He had to take some action before that happened.
Just then, the monsters spoke to each other in an unknown language of their own.
“What! What are you babbling about!”
Aaron shouted, but the monsters merely gave him sinister smiles. They spread out slightly, encircling Aaron.
‘Are they going to attack all at once?’
One of them shouted in their language. Aaron only felt as if they were chanting some spell; he couldn't understand it at all. Then, the already dark forest became completely black. So dark that he couldn't even see his own hand. Aaron felt the presence of terror in the darkness.
‘Where in the world are these things?’
Aaron lunged his dagger into the darkness, but felt nothing. He couldn't even tell where he had aimed the dagger. It was a complete darkness where he couldn't see his own body.
Aaron felt a chilling sensation and rolled his body, but he hit something that felt like a thick tree trunk, and pain shot through one of his arms. One of his arms had been grazed by their axe.
‘Damn it. These guys can see in the dark. They're playing with me.’
Just then, a light briefly flashed from one side. It was Shagya's flame attacking a monster again. For a brief moment, the monsters and the forest appeared in Aaron's sight. However, Shagya was soon caught by the monsters, as no more flames were emitted, and all Aaron could hear was Shagya's frustrated gurgling and the monsters' sinister, laughing-like breathing.
Several more attacks came from the monsters. They weren't fatal wounds, but they were enough to make Aaron lose his confidence and will to fight. Aaron began to fear the threat of death. It felt unfair to die like this.
‘Damn it. What kind of Warrior of Light am I! To die so meaninglessly in a place like this… not even by Esbaal's hand… in a place like this…’
Then, the phrase "Warrior of Light" suddenly made something click in Aaron's mind.
‘Right. Light!’
The monsters must have knocked away the dagger, which they considered a threat, as Aaron lost his grip on it. However, Aaron, having realized the solution, ignored the dropped dagger and quickly chanted a magic spell.
“Aswat!”
A powerful light burst forth. Originally, it was a technique to quickly escape while temporarily blinding the opponent, but its effect was different on these creatures. For monsters that lived only in dark places, it was even more fatal. Instantly, the darkness spell was broken, and the creatures were seen covering their eyes in pain. Shagya was also freed.
Aaron, without delay, picked up Lisia and began to run, with Shagya swiftly leading the way in front of him. Scratched and torn everywhere… but he had no time to care about such things. Behind them, the monsters were chasing with ravenous sounds. Aaron, a hunter, was confident in running through the forest, but the creatures, like fierce beasts of the forest, closed the distance at a terrifying speed. It was still dangerous until they reached a brighter area.
Soon, a small light appeared in the distance. The forest was ending. Aaron threw himself towards it. As he exited the forest, Aaron tumbled head over heels. An axe thrown by one of the creatures had struck his leg as it passed. Aaron, still holding Lisia, fell directly into the light. To prevent Lisia from getting hurt, Aaron cradled her head with his hand and chest. After rolling several times, Aaron and Lisia landed tangled together on a roadside that was slightly lower than the forest. The sun was already setting. Fortunately, the monsters seemed unable to leave the forest before dark and stopped their pursuit.
Aaron got up and first checked on Lisia, whom he was holding. She was still breathing heavily and unconscious. He touched her forehead; it was quite hot.
And then, Aaron realized that Lisia had been…

Her chest was half-exposed. Aaron blushed and properly dressed Lishia, and only then did Aaron feel a severe pain in his leg.
The axe's deep and old marks were clearly visible, and the bleeding was severe. Aaron immediately tore his clothes to bind his leg and stop the bleeding, and then, with a limping leg, he carried Lishia on his back.
And, thinking he had to get out of there quickly before dark, he limped with his exhausted body back towards the city where his companions were. A severe pain in his leg twisted Aaron's face. He felt blood seeping out again from the hastily bound wound on his leg. However, the joy of having saved Lishia outweighed the pain.
He felt Lishia stir. Lishia's warm breath was felt on Aaron's back.
"Aaron... you fool..."
At that moment, Lishia uttered a single phrase in a small voice, perhaps in her sleep.
"Yes. I am a fool."
Aaron replied with a smile.
"The reason I didn't call you 'Oppa'... was because I wanted you to treat me like a woman..."
Aaron checked if Lishia had woken up, but she was still asleep.
Aaron chuckled lightly.
"I'm sorry... It's hard for me to think of you as a younger sister... So I'm the one having a hard time."
Lishia continued to mumble something.
It was hard to tell if it was sleep-talking or what it meant, but Aaron interpreted it as he pleased and answered as he pleased. Aaron sometimes got flustered by himself, sometimes laughed by himself... and so he continued walking with Lishia on his back.
Before he knew it, stars were peeking out one by one in the night sky. On the dark night road... Aaron was still walking. His leg still throbbed with severe pain, and having not eaten all day, overexerted himself, and lost blood, a slight dizziness came over him. Yet, strangely, Aaron felt happy.
Someone had called Aaron a skilled warrior, but he was now tired of battles. He wanted to live a peaceful life. If only he could...
Aaron began to sing. Of course, Aaron knew very well that he was tone-deaf by nature.
But he just wanted to try singing the spirit's song that Lishia used to sing. So, perhaps not wanting anyone to hear his voice, he sang the spirit's song in a quiet voice. Before he knew it, the warm lights of the city welcomed Aaron.

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
In front of the cave where the Temple of Darkness was located, there was a huge crater, as if a large meteor had fallen. The surrounding trees were bent or broken outwards from the pit, showing the power of Rice's self-destruct spell. In the middle of the pit, a half-buried tree was shaking.

The tree moved slightly, and then a human hand emerged from under the soil. The hand grabbed a branch of the fallen tree, which was buried in the dirt, and pulled up a naked, emaciated body. From somewhere within that gaunt body, a strength comparable to that of a young man could be felt. The old man with sharp eyes was Esbaal, who had been wounded by Rice. As he stepped out from the shade of the tree into the sunlight, his skin sizzled and burned. Esbaal was startled and quickly retreated into the shade, muttering.
"Damn it! He put a dark spell into the self-destruct spell."

Esbaal had shed his monstrous form and returned to his human shape. However, his body was severely wounded, and he staggered out of the pit, shielding himself from the sunlight as much as possible, and slowly re-entered the cave.
The cave was enveloped in complete darkness, and it seemed as if that darkness would perfectly cover him no matter what he did. Esbaal gasped for breath and began to recover his body in the darkness. But he knew that he would never be able to bask in the sunlight again.
"It's all for nothing anyway... Rice... I will cover this world in darkness with my own hands anyway. When the sun loses its light, your curse will be useless... Hehehe."
As his low, eerie laughter echoed through the cave, the candles hanging on the cave walls flickered, and the shadows danced with them.

"Are you alright, Lishia?"
Aaron asked, concerned by Lishia's unusual expression. Lishia's normally pale face was even paler, almost sickly. Lishia didn't answer. Aaron felt sorry for her. It seemed the emotional wounds she had suffered from Esbaal earlier were deep, especially for someone already so fragile.
"Let's take a short break."
They found some shade under a tree and sat down by the roadside. It was a quiet forest path, but the sun in the sky beat down quite hot on the group. The number of breaks the group took was increasing due to Lishia's weakened state. Lishia was mentally and physically exhausted.
"It seems Rice succeeded in stopping Esbaal. Given that they're not chasing us..."
Dagmon wiped his sweat, looking relieved, but Elon replied with a worried voice.
"Since he sacrificed so much, I hope he dealt with him completely... If not..."
"As he said, we need to find the magic of light quickly."
"But Lishia's condition is like this..."
Elon worried about Lishia.
"She'll recover soon."
Aaron was very worried inside, but he answered calmly without showing it. Just then, Lishia suddenly seemed to remember something and began to chant a spell while sitting. Suddenly, darkness began to spread around the group.
"What! What is it? Is it Esbaal!"
Aaron jumped up and shouted. Soon, a darkness so profound that the group couldn't see an inch in front of them enveloped them.
"No, it's Lishia. She cast a spirit summoning spell."
Dagmon cautiously spoke, surveying the completely darkened surroundings. Aaron looked around. The surroundings were completely dark, but strangely, he could still make out his companions next to him. Beads of sweat formed on Lishia's face as she chanted the spell, looking very strained. Suddenly, Lishia stopped chanting.
Then, the darkness vanished as if it had never been there. Lishia then looked startled by something with unfocused eyes and collapsed on the spot.
"Lishia! Lishia!"
Aaron's urgent shouts grew fainter and fainter in Lishia's ears.
In the darkness, Lishia heard rough breathing.
It seemed to be breathing right by her ear. No... she wondered if it was her own breathing. But the breathing didn't sound human. It was the sound of something that everyone cursed, something she had occasionally felt since childhood. Father... she remembered her father's back from when she was little. Her father never returned home after that day.

Lishia screamed and sat up. Her last memory was casting a spell by the roadside, but now she was in a neatly made bed. The room was dark. Lishia realized she was wearing a pure white nightgown instead of her usual traveler's clothes. Her body trembled slightly, and a chill ran through her. It was a moment when she truly felt alive.
Looking around, she saw light seeping from under the door, and outside, she heard people chatting. Lishia soon realized she was in an inn room. Memories slowly returned. The fight with Esbaal, the things Salmora, the spirit of shadow, had shown her.
Suddenly, Lishia was overcome with sorrow. She just wanted to cry her eyes out. But Lishia didn't want anyone to hear her crying. She soon pulled the blanket over her head, her shoulders shaking, and began to soak the pillow underneath. As Lishia cried silently, she heard the door open.
"Lishia, are you okay?"
Serah's worried voice was heard.
"......."
Lishia, not wanting to be caught crying, didn't answer. Serah then sat by the bed and gently lifted the blanket.
"Lishia... why are you crying?"
Serah gently patted Lishia, asking like an older sister. Lishia then burst into tears and hugged Serah.
"Sniffle... Sister..."
"What's wrong? Why are you just crying like a fool?"
"There's a terrifying evil power in my body. I wish I had never been born... Sniffle."
"What are you talking about? Silly girl?"
Lishia cried while talking, still hugging Serah.
"Salmora told me. Esbaal is my grandfather. He was the former chief of the tribe of darkness, and he cultivated evil power in my mother. But when my mother married my father, who was a light mage, my father sacrificed his life and freed my grandfather in exchange for saving the child my mother was carrying and my mother from the power of darkness. The child she was carrying back then, Rice, who saved us last time, is my older brother. And I... I... I shouldn't have been born... Sniffle. There's a terrifying power residing in my body."
"Don't talk nonsense. Where is such a thing in your body?"
"I'd rather die. It would have been better if I hadn't been born. Sniffle."
"Don't say such things."
"Everyone will be afraid of me or hate me. Even you, Sister, and Aaron... I know what that's like. In the end, I'm all alone. Sniffle."
Lishia remembered the time when she was a child, when other children ostracized her for using magic and hearing things others couldn't.
"That's not true. People wouldn't be afraid of or hate Lishia... Neither would I or Aaron... Stop it, rest. You're probably just tired."
Serah continued to comfort Lishia, and Lishia gradually calmed down.
"You're thinking these things because you're not feeling well right now. You'll feel better when you regain your strength."
Serah stroked Lishia's forehead, laid her down, and spoke gently.
"I'm sorry."
Lishia had completely stopped crying.
"What do you have to be sorry to me for?"
"Just."
Lishia smiled slightly, tears still in her eyes. Even with only the light coming from the open door, her smile looked beautiful enough.
"You're good at smiling. It makes even those who see it feel at ease."
Serah pulled the blanket over her.
"Pfft~ There's no such thing."
"You like Aaron, don't you?"
"No. Why would I like someone like that?"
Lishia's face flushed slightly, and she answered with a start.
"Surprised? It's written all over your face."
Then Lishia spoke with a slightly hesitant tone.
"Actually..."
"What is it? Tell me. Your big sister will listen to everything."
"What does Aaron think of me? He always tells me to just call him 'Oppa.' He just teases me for being young..."
"Hmm... Well, Aaron probably doesn't dislike you. Any man who dislikes such a pretty young lady would be a fool."
"Sister... don't confuse me."
"More than that... seeing that fool sweating profusely with a worried expression, carrying you all the way here, it seems he does like you. He ran so fast that we had trouble keeping up. Even though he seems so nonchalant on the surface."
"Really?"
Lishia asked with a much brighter face.
"Yes."
"Then, that's enough."
"Then, good night."
"Sister, do you really have to leave?"
"Why?"
"I'm scared..."
"That's why Aaron says you're young."
Serah chided her.
"Still..."
Lishia, with sad, teary eyes, clutched Serah's sleeve.
"Alright. I'll stay here holding your hand until you fall asleep."
Lishia closed her eyes. Lishia was truly afraid of being alone and of the darkness. It wasn't because she was young. It was because of the terrifying thoughts and images that came with the darkness. They constantly swirled vividly within her, in her ears, making Lishia even more alone and trembling with fear. That presence would appear in the darkness at any time and whisper to her.
"How's Lishia?"
Aaron asked Serah.
"She just woke up and fell back asleep. What's wrong? Aaron worrying about Lishia?"
"Still, he's the one who carried Lishia all the way here..."
Elon said, raising a glass of milk.
"Don't think strange thoughts. Lishia is my sister."
Aaron stated definitively.
"Lishia probably doesn't think so, though?"
Serah said with a smile.
"More importantly, how am I?"
Dagmon asked Serah with a smile.
"Don't talk nonsense,"

"Who would like a man who talks like a younger brother, always adding 'yo' to the end of his sentences?" Sera said mischievously. Elron looked slightly displeased by Sera and Dagmon's jokes. Aaron didn't miss Elron's expression.

It was strange even to Aaron. There was nothing for Elron, a talent of his caliber, to gain by staying with Sera. No matter how long they had been friends since childhood... Sera could only be an obstacle, holding him back as a soldier, yet he remained by her side until the end, which was incomprehensible by conventional standards.

"How did we suddenly get onto the topic of romance? More importantly, how will we go to Agol with Lishia like this?" Elron suddenly changed the subject.

"First, with Lishia like this, we have no choice but to rest," Dagmon replied in a weak voice.

"Even if Eva might be chasing us?"

"Right now, Aaron and I are the only ones who can read ancient languages, but we're at a child's level compared to Lishia. And Aaron and I don't know everything. It could take months if we were to decipher it ourselves."

"Oh. This is a predicament," Elron replied with a disappointed voice.

"What are you talking about? Leaving a sick person behind," Sera replied, sounding annoyed.

When the party was startled by the roar from inside the cave, a tremendous gust of wind and energy simultaneously poured out from within.
“Everyone, get away from the cave!”
Aaron, who quickly assessed the situation, shouted, and Dagmon, Sera, and Elon swiftly moved away at Aaron's command, but Licia and Islia were not as quick as them. A massive flame, large enough to fill the cave, erupted from the cave entrance, about to engulf them.
“Those fools!”
Aaron threw himself, rolling with the two of them, and the flames incinerated the spot where they had been.
- Wow... this brother is faster than I thought... -
Islia exclaimed in admiration.
- What are you talking about? We almost died. -
Licia, despite the danger, felt strangely good. However, she knew this was not the time for such feelings. A dark energy emerged from the cave, taking shape. Aaron drew his sword and quickly stood up.
Aaron expected some grotesque monster to appear, but instead, an old man wearing the tattered clothes of the Tribe of Darkness, looking gaunt, emerged holding a black magic staff. Due to the nature of the Tribe of Darkness's attire, the old man's face was unrecognizable.
“So it was you... Hehehe... I wondered who it was.”
The old man's eerie voice echoed.
“What on earth are you doing inside the cave?!”
Aaron, convinced that he was responsible for the situation inside the cave, shouted.
“I am Esbaal.”
“Esbaal?”
Aaron was startled to hear that name.
“Are you the one who has been trying to kill me, for whatever grudge you hold?”
“Yes. The power of light is a nuisance... It's the only way I can be defeated. Rice must have failed. Seeing as you've made it this far...”
Just then, as soon as those words fell, Rice appeared from the forest.
“You've arrived just in time... Rice.”
Esbaal said with a slightly sly smile.
- Brother! -
Islia made a joyful expression upon seeing him.
“There was no one in the village, and I saw smoke coming from the temple, so I came to check. It was you all.”
Rice first assessed the situation. Normally, he would have attacked Aaron's party, but now that he knew Esbaal's objective, he didn't know what to do. Yet, defying Esbaal was not an easy task. Rice knew best that Esbaal possessed power greater than all of Rice and Aaron's party combined, and regardless, Esbaal had been his benefactor since childhood.
Aaron was in a predicament with Rice's appearance.
‘It's raining cats and dogs.’
Aaron had already witnessed Rice's formidable power. He could easily predict that Esbaal would be even more powerful.
“The chances of winning this fight... are almost zero.”
Aaron muttered to himself.
“You know it well... young man. Hehehe.”
Esbaal's unpleasant laughter echoed.
“The old man has sharp ears... But even so, we can't lose without even trying.”
Aaron gripped his sword. Esbaal's incantation rang out. Soon, a dark energy seemed to extend from his body, then all of it poured down towards Aaron. Aaron swiftly dodged the energies. The moment Aaron thought he had avoided the energy, he felt as if his head was splitting. Esbaal's staff had already struck Aaron.
‘Ugh... fast...’
Esbaal deliberately struck Aaron towards where the other party members were. Aaron collided with them, rolled around, and then, letting out a faint groan, barely managed to get up.
‘No way... so easily...’
“Aaron, are you alright?”
Dagmon supported Aaron. Blood was flowing from Aaron's head, and his knees buckled momentarily, perhaps from a slight concussion.
“Hehehe. I could have killed you. Understand? Young man?”
Esbaal mocked Aaron as if playing with him.
“We have no choice but to attack simultaneously.”
Dagmon said.
“There are two opponents. What should we do?”
Elon said, looking at Rice who was just watching from a distance.
“Sera and I will take on Rice, and Elon, Licia, and Aaron will face Esbaal. A real fight is impossible. We just have to find an opportunity to escape... I'll set off a smoke bomb.”
Dagmon quietly told his plan to the party. Dagmon signaled Licia, and simultaneously, they began to charge.
Licia also received the signal.
- Islia. You stay back. -
Islia stepped back for a moment at Licia's words.
“Amasha!”
Licia chanted a spell, Dagmon aimed his crossbow, and Sera, Elon, and Aaron each drew their swords and charged at their respective opponents.
Esbaal easily blocked Licia's magic and prepared for the next move, but...
Rice, caught off guard by the sudden attack, failed to dodge Dagmon's crossbow bolt and was hit in the shoulder. Then, letting out a faint groan, he narrowly avoided Sera's incoming sword.
“Ugh...”
Sera's continuous attacks kept coming. Rice also possessed considerable warrior capabilities, but since Rice was a mage, Sera's basic skills were superior, so Rice couldn't find an opportunity to cast a spell and kept dodging.
Islia was startled by the sight of Licia's party attacking Rice.
- Stop it! -
Islia shouted, but her voice was only heard by Licia.
Dagmon, still flustered and dodging Sera's sword, aimed his crossbow at Rice's heart.
‘Mages can't cast spells if you don't give them a chance. This is the end.’
Dagmon pulled the crossbow's trigger while aiming precisely. However, the crossbow did not fire.
‘Click, click’
He pulled the trigger several times, but it was the same.
‘Huh? What's wrong?’
As Dagmon was wondering what was wrong, the crossbow in his hand suddenly shattered, and Dagmon's body seemed to float up before being flung into the bushes. He screamed as he fell. Licia, realizing Islia had used her power, was startled and stopped fighting Esbaal, shouting at Islia.
- Islia! What are you doing?! -
- You hurt my brother! -
- What are you talking about?! -
- My brother. Brother Rice, I mean! I see now you sisters were bad people! -
As Islia began to use her power, an eerie wind started to blow around her.
Esbaal was facing Aaron and Elon, the most skilled swordsmen, but he seemed to be holding back, fighting with little effort. Then, when Islia used her power, he even had the leisure to look her way with an inscrutable smile.
When Islia unleashed her power, everyone except Esbaal and Rice was swept away and sent flying.
“Quite an interesting child... Heheheh.”
Esbaal laughed with an unpleasant voice, as if amused. Dagmon's plan to escape at the opportune moment was completely derailed thanks to Islia.
- Islia! Stop it! -
Licia barely managed to get up and said. Then Islia stopped her power, as if suppressing her anger.
As Esbaal chanted a spell, a black magic barrier was cast around the fallen party members. Aaron and his companions tried to move, but they couldn't move a single hair.
‘Damn it... it's over.’
Aaron felt despair.
- That's a misunderstanding. -
Licia tried to communicate with Islia even in her immobilized state.
- Enough. I don't need to listen to you, sister. My brother's enemy is my enemy. -
Islia's voice echoed sharply in Licia's mind.
“Kill those guys, except for that girl!”
Esbaal pointed at Licia with his finger and said curtly in a cold voice.
Rice approached Aaron's party. However, Rice's answer was unexpected.
“I have no business with you.”
Rice said to the party, pulling out the arrow from his shoulder that Dagmon had shot.
‘What on earth does that mean?’
Aaron tried to ask the meaning of those words, but he couldn't move his lips within the barrier.
‘Damn it...’
“Are you defying my orders?!”
Esbaal shouted at Rice with an enraged voice.
“No, sir. But before that, there's something I'd like to ask.”
However, Rice still maintained a respectful attitude towards Esbaal. Rice went before Esbaal, knelt on one knee, and looked up at Esbaal, asking.
“What exactly are you planning? I saw documents in the Temple of Light about the magic you, Esbaal, have been performing. First using animal corpses, then human beings, to revive the dead. Why did you use the villagers as sacrifices?”
“Small sacrifices are inevitable.”
“Sacrifices? What is it you wish to gain by going to such lengths? Is it truly to reclaim our land?”
At that, Esbaal burst into loud laughter.
“Land? To the God of Darkness, all land belongs to the God of Darkness. Land is not needed.”
“Then what is your objective?”
“A world of ultimate darkness and resurrection. A world where there is no pain, no suffering, nothing at all.”
Esbaal spoke in a low voice after a faint, cold smile. Rice remained silent for a moment.
“Then, what do you intend to use that girl, Licia, for?”
“Once the world of darkness is created, a leader will be needed to govern those resurrected with powerful dark energy. Dark blood, which I implanted, flows within that child's body, giving her immense dark power. That power will summon the Dark Lord.”
“What do you intend to do by plunging the world into darkness...”
“Heheh. This wretched world deserved it. Ever since those damned two generals tried to kill me! If only that accursed Eldge hadn't used light magic...”
Esbaal removed the black hood he was wearing. A gaunt old man with eerie, cold eyes was revealed. The old man's gaze was filled with resentment for something. Rice felt an evil aura along with a sense that something was deeply wrong in the old man's eyes.
“The dead

“If they are revived, what will they find joy in, and what will they live for in a world devoid of hope? You are truly insane...”
Rice shouted in an agitated voice, then finally scoffed.
“Insane, you say! Look at this fellow's words! Who raised you, you scoundrel!”
Rice sprang to his feet. And then he shouted.
“The Tribes of Darkness... Although they lived scorned by the world, they at least never thought of plunging the world into darkness!”
“Hmph... Tribes of Darkness, you say? Those aren't the Tribes of Darkness! They are merely those who *pretend* to be the Tribes of Darkness. Those two dead old men changed them. They tainted them with the spirit of light. You don't know the true race of perfect darkness. Perfect darkness is not like that.”

The day after a battle that felt like it would last forever, they were greeted by the same ordinary morning. Only their still-tired bodies and wounds that even magic couldn't heal remained as vivid evidence of yesterday's fight, yet the party members acted as if they had forgotten yesterday, waking up and behaving just the same.

Licia could feel them trying to act even more nonchalantly, as if yesterday's events had never happened. Their demeanor felt strange, but Licia realized there was nothing she could do.

And so, they began their journey again. They chatted idly as usual, laughed at jokes that weren't particularly funny, and seemed to be trying to forget yesterday's events as quickly as possible. Only then did Licia begin to understand Aaron's past behavior a little. When Aaron occasionally showed a strange sadness, she didn't know exactly where it came from, but she merely guessed it was something similar. However, Licia concluded that only Aaron himself would know the detailed reason for his actions.

They left the front lines and entered Dobel, the nearest village. The village was already nothing short of ruins. It seemed a fierce battle had taken place just a few days ago, leaving houses with only their walls standing, scattered household items, a half-burnt rag doll that some child must have cherished... And the nauseating stench of unburied corpses, naked crying children, and smoke still rising here and there, indicating lingering embers. Even the buried bodies were more like covered with dirt than properly interred, and rats and flies swarmed. The surviving children and elderly were searching for food amidst the chaos, but as Aaron's sword-wielding party approached, they kept their distance and hid.

Each of them, with eyes that seemed to be mere holes, watched Aaron's party from hiding, filled with fear, curiosity, and a faint hope for help. The sight was so horrific that it shocked Licia and Sera. But Aaron, seeing it, remained unmoved and said,

“It's impossible to rest here today. We should leave this place quickly.”

For some reason, Licia found Aaron's demeanor frightening and unfamiliar. Seeing a naked child staring intently from behind a collapsed building, her throat tightened.

“Can't we help them before we go?”

Aaron, as expected, firmly refused.

“No.”

“Why not?”

“There's nothing we can do.”

“Dagmon can fix houses, I can heal the injured, and we can share food, can't we?”

Licia pleaded like a child whining. Licia sent Dagmon an encouraging look, but Dagmon also avoided her gaze. Aaron explained to Licia as if annoyed.

“We can't help some and not others. There are countless people like them here. Moreover, any change would only be temporary. Until the war ends, this place will almost always look like this. Or, this village will soon disappear...”

Licia asked Aaron, sounding resentful.

“Aaron, do you have no blood or tears?”

But Aaron simply said calmly,

“If it can't be done, it can't be done. Let's get out of here quickly. Places like this have many thieves, so it's not a good place to stay long.”

Aaron merely quickened his pace.

“What kind of person is he?”

Sera muttered, seeing his back, and Dagmon admonished her.

“Aaron doesn't want to be like that. It's because he knows it's futile. I, too, initially had thoughts like Sera's and Licia's. I tried. It's too much for us to handle. It's all the same anyway. Until the war ends...”

“When will this damn war end?!”

Sera complained.

“I don't know...”

Dagmon replied quietly with a faint, bitter smile.

“Dagmon, what do you fear on the battlefield?”

Licia, who had been listening quietly beside them, asked. But again, Dagmon didn't answer. Just as Licia was thinking she wouldn't get an answer from Dagmon again, he replied softly.

“Myself. My own self, for having these thoughts. Can I truly be called a human after this? And am I truly fit to be a leader?... But at the same time, I cannot think only humanely. I once engaged in war that way. Because of it, I saved dozens of lives I tried to rescue, but I lost thousands of my subordinates. I hate this battlefield that forces such thoughts upon me, and I fear this place that makes me, as a prince, bear the responsibility of choosing victims. Those people right there are such victims. Aaron, in fact, knows better than Licia what will happen if they are left as they are. That's why Licia's words must have sounded like a dagger to Aaron.”

“What words?”

“The words 'you have no blood or tears.'”

“But it's true.”

Sera replied in a sulky voice.

“Aaron wouldn't have said those words happily either. But reason and reality teach that such emotions are futile for survival, and Aaron acts according to that reason. Reason is wise, but also a cold entity. He hates himself for being swayed by it. And so do I.”

“So, do reason and reality command that it's okay to kill people?”

Licia asked again.

“As needed...”

“You mean human lives are 'as needed'?”

Licia asked reproachfully.

“........”

Dagmon fell silent again. Licia already vaguely understood. But she hated it. That human lives could be extinguished 'as needed'...

However, Licia was gradually coming to understand many things. She felt that the battlefield was teaching her far too many useless lessons.

But no matter how much she understood intellectually, Licia could not bring herself to commit to killing people.

Before they knew it, they had left the front lines and approached the camp where Laodicea's advance troops were stationed. Thanks to Dagmon, they were able to get through there safely without any major incidents.

At any rate, they were getting away from the battlefield. Licia looked at the soldiers marching towards the front lines again. Their expressions were no different from those of General Yeogoniya's subordinates.

‘By birth, I am a person of Laodicea, and Aaron is a person of Ceres. What on earth are we fighting for? The kings' excuses about national glory sound ridiculous... Hurting, bleeding... Am I truly powerless? They will continue to bleed even after we leave.’

Most of them, like the soldiers of Ceres, were risking their lives fighting a war they didn't want. Seeing their backs, Licia felt tears welling up. Aaron approached Licia, roughly ruffled her hair, and said,

“Don't think too deeply, you're still just a child.”

Licia bristled again at Aaron treating her like a child.

“What?! A child?!”

But Aaron didn't retort; he just smiled and replied,

“That's more like you.”

At his smile, Licia was momentarily speechless.

To return to Laodicea, Rice boarded a ship bound for Nicopolis. In his skirmish with Herodion, one of Rice's arms, hidden beneath his black clothes, had become unusable. It was a side effect of overusing dark magic to detoxify a poisoned arrow. Though recovery magic had somewhat healed it, reducing the pain, the arm still felt cumbersome.

He stood on the deck, watching children playing. Laughing... chatting... Rice knew those children would fear and dislike him, a being of darkness, but he found their sight pleasing.

Rice thought of Islia. The child's innocent smile... But he clearly felt something was missing in Islia. Was it because she was a being of darkness? Rice wanted to fill that missing something for Islia.

The confirmation that Aaron's party had gone to Laodicea came from the Light Ruins, where they arrived late. They found the Temple of Light in the ruins and deciphered the stone tablets Aaron's party had left behind after searching. Thanks to this, they also learned of Esbaal's plan.

The plan was one that even Rice, a being of darkness, could not comprehend. His promise to the tribesmen about reclaiming lost lands was a lie. The truth was to resurrect the dead and create a world of complete chaos and death. It was neither conquest nor anything else; it was pure destruction and chaos itself. Then, the innocent smiles of children would surely never be seen again.

그 병사는 리시아에게 가라고 재촉했다.
“ 아저씨. 제발 무사하세요. ”
리시아는 그 병사의 볼에 키스를 했다.
“ 아가씨를 보면 정말 내 딸같은 기분이 드는군. 자. 이제 한바탕해야지. ”
그 병사도 창을 집어 들었다. 리시아도 엘론과 아론이 있는 무리로 들어갔다.
“ 가자! ”
우렁찬 병사들의 외침이 피의 고지를 가득 채웠다. 피의 고지를 다시 물들일 여고니야 장군의 마지막 접전이 시작되었다.

Then Yegoniya chuckled and replied, "It's an honor, but I'm not that great a general. The number of soldiers I've sent ahead so far is as numerous as the stars in the sky."
Dagmon felt a strange sense of shame in front of Yegoniya and said with a somber expression, "I respect how you think of your subordinates and take responsibility. In contrast, I..."
Yegoniya cut Dagmon off. "Wait a moment, Prince. I know what you're about to say. I know what battle you participated in two years ago. I remember the soldiers of Laodicea who piled up mountains of corpses to protect you then. One of the units that attacked you was mine, after all. But are you someone who only has to take responsibility for your subordinates? Your caliber is different. And don't be afraid; fulfill that responsibility. That is the path to atonement for the subordinates who died for you."
Dagmon froze at Yegoniya's words, unable to say anything. Yegoniya smiled, patted Dagmon's shoulder a few times, and then returned to his subordinates.
Before long, the appointed night arrived. Elon selected the soldiers who would break through the encirclement. However, many of the able-bodied soldiers he chose said they would stay with Yegoniya. Elon, knowing well that he couldn't stop them, gave them no other orders.
"Something's wrong."
Lisia muttered to herself, watching the scene.
"What's wrong?"
Aron asked in a low voice.
"Why... do we have to leave them behind? The wounded, the suffering ones. If we leave them like this, they'll die. I can even use healing magic."
"Don't even think about using healing magic."
"How can you say that? They are lives too. Precious ones."
"I know."
Aron replied curtly.
"How can someone who knows say such a thing!"
"......."
"Aron has changed too. He wasn't that cold of a person before..."
"I know."
"Aron is a beast. Bloodthirsty."
"I know! I know!" Suddenly, Aron yelled in anger and stormed out of the cave. Lisia's words felt like torture to Aron, piercing only his sore spots.
Just then, the soldier who had saved Lisia during the day approached her.
"Mister. Are you going to stay here too?"
The soldier silently nodded his head.
"What kind of talk is that! What on earth is going on? Everyone? Am I the strange one, and are Aron and Elon right?"
"If you mean Aron, you're talking about the young man who told you not to use healing magic. He didn't look like a soldier, but judging by his skill, he seems to have mercenary experience. He's right. You shouldn't use magic, young lady. Here, your own survival is the most important thing."
"Then why are you trying to stay here, mister? While saying survival is important. You don't have any remaining family, so you could just flee to Laodicea, couldn't you?"
"No. Rather, because of that, I want to end it now."
"What kind of talk is that!"
"That's..."
The soldier didn't answer easily, as if searching for an excuse.
"I don't know. Since you ask, young lady... It's just that no matter how scary a face I make, or how many opponents I kill, it's hard and scary now. Everyone is afraid."
"What are they afraid of? Killing people? If you're so afraid, why do you do it?"
"Well, I don't know. It's probably not just the fear of killing."
"Then what are they afraid of?"
"Themselves."
"Themselves? What does that mean?"
"Aron, that friend, and Prince Dagmon will know the answer. Think about it carefully. You have plenty of time..."
"That sounds like a very difficult quiz."
Lisia offered a faint smile.
"Beautiful."
"What is?"
"Your smile, young lady..."
"Laughter here isn't normal. Everyone just laughs meaninglessly. Isn't there a passage in the song of the Tribe of Darkness that goes like this?"
"What is it?"
"It's strange for a mage not to know that."
The soldier began to sing a gloomy song.
"The Moon Maiden sings... a song of darkness... Darkness brings blood...
Blood brings death... Death brings... nothing. Nothing...
The Crescent Maiden sings... a song of sorrow. A song of sorrow that flows eternally...
A song of blood... That song laughs... laughs..."
"There was such a song? It's too unpleasant to call it a song."
"Because I was once part of the Tribe of Darkness..."
Just then, shouts were heard from outside the cave.
"The Laodicean army's offensive has resumed!"
The urgent cry of a sentry was heard.
"Oh no. So soon!"
Aron picked up his sword.
"Alright! My comrades! Let's face the end together!"
General Yegoniya's voice and the thunderous shouts of his soldiers echoed.
"Alright! Let's go!"
Elon, outside the cave, also led a group of soldiers and shouted.
"Now, young lady, hurry and go. Stick close to that young man. He seems trustworthy."
The soldier urged Lisia to go.
"Mister. Please be safe."
Lisia kissed the soldier's cheek.
"Seeing you, young lady, truly makes me feel like you're my daughter. Alright. Now it's time for a fight."
The soldier also picked up his spear. Lisia joined the group where Elon and Aron were.
"Charge!"
The thunderous shouts of the soldiers filled the Bloody Hill. General Yegoniya's final battle, which would once again dye the Bloody Hill, had begun.

{{IMG:1}}
The tribes of darkness traditionally did not light many fires at night, making the entire village seem to exist within a black veil, as if it didn't exist at all. In a small room of a house in the village where the tribes of darkness lived, Islia lay on her bed, eyes closed, singing. Various sounds kept reaching her ears. Whispers, animal cries, screams... She couldn't tell which were real and which were hallucinations. In the dark shadows of the room's corner, she felt as if someone was there. She wanted to light a fire, but she knew the aunt who cared for her would surely get angry. Islia squeezed her eyes shut and sang in a small voice.
- The Moon Maiden sings. A song of darkness. Darkness is blood.
Blood is death. Death is nothing. Nothing.
The Crescent Maiden sings. A song of sorrow. A song of sorrow that flows eternally.
A song of blood... That song laughs. It laughs.-
Islia pulled the blanket tight and closed her eyes. Rice-oppa came to mind, but he wasn't by her side now. Suddenly, loneliness crept in between her fearful emotions. To chase away the fear and loneliness, Islia sang. The song was a traditional tune passed down among the tribes of darkness, singing of the play of death. Yet, the song only made Islia more afraid.
However, Islia knew no other songs. All she could do was sing, hoping the darkness would recede. Islia lowered her blanket again and gently opened her eyes. But still, the room was filled with darkness, and she could see nothing. Just then, as if the wind had started to blow, the rattling window sound shook Islia even more intensely.
'I'm scared...'
Islia was becoming increasingly terrified, unable to bear it. The wind grew louder, and the rattling of the window became more severe. Islia kept singing, but the more she sang, the more afraid she became.
'Clatter, clatter,'
The sound of the window continued.
'If I couldn't hear it... if only I couldn't hear it... I'd be less scared...'
Islia's entire focus began to concentrate on her ears. Before she knew it, the sound of the window was gradually fading away. Only in Islia's ears...
The next morning, Islia woke up. It was a bright morning... Outside was bright. But the usual morning birdsong was absent.
'Why?'
Islia was afraid. Startled, Islia flung open the door and went outside. Children were playing as if they were from another world. The only difference from usual was that no sound could be heard. The entire world was nothing but silence. Just then, someone snatched Islia's hand. It was the aunt who cared for Islia. The aunt shouted something at Islia. But she couldn't hear it. The aunt started hitting Islia again. Islia cried, but she couldn't even hear her own cries. The entire world was enveloped in silence.
'Waaah~! Whoosh! Boom~ Boom~'
From afar, loud explosions, shouts, and drum-like sounds could be heard. Aaron's party, heading south by land, could already feel the battlefield drawing near.
"It must be a huge battle~ to be heard all the way here."
"I really don't want to get caught up in those guys' fighting."
Aaron muttered, looking troubled. Just then, there was a rustling movement in the bushes by the roadside, and the party froze, a chill of killing intent running down their spines.
"Who's there! Sky!"
A voice from one side of the bushes shouted a password to the party. Aaron's hand went to his sword hilt. But the enemy's form was not visible.
"Wait, Aaron. If you rush in carelessly, you'll only get hurt."
Ellon stopped Aaron.
"Sky! Give the password! We have you targeted from this side!"
The shouting voice was heard again.
"I am General Ellon, third in command of the Royal Guard of Ceres! If you doubt me, you may bind me and confirm it at your camp!"
Ellon shouted, holding his sword forward.
After Ellon shouted, a moment of silence passed, then a group, seemingly Ceres soldiers, walked out.
Their faces were painted black, and their armor was adorned with leaves for camouflage, making them look like moving bushes. Their faces looked a little tired, but they had bronzed complexions, and upon closer inspection, their armor bore many scars, indicating they were seasoned soldiers with considerable combat experience. They were still wary of Aaron's party, and it was clear that in addition to those carrying swords and spears, there were more hidden, aiming their bows. One soldier, seeing Ellon, showed a welcoming face, gave a short salute, and approached.
"Isn't this truly General Ellon? I had the honor of seeing your face before."
"What is your unit?"
When Ellon asked, the soldier replied.
"We are the scout infantry of General Yeogoniya, currently stationed near Dabanes. But why have you come here without a messenger in advance? It's a good thing I recognized you, or we might have attacked by mistake."
Ellon's face brightened at the mention of an acquaintance's name and he asked again.
"Yeogoniya? He was in Dabanes?"
"Yes. The recent war situation hasn't been very good, so General Yeogoniya is personally preparing a surprise attack to turn the tide. But, who are these people with you?"
"This is Princess Sera."
"Princess? Everyone, come out and pay your respects to the Princess!"
Then, those who had been in ambush emerged from the bushes, and all the soldiers knelt before Princess Sera and paid their respects. Sera's face turned red, feeling more honored here than she ever did in the palace.
"It will be night soon, so no matter where you're going, please come with us. It will be safer to spend the night at our camp."
"Understood."
Aaron's party followed the soldiers. The soldiers buzzed at the mention of Princess Sera and also glanced at Lishia. Aaron somewhat understood the meaning of those gazes, so he wasn't in a good mood, but he knew it was difficult to impose on soldiers on the front lines. Lishia wondered why they kept looking at her, but not knowing the meaning, she was only a little embarrassed.
The soldier who first recognized Ellon spoke to him.
"Our unit is preparing to ambush an enemy unit of Dangeup (approx. 2,000). Oh, and many of the soldiers who used to be under General Ellon's command have recently been reassigned to our unit. Their praise for General Ellon is immense. Well... among us, the battle records of that unit are passed down like heroic tales. General, you are clearly future commander-in-chief material. A hundred times better than the current commander-in-chief. That cruel..."
As the soldier kept praising him, Ellon, feeling awkward, cut him off.
"That's enough. You've praised me enough."
"Anyway, no one on the battlefield wouldn't know General Ellon. The war situation is really bad these days, and everyone is anxious. If General Ellon is here, morale will surely rise."
They walked for a while and arrived in front of a large wooden fortress.
"Sky!"
As the password echoed from atop the fortress, the soldiers replied.
"Rear scout unit. Eagle. Open the gate! We've brought guests."
When he shouted, one of the wooden gates opened. They stepped inside the fortress. They were led into a large tent built in the very center of the fortress. Inside, a knight in armor seemed to be giving tactical instructions to his staff.
"General Yeogoniya. We've brought guests."
"What are you talking about? We're in a strategy meeting right now! Talk later!"
Yeogoniya snapped, yelling without even checking the party's faces.
"Please wait a moment."
The soldier approached the party and spoke apologetically.
"It's fine. He's always like that during strategy meetings... More than that, I'd like to see his skill for once."
When Ellon told the soldier it was okay, the soldier finally seemed relieved. After a while, having finished explaining the strategy, Yeogoniya slammed his hand on the table and shouted.
"That's all! Any more questions?"
Ellon gently raised one hand and asked.
"In that case, where do the 2nd and 3rd companies retreat after the attack? It seems they might get isolated, General?"
Yeogoniya then seemed to recognize Ellon's face, grinned, and replied.
"You don't know that either? You, soldier, you've wasted your military rations. You retreat into the valley between Hill 28 and Hill 32. If you want to survive, you have to find that much. And I made the 2nd and 3rd companies with guys who may lack skill but are like ghosts at escaping, so don't worry about getting isolated."
"Isn't that too much? Saying we lack skill. You said we were special operations mobile forces before."
When a soldier, who appeared to be the commander of the 2nd and 3rd companies, complained, those around them burst into laughter.
"Anyway, if there are no more questions, that's all! Everyone, memorize the strategy I've told you tonight, even in your dreams."
Yeogoniya approached the party.
"Oh~ look who it is? Isn't this Ellon?"
"Long time no see, Yeogoniya. You haven't changed. You're too defensive. Looking at that tactic."
"That's the only way to surely reduce casualties among our soldiers, isn't it? Support from the rear isn't great anyway, so we have to conserve what we have. So. What brings you to this battlefield again? Have you avenged the prince?"
"Well... things got complicated. Haven't you received the message yet?"
"What message?"
"We've become wanted fugitives. We need to quickly pass through the front lines to Laodicea."
Then Yeogoniya's expression changed.
"So you're asking me, a general of Ceres, to help you betray Ceres and defect to Laodicea?"
"Was it too much to ask, after all?"
Ellon said with a look of dismay. Then Yeogoniya clapped Ellon on the shoulder and laughed heartily again, replying.
"Too much? You've come to the right place. That harlot has taken the lives of several good generals."

“I know best what she's achieved, so what? And seeing as I've been sent to the front lines like this, it seems I'm not exactly in her good graces either. I'm stingy when it comes to bribes, you see. We don't even have enough to feed our own kids, when would I ever take care of *her*? If you were to sleep with that rude bitch, I'd crush her 'there,' you know. Haha.”
“Heh heh. That's only if you can defeat that girl.”
“We're in quite a difficult situation right now. You want to pass through this battlefield. It'll be quite tough. I'll help you as much as I can.”
“Thank you.”
“Actually, our troops have been ordered to attack Hill 452 over there.”
“Hill 452? You mean the Hill of Blood?”
“That's right.”
Elron couldn't help but be surprised upon hearing that. The Hill of Blood was the hill whose ownership had changed hands the most during the long war. While it served as a strategic stronghold for magical attacks, it was a very poor place for defense. That's why many units had fallen there. The ground there was so stained with blood that it was said to appear blood-red from a distance.
“It seems you're not exactly in Anania's good graces either.”
Elron let out a deep sigh.
“Heh heh, don't worry. I won't be defeated so easily. Even if that's the case for me, seeing them cast you aside too, it seems this country is truly coming to an end. The recent war situation is becoming very unfavorable for the Ceres Kingdom. We need strong support from the rear to fight, but *she* is only interested in her own gains. Do you think it makes sense that the Ceres Kingdom, which is full of granaries, has less military provisions than Laodicea, which is half desert?”
“Is it that bad...?”
Elron bit his lip, and Yeogoniya looked at his soldiers and spoke.
“It's because of my soldiers, who are like my own children, that I can't leave this place. It's actually good for you. Maybe I should also get completely blacklisted by Anania this time and defect to Laodicea? We're deploying tomorrow. At that time, when we head west, if you follow the ridge in the northeast direction, you'll be able to avoid the battlefield. Today, look around our camp and get some good rest. And, though the princess there might not know it, keep a close eye on that girl. As you know, our boys are longing for women. And so am I, for that matter.”
Licia, who had been listening from behind, blushed. Only then did Licia understand the meaning of the soldiers' burdensome gazes.
“Alright. Go on and rest. Chief of Staff! Escort them.”

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
Aaron's party left Enrogel village and walked for several days, arriving at the Ruins of Light recorded in Eldge's notebook. And. They spent several more days investigating the ruins. Fortunately, Rice and Anania's royal guards did not reappear before them, perhaps because they didn't know where they were headed. Since the ruins covered a considerable area, they set up a camp near the ruins and were conducting their investigation. It was a temporary camp, but thankfully the weather remained good.
"Phew~ This ruin is incredibly vast."
Dagmon complained as he returned after a full day of investigation.
"It's annoyingly vast, indeed."
Elon chimed in.
"How are we ever going to get revenge like this?"
Sera muttered. However, instead of investigating the ruins, Lisia was wandering around nearby, picking armfuls of flowers and arranging them on a mat. In fact, Lisia's work began in the evening. She was responsible for deciphering what others had investigated, as it was faster than each person deciphering things individually.
"Lisia. Please decipher this."
Dagmon handed her what he had written down. But Lisia was more interested in the flowers she had arranged than in the work.
"Dagmon, what's the name of this flower?"
"Hmm... a fringed pink."
"And this one?"
"A pasqueflower."
"A pasqueflower? Heh heh. This looks interesting. It suits its name."
Lisia was happily examining each flower she had laid out on the mat by the campfire. Dagmon felt his spirits lift at Lisia's innocent appearance and smiled. Then, he sat down by the fire and gazed at the flickering flames.
The blazing fire soon drew Dagmon into a world of contemplation.
Remembering his grandfather's teaching to look squarely at the world, he had seen more bad than good after leaving the palace. He lost loved ones and friends, fled to the Eastern Kingdom as if escaping, and studied. After returning from the Eastern Kingdom, he participated in the war his father was waging, but he couldn't bear the sight of people dying before his eyes and the expectations they placed on him. The day he barely escaped from a pile of his fallen subordinates' bodies, he lost all confidence and fled again.
'I cannot save anyone. I am not worthy of their lives.'
He shuddered as if he could hear again the screams of the soldiers he had heard while buried under the pile of corpses.
"Dagmon. What are you thinking about?"
Sera, who had approached him at some point, asked Dagmon.
"Nothing."
"Well. It doesn't seem like nothing."
"Old memories came to mind."
"Old memories? Hmm... I don't recall many good memories from the past either. But seeing you always smile, Dagmon, I thought you had many good memories."
"Good memories?"
Dagmon smiled faintly, recalling good times from long ago. One person's name came to mind.
"I did have them. But I destroyed them with my own hands."
Dagmon said, adding more wood to the campfire.
"Everyone makes mistakes."
"But there are also mistakes that are hard to forgive."
"Why the long face... the most beloved third prince of the Kingdom of Laodicea?"
Sera wanted to say something to cheer Dagmon up. But Dagmon looked at Sera and answered first.
"Thank you."
"Huh? For what?"
"You said it to cheer me up, didn't you?"
Sera was dumbfounded that Dagmon had seen right through her so quickly.
"What? I haven't even started yet. Aren't you too quick on the uptake? Sometimes, it's embarrassing for the person on the receiving end, so please pretend not to notice."
"Haha. Anyway, thank you."
Dagmon chuckled lightly.
"Lisia makes me happy when I see her."
Sera said, looking at Lisia who was still fiddling with the flowers.
"She looks like she doesn't have a care in the world."
"There's no such person. Lisia is probably the same."
"Still, Lisia..."
"I know. She puts people at ease. She brightens everyone's spirits."
"I heard from Lisia why Dagmon uses honorifics, but talking to you like this makes it even stranger. You're a prince of a nation, after all. Why don't you speak more casually?"
"What can I do about my nature? What about Elon?"
"What about Elon?"
"I mean, what kind of person do you think Elon is?"
"He's a good retainer. Loyal... and most of all..."
"Most of all?"
"He's wise. He corrects me when I make wrong judgments... and he's always by my side, which is reassuring."
Sera lowered her gaze slightly, her face flushing. Dagmon felt somewhat uneasy seeing her blush at Elon's name.
"Have you ever thought about him romantically?"
"I always think rationally."
"Not that kind of rationality. As a man."
"As a man? He's cool enough. Brave and decisive."
"When I see Princess Sera, someone comes to mind."
"Who? Surely not a woman like that Gray Witch of the Sea from last time, right?"
"No. Of course not. Haha. She's someone I wronged greatly. I made that unforgivable mistake with her."
"Hmm. Still, if you ask for forgiveness, wouldn't she forgive you?"
"Even if I wanted to ask for forgiveness, I can't anymore."
"May I ask what kind of person she was and why?"
"Everyone has secrets they don't want to tell anyone, don't they? But I can tell you one thing. Princess Sera resembles her a lot in appearance. Her blonde hair, clear eyes... and the overall atmosphere she gives off..."
"Was she a tomboy like me too?"
"No. Her personality seemed quite different."
"What? Only her appearance is similar?"
"Somehow, that's a bit disappointing..."
"Now that I think about it, I also remember feeling upset with Princess Sera once."
"What? When? When I was chasing you to capture you? I'm sorry about that."
"No. Back then, I didn't even know who Princess Sera was."
"Then, when?"
"At Sibiya's deathbed."
"At that time, didn't the princess say? 'We're nothing to each other.'"
"I certainly did."
"Heh heh. Somehow, that phrase 'we're nothing to each other' bothered me."
"What? So, you wanted me to say, 'He's my lover!'?"
"It might have been better if you had."
Dagmon said, as if making a silly joke.
"Tch. What nonsense. Dagmon wouldn't like me, and he must remember when I was chasing him to kill him..."
Then Dagmon closed his eyes for a moment, as if searching for something to say. Just as Sera was getting bored with Dagmon, he opened his eyes again and replied.
"Honestly, I still don't know. Sometimes I get jealous of Elon. And it would be too cowardly to say it's because Princess Sera resembles that person from the past, wouldn't it? Perhaps... I like Princess Sera?"
"What?!"
At Dagmon's sudden and unexpected answer, Sera's face turned red.
"You said her personality was completely different from mine, and she was much more feminine."
"When did I say Princess Sera wasn't feminine? I said her personality was different. Rather, hmm... I'd say she's provocatively sexy in her own way? Princess Sera, look at me for a moment."
Dagmon leaned in close and looked at Sera's face.
"W-what is it?"
Then Sera's face turned red... and Dagmon's face also flushed slightly.
"Indeed. I think I really do love Princess Sera."
Sera shrieked and jumped to her feet, her face bright red.
"Don't make unfunny jokes! Who confesses like that?! And don't look for other women in me, you playboy!"
Sera got up from beside Dagmon and disappeared into the dark shadows of the forest. Dagmon then let out a deep sigh and hung his head. Elon was seen following Sera.
"Did I say something unnecessary..."
Dagmon shook his head, recalling his past with a woman six years ago. How surprised he had been when he first saw Sera's face... It was as if he had met her again, the woman he thought he had forgotten, and he almost burst into tears. But he felt it would be too apologetic to Sera if he said all that.
He was simply driven by the thought that he didn't want to foolishly lose her again, like he did back then, and above all, she felt like a goddess of salvation who had appeared in place of the deceased woman. That's why, in truth, every time he saw Sera, a corner of his heart ached, but he didn't want to reveal those feelings, so he acted playfully. He clutched his chest and silently swallowed his tears. And he thought that he wanted to see Sera smile instead of her.

Sera, who had heard someone say they liked her for the first time in her life, fled from her spot as if escaping, standing behind the forest shadows, trying to calm her racing heart.
However, Sera had no idea of Dagmon's thoughts, and Elon, her escort knight, stood a little distance from her, guarding her as always.

Sibiya's footsteps echoed loudly on the dark night street. After walking a few steps, Sibiya felt something strange. It wasn't just her own footsteps she heard. Someone was walking in sync with her. Too afraid to turn around, she quickened her pace slightly, and the other footsteps also sped up. She instantly turned around. The shadow of a man stood there, holding a long sword.

Sibiya gasped in surprise, stumbled back a few steps, and then began to run desperately towards her home. However, she was soon caught by the man who had been chasing her, her hair grabbed. She was too shocked to even scream. The man's sword was raised. Just as it seemed the sword would strike, the man was pushed by an unknown force, letting go of Sibiya's hair and rolling to the side. Before she knew it, Nergal had arrived, drawing his sword and standing ready.

The man who had tried to kill Sibiya got to his feet and lunged at Nergal. Nergal, being one of the King's Royal Guards, was no ordinary fighter, but the assailant was also no pushover. They clashed swords, inflicting both major and minor wounds on each other. Sibiya was at a loss every time Nergal was wounded, but eventually, Nergal struck the man down and plunged his sword into his body. However, Nergal too was wounded and staggered slightly, and Sibiya, startled, rushed to him and supported him.

"Phew~ I barely made it. From now on, I'll have to wear armor even when I meet you."

Nergal said, panting and smiling at Sibiya. However, there was no trace of ease in his smile.

"Nergal. Let's go home first. You're wounded."

Sibiya spoke worriedly, looking at his wounds. A lot of blood was flowing from his arm, and he had a cut on his waist that he was pressing with his hand. However, unlike his earlier smile, Nergal resolutely shook off Sibiya's hand and staggered down the street.

"No. There's no time."

"What are you talking about? No time?"

Sibiya supported Nergal again.

"I need to tell Princess Sera what you told me. Before danger strikes. And you, hide yourself for a while."

"You said you'd tell the General tomorrow."

"Don't be naive. It's no use. Anania holds all the real power in the royal palace."

As Nergal, staggering, turned into the alley, his horse was there. Nergal laboriously hoisted himself onto the horse.

"But how did you know that man was chasing me?"

"That's because you screamed."

"I didn't scream."

"............"

Nergal did not answer.

"You. You knew, didn't you? That man would come..."

Sibiya asked Nergal again, but Nergal still avoided answering.

"I have to go now. I need to inform the Princess quickly. I may be your boyfriend, but I'm also one of the Royal Guards of this palace. I have to work for the country. And you, go home, pack your bags immediately, and hide. Understood?"

"If you don't answer, you can't go."

Sibiya blocked the horse's path. Nergal stared intently into Sibiya's eyes for a moment. In her eyes, reflecting the moonlight, he could read a certain resolve.

"Alright. I'll tell you. If what you said earlier is true, Anania couldn't possibly not know what you overheard. Then, of course, you'd be in danger."

"Then why didn't you tell me earlier? That Anania would try to kill me."

"In case you felt guilty."

"About what?"

"............"

Nergal did not answer again. Only then did a thought strike Sibiya.

Nergal was involved in this because of her, and Nergal's life was also in danger. Although he had saved Sibiya once, he was still putting himself in harm's way. If he were to go to Princess Sera, the one whose life would be most at risk was Nergal himself.

As that thought came to her, Sibiya couldn't hide her dismay.

"I've said all I need to say, so move aside."

"Oh, you fool. Then all the more reason I can't let you go. I'm coming too."

"Don't talk nonsense. It's too dangerous for you to go. You just hide and then escape the castle."

"If you don't take me, you won't take a single step from here."

Sibiya spread her arms wide, completely blocking Nergal's path.

Just then, the sound of people was heard. Someone was coming. Amidst the sounds of people, there was the metallic clang of heavy armor and swords clashing. Soldiers were approaching.

"Damn. No choice then. Get on."

Nergal pulled Sibiya onto the horse in front of him, as if embracing her, and spurred the horse on.

"Hya! Let's go!"

"There he is! Chase him!"

The soldiers spotted Nergal and shouted. Nergal, evading the soldiers, galloped towards the castle gate like an arrow. Nergal was riding through the dark night streets, and Anania was watching the situation from the castle wall above the gate.

"Damn. One of the King's Royal Guards is causing trouble."

"Archers!"

The archer unit of Anania's Royal Guard drew their bowstrings. As Nergal approached the castle gate, arrows flew with a whooshing sound. Nergal spotted the arrows, drew his sword, and deflected them.

"Kyaak!"

An arrow grazed Sibiya's arm.

"Sibiya! Are you alright?"

Nergal looked at Sibiya's arm. The grazed area began to swell as if it had been burned black. Nergal quickly turned the horse away from the castle gate and disappeared into the streets. On the galloping horse, Nergal tore his clothes and tightly bound the area above Sibiya's wound.

"You'll be alright, Sibiya."

Nergal comforted Sibiya, who was trembling with fear.

"Alright! Let's go again!"

Nergal turned the horse back towards the castle gate and spurred it on. As Nergal reappeared before the gate, Anania gave an order.

"Raise the drawbridge!"

As Anania's command was given, soldiers began to laboriously crank the wheels to raise the drawbridge.

"What do we do? The drawbridge is going up."

Sibiya said, sounding anxious.

"Don't worry. Hya!"

Nergal increased the horse's speed. As he approached the castle gate, the archers on the wall above drew their bowstrings again.

"This time, make him a hedgehog! Fire!"

As soon as Anania's words fell, arrows from the skilled archers sprang from their bows.

"They're coming!"

'Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!'

However, Nergal did not deflect the arrows with his sword; instead, he tightly embraced Sibiya. Sibiya was helpless in the face of Nergal's sudden action. The drawbridge was halfway up, but Nergal's horse powerfully leaped onto the drawbridge.

"Kyaak!"

Sibiya screamed, and the horse, flying through the air for a moment, cleared the moat and landed on the ground outside the castle gate.

"Nergal! I can't breathe."

Sibiya called out to Nergal because he was hugging her so tightly she felt suffocated, but he didn't answer and continued to ride, holding her close.

"We... we made it. Whoa... whoa..."

Nergal finally stopped the horse when they reached a narrow path in the forest outside the castle, where the castle was visible. Nergal, who had been embracing Sibiya, finally straightened up, and Sibiya was able to pull herself out of his arms.

"You... what did you do?"

Sibiya looked at Nergal and was shocked. His body was covered in blood, and arrows were stuck in his back.

"I... I couldn't have broken through the gate otherwise."

"But not like this..."

"At least one person has to go to the Princess and tell her the truth. I'm a Royal Guard, I made an oath. From the moment I gained this honor, my life... for the country... I'd gladly... *gasp*..."

Nergal was smiling, but he looked to be in great pain. In the distance, the drawbridge was lowering again, and soldiers could be seen approaching.

"They're still chasing us."

Nergal placed the reins in Sibiya's hand. Then he gave Sibiya a smile. As Sibiya was wondering why he was acting this way, Nergal unexpectedly gave her a deep kiss. Sibiya was startled. It was her first kiss. Although she and Nergal were dating, she had never allowed a kiss before.

"I always wanted to do that someday. I guess I'm not a good man."

Nergal smiled, tossed out that one line, and then jumped off the horse. He then slapped the horse's flank with his palm. The horse, startled, began to gallop away, and Sibiya, surprised, grabbed the reins and crouched low. From behind Sibiya, Nergal's clear voice rang out.

"Sibiya! Make sure to tell the Princess! And the arrow that hit you is poisoned. Get treated first when you get there!"

Sibiya collected herself and looked back

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode 38 - The Girl with Power
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
In a small village where the sun was setting, a group of children were playing. The village was where the Dark Tribes lived, hidden in the mountains. Just by looking at the children playing, it was hard to tell that they were from the Dark Tribes. After the Ruba tribe lost the war to Eldge, the lifestyle of the Dark Tribes became very similar to that of those from the Angara Kingdom. The war left behind resentment, but it also had both large and small influences on both sides. The Dark Tribes adopted methods of acknowledging human emotions to some extent, and the people who served the light became stricter about sin and its consequences. However, the perception of the Dark Tribes, the losers, was still not good, and one of the main reasons for this was their exclusiveness. The idea of being chosen, that only the Dark Tribes, children of the Dark God who governs the night, were chosen, was one of the reasons they were looked down upon by the people of light, but it was also the only thread that allowed them to endure persecution.

A small girl was peeking out from behind a shed, watching the children play. The children were drawing on the ground and throwing stones, and the girl was watching them enviously. Then, one of the boys playing suddenly noticed the girl's gaze.
"What! What are you looking at, you crippled girl!"
The boy suddenly huffed and ran towards the girl, pushing her and shouting. The girl, looking as if she was about to cry, couldn't say anything and limped away from them to another spot.
"Islia! Islia!"
The girl soon heard her name being called and looked in the direction of the sound. The plump woman who was taking care of Islia was glaring at her with scary eyes.
"Come and eat quickly!"
Islia slowly walked with weak steps towards where she was called.
"If it weren't for Rice... Tsk."
The woman looked at Islia with contempt. After dinner, Islia quietly got up, checking the woman's mood, and went outside. She wanted to avoid any conflict as much as possible, as it was clear she would be beaten if her actions bothered the woman even a little.

The wide rock on the hill behind the village was always Islia's go-to spot. Islia lay on the rock and looked up at the sky. Before she knew it, the sky had turned from deep purple to dark indigo, and stars were beginning to appear one by one.
"Brother..."
Islia looked at the stars in the sky and thought of Rice's face. She missed the reliable Rice, who would always approach her kindly and talk to her whenever she was like this, as if he knew. But Rice wasn't here. All around her were eyes that ignored and scorned her. At some point, Islia's limp in one leg had worsened, and her silence deepened even further.

Islia suddenly heard a rustling sound from the forest. She got up at the sound and looked in the direction it came from. Islia, who had good night vision, saw something white huddled there. It was a rabbit. The pure white rabbit seemed unusually bright against the dark forest shadows, and its eyes sparkled black.
"Come here..."
Islia extended her hand and whispered for the rabbit to come. But the rabbit startled and began to run away. Islia then, without thinking, used her power on the rabbit. The rabbit's body seemed to float for a moment, then with a thud, it fell into the grass, spilling red blood from its side. The rabbit, bleeding from its side, just blinked its black eyes, not knowing what had happened.
"Ah... I didn't mean to..."
Islia mumbled, stepping back.
"I'm sorry... I'm sorry..."
Islia took a step or two forward again and approached the rabbit. Islia stroked the rabbit.
"I'm sorry... I'm sorry..."
Suddenly, Islia picked up the rabbit with both hands.
"But, you... you... you made me..."
Emotionally agitated, Islia threw the rabbit with all her might.
"I hate you! You hated me! Just like everyone else!"
Just before the rabbit's body hit the ground, Islia raised her head and glared at it.
'Thump'
The rabbit's body shattered into pieces and scattered on the ground. Islia looked at her hands. There were traces of the rabbit's blood.
'Everyone hates me...'
Islia stood there and let out a scream.
'Whoosh!'
Suddenly, the wind blew, and everything within a few steps of Islia shattered. Islia collapsed in the middle of it. And without a word, she stared at her blood-stained hands with unfocused eyes.

The ostracism and loneliness around her had become unbearable for young Islia. Islia thought about using her power to kill everyone. Then she shook her head vigorously and looked again at the mess she had made. Trees were broken, and even part of the rock she had been sitting on was shattered. The rabbit's corpse was so broken that it was no longer visible.
She trembled with fear at herself for having had murderous intent, even for a moment, and at what she had done.
"Now... I really hate it..."
Islia's tears fell one by one onto the thick red blood on her hands.

Islia was afraid to go in while the woman was awake, so she slowly got up late at night and returned to the house where she was being cared for. However, the woman was waiting for Islia as if she had been biding her time.
"You wicked girl. What were you doing out so late! And what's that on your hands! Covered in blood!"
The woman taking care of her shrieked fiercely. Islia just stared at the woman.
