"Look at that girl. How dare you glare at an adult!"
"I wasn't glaring..."
Islia replied in a barely audible voice. The woman approached Islia and slapped her cheek. Islia was pushed back by the woman's force and fell. Islia clenched her fists. She wanted to unleash her anger on the woman. Islia knew well what would happen if she did. She wanted to turn the woman into the same state as that rabbit.
Then, suddenly, Rice's face, telling her not to use her power recklessly, came to mind. And the fear that she would truly be driven out of this village if she did that to the woman took precedence. No matter how much she hated the villagers, she didn't have the confidence to live alone.
'Sob, sob.'
Islia knelt down and cried.
"Tsk! I told you, you're an unlucky girl, anyway."
The woman spat in front of Islia with a contemptuous expression. All Islia could do was suppress her terrifying power and shed tears as sadness overwhelmed her.

In a small tavern in Imra Port, Laodicea's only trading port, a group of travelers sat chatting. One woman and two men. It was Aaron's party, but Elon and Sera were not visible.
"So, you see. If I do this with this object. Look!"
Under Dagmon's hand, a stick floated in the air. The stick floated in the air and moved as Dagmon's finger directed it.
"Wow~ What kind of magic is that? Was Dagmon a wizard too? It looks like Dillon's, but I don't feel any magical energy at all. It's really amazing."
Lisia asked, amazed.
Dagmon grabbed the stick in the air with his hand and said,
"Secret."
"That's not fair."
"If I teach you a magic trick, how is it still a magic trick?"
"A magic trick? Not magic?"
Then Aaron interjected.
"In other words, it's a trick."
"A trick?"
Lisia asked, puzzled by the remark.
"Look closely at the end of the stick."
"Hehe. Aaron caught me."
Lisia snatched the stick from Dagmon and looked at it.
"What is this? It's a thin thread?"
"But, they say there are people who can really do it like me. People who can move objects like this with their mind."
"There are such people?"
"They're usually called psychics. No one knows the source of their power."
"I've traveled a lot, but I doubt such a thing exists."
Aaron said, as if he didn't believe it.
"I'm telling you, they do. I really saw them."
"No way."
Then a man's voice was heard.
"Well. Why don't you believe him, Aaron?"
Sera and Elon appeared before them, shaking off their rain-soaked cloaks, and Elon immediately told the doubting Aaron to believe Dagmon's words.
"How can you tell me to believe or not believe something you don't even know? Without even hearing the story before."
"Whatever it is. Prince Dagmon's words are trustworthy."
Elon said with a shrug.
"Did you buy enough food?"
Dagmon asked.
"Plenty."
Elon replied.
"What are you going to do now?"
Aaron asked again.
"What do you mean?"
Sera asked.
"This is the country of Ceres, so it doesn't matter if we part ways now, does it?"
"Tsk. So you're saying you don't want to see us anymore, after all."
Sera sneered, displeased. Then Dagmon interjected.
"Aaron. As I told you last time, I'd like to investigate the incident of the young prince of Ceres being killed."
"Who told you to investigate that!"
Sera snapped, shouting.
"Dagmon's actions are Dagmon's business. Not Sera's, right? Dagmon is the only one who witnessed that incident, after all."
When Aaron took Dagmon's side, Sera turned her head in anger.
"Since we're going to find the ruins of light anyway. First, I'll go to the village where the prince was attacked before."
"My brother has a name too, don't keep calling him 'that prince, that prince.' His name is Esther!"
Sera shouted, displeased.
"Esther? Sounds like a girl's name. Hehe."
When Aaron chuckled after hearing the name, Sera flared up again.
"What did you say!"
"Tsk. Anyway, it doesn't matter. I'll go my own way now."
As Sera was about to go outside, Elon stopped her.
"Princess. How can you leave the prince's matter to strangers?"

Should we only leave it to them? We have to find the culprit anyway, don't we?"
"What? So you're telling me to keep following these idiots?"
"Wouldn't that be for the best?"
"I refuse!" Sera said flatly.
"Princess!"
"Since when did Elron start defying my words like that?"
"If you intend to avenge the Prince, I believe that is the best method."
Sera couldn't find a reply to those words.
"You're right, Elron. I'm sorry. It's right to do as you say."
Sera easily gave in. Elron was surprised that Sera had given in so easily and asked again.
"Are you sure, Princess?"
"You're the one who suggested it, Elron. Why are you asking again?"
Sera replied coolly, as if she had made up her mind. Then Aron stood up and asked Dagmon.
"Alright, shall we set off now? What was the name of the village again?"
"It's Enrogel Village to the northeast. You should be able to reach it easily by following the central highway."
"Enrogel isn't far from the capital, Brugia Castle, then. We might be able to stop by the castle and get some troops." Elron replied.
"I... even so, Brugia is a bit..."
Dagmon replied, hesitant to enter the capital as a prince of an enemy nation.
"I will guarantee the Prince's safety."
Elron spoke as if to tell him not to worry, and Aron grumbled again.
"Near Brugia Castle... isn't that near where those well-fed, warm-backed folks live? I'm not really keen on it."
Licia, who had been looking outside, lifted her luggage and shouted.
"Aron, stop complaining! I don't hear the rain outside, so it seems to have stopped. Let's go!"
They gathered their belongings and left the tavern. The road, just after the rain had stopped, was wet and muddy, and only a few children could be seen splashing around happily. The streets, befitting a trading port, were bustling with people buying and selling goods, and their merchandise overflowed.
"Wait a minute. It's too heavy! Can't someone help me with my luggage?"
Licia grunted under her load and shouted to the group.
"Shouldn't you carry your own food?" Aron snapped at Licia.
"Elron."
When Sera called Elron's name, Elron immediately went to Licia and took her luggage.
"Thanks, Elron. Aron has terrible manners."
Licia stuck out her tongue at Aron.
"So childish... How old are you?" Aron mumbled. Licia, holding her slightly lighter luggage, was about to catch up with the group when she suddenly felt someone watching her and looked back. Licia looked towards a dark alley. She stared intently due to the strange feeling, but only the shadows of the alley were visible; there was no one there. Just then, Shaga flew in from somewhere, as if worried Licia would fall behind the group, and urged her on.
"Ah, I get it, Shaga. I'm going."
'That's strange...'
Licia looked forward again and splashed her way towards the group, who had moved a little further ahead.
"Elron even took your luggage, so why are you so slow?" Aron asked.
"I don't know." Licia replied curtly, as if sulking at Aron, and walked ahead of him.
"If you're leading, do you even know the way?"
Licia, with a pouting expression, stood behind Aron again. Then Dagmon smiled and showed Licia the way.
"It's not that difficult; you just need to follow the main road."
Licia stood in front of Aron again.

Aaron and Lishia were on the deck of the Hebel, enjoying the sunshine. Lishia rested her chin on the railing, gazing at the sea, while Aaron sat on the railing beside her, sharpening his dagger with a small charcoal stone.
"Ugh, this is boring. Are we still far?"
Lishia, who had been on the ship for several days already, leaned against the Hebel's railing, looking like a bored cat.
"I'm sick of this horizon now~"
"One more day, and we should be there."
Aaron replied, fiddling with the blade of his dagger.
"The sea is so vast. I can't even tell if the Hebel is moving or not. It never changes, you know."
"The sea changes."
"What do you mean? The sea changes? It's always the same like this?"
"Depending on the weather... it's terrifying when a storm hits."
"Heh~ Is that so?"
Lishia replied as if she had just learned something new.
"Who doesn't know that?"
Aaron chided her. Lishia, feeling offended, retorted.
"Hmph. It's understandable if you're seeing the sea for the first time. Such a show-off. But is there anything Aaron is scared of?"
"Is there anyone who isn't scared of anything? All done."
Aaron answered, sheathing his dagger, then clasped his hands behind his neck and looked up at the sky. A clear, blue sky filled Aaron's vision.
"Huh?"
He felt a hand grab his knee as he sat on the railing. Aaron identified the owner of the hand. It was Lishia. Lishia looked at Aaron and smiled sweetly. As Aaron wondered, an ominous thought crossed his mind.
"Ah!"
Lishia suddenly shook Aaron. Aaron barely managed to keep his balance, narrowly avoiding falling off the railing. Lishia giggled, finding his struggle amusing.
Aaron, fearing Lishia would play another prank, stepped down to the deck and said,
"You're what I'm most afraid of."
'Bang!'
Just then, an incredibly loud noise suddenly echoed from one side of the ship.
"What was that sound? Let's go see."
Lishia pulled Aaron along.
People were murmuring and gathering. Lishia pushed through the crowd to see what was happening. In the middle of the gathered people stood the merchant who had sold Lishia the brooch, looking flustered.
"Oh, it's nothing. Please, move along."
"Why is he acting like that?"
Aaron also pushed through the crowd and stood next to Lishia. The merchant was hiding something behind him. Just then, Sigron, the captain of the Hebel, arrived, huffing and puffing.
"What's all this commotion about?"
"Oh. It's nothing."
"Hey! What's this! The deck is broken!"
A part of the ship's floor was broken. Around it, there were clear traces of something having burned.
"I apologize. I will pay for it."
The merchant was carrying a long box, and one corner of the box was broken, just like the deck floor. Despite its size, which made it impossible to hide, the merchant's attempt to conceal it looked comical.
People soon lost interest and dispersed. Only Lishia remained, crouching by the broken deck, staring at the damaged spot.
"It's magic."
Lishia said.
"What?"
"It's magic. It was broken by magic. Fire-type, I think?"
"So, was that merchant a wizard?"
Aaron mumbled indifferently, looking elsewhere, as if uninterested. When Aaron looked at Lishia again, she was running off somewhere. Behind her, a bird-like creature swiftly descended from the mast and chased after her. It was Shaga, Lishia's small dragon.
"Huh? Lishia! She's really incorrigible..."
'By the way, Shaga was on this ship too. Haven't seen him in a while... Well, he's always around Lishia, so...'
Lishia peeked into various cabins, searching for something. Then, she peered into one cabin, seemed to find something, threw the door wide open, and entered the cabin.
"Mister!"
The merchant, who was inside resting and drinking tea, was startled and spilled hot tea on his hand.
"Ouch, hot! Young lady, why did you come in so suddenly!"
The merchant exclaimed, wiping the tea from his hand, clearly annoyed.
"Oh. You're the young lady who bought the brooch before. Is something wrong?"
"No. That brooch is so pretty. And cheap."
Lishia was so naive that she truly believed it was sold at that price.
"Did you use magic, mister?"
Lishia smiled and suddenly asked. The merchant was startled, as if caught red-handed.
"Why are you so surprised?"
"Uh... that is..."
"I'm a wizard too, you know. I can tell when something's been broken by magic."
The merchant was so surprised by Lishia's sudden actions that he couldn't say anything.
"What happened?"
"Well..."
"Then, I'll go tell everyone that it was broken by magic."
The merchant looked even more flustered. Then, as if making up his mind, he said,
"I'm only telling you because you're a wizard, and you seem like a good person, young lady."
The merchant pulled out a long wooden box, broken at one end. Just then, Shaga entered through the open cabin door and perched on Lishia's shoulder.
"Oh. Is that? A dragon, isn't it, young lady?"
"He's my friend."
"It's small, but it really looks just like a dragon. How fascinating. How much did you pay for it?"
"He's my friend!"
Lishia flared up at the merchant, who seemed to quantify everything in terms of money.
"Oh. I apologize."
"But what's in that box?"
"This... this."
The merchant opened the wooden box. Inside was a staff. Made of jet-black wood, the staff was inscribed with ancient magical characters, and a blue gem was embedded in its tip.
"This is the one."
"Isn't that a magic staff?"
As Lishia reached out to touch it, the merchant stopped her.
"Ah. No, don't touch it. You'll get hurt."
"What do you mean?"
"This staff clearly possesses very strong magical power, but there's no one who can wield it."
"What do you mean?"
"So far, no wizard has been able to use this staff. They get burned when they touch it, for example..."
Shaga circled around, then saw the staff and growled, making strange noises. Then, the stone at the tip of the staff glowed blue.
"Eek! Get down, young lady!"
The merchant, startled, ducked down. Lishia also instinctively ducked. The next moment, with a 'whoosh' sound, a blue light burst forth and struck Shaga. Shaga was slammed into the ceiling by the impact of the magic. The next moment, Shaga, not to be outdone, swiftly flew down and breathed fire at the blue stone of the staff. Blue light again emanated from the staff, but this time Shaga dodged it. Shaga flew back to the staff and breathed fire again.
"What are you doing! Stop that animal! You'll damage the expensive staff!"
The merchant shouted in alarm.
"Shaga! Stop it!"
Lishia yelled in an angry voice. Shaga was flapping his wings in the air, huffing.
"Is it over now?"
The merchant stood up again.
"What happened?"
"That thing sometimes unleashes its power on its own like that. But this time it was weak magic, thankfully. Sometimes it emits immense magical power. It's very dangerous. That animal was lucky."
"Shaga. Come here."
When Lishia called Shaga's name, Shaga perched on Lishia's shoulder.
"You blockhead. Is that how you take out your anger on a staff?"
Lishia said, giving Shaga a light punch.
"Thanks for showing me. But why are you hiding it?"
"It's quite valuable, so many people are after it."
"Can I touch it?"
"I told you, didn't I? You'll get hurt. Especially if you're someone with magical power, it could be even more serious."
"Is that so?"
Lishia mumbled regretfully.
"Huh? That's strange. The ship isn't moving."
Suddenly, the regular rocking of the ship was completely gone.
"Shall we go out?"
Lishia stepped out of the cabin. The merchant also slung the wooden box over his shoulder and followed Lishia.
"Why are you carrying that out?"
"I have to have it with me; it puts my mind at ease. If people knew its value, there would be plenty on this ship who would try to steal it."
Outside, several people, also sensing something strange, were looking down at the sea. The sea was incredibly calm. Like a lake... Aaron and Umma were seen together. Lishia ran to Aaron and asked,
"What happened?"
Umma spoke with a serious tone.
"There are no waves, no wind. In this state, the ship won't move in any direction."
"Then what should we do?"
Lishia asked.
"We'll have to wait for days, for however long it takes for the wind or waves to blow. Until this weather witch leaves."
"Weather witch? That's an interesting expression."
"When you get stuck on a day like this, they say you've been caught by the weather witch."
"I see..."
Lishia ran to the railing and leaned against it tightly.
"Look at that. It's so calm that you can see the green seabed."
"You seem to be in a good mood despite the situation."
Aaron looked at Lishia with a look of exasperation.
Just then, on one side of the sea, water surged upwards with a 'whoosh' sound, like a dragon rising into the sky. Of course, there was still no wind, and the day was clear. Dagmon, seeing the sight, mumbled as if it were strange.
"No wind, yet a waterspout."
The column of water slowly began to approach the Helon.
"What is it?"
Some people on the deck screamed and ran into the cabins in surprise, while others just stared in wonder.
"Captain. Can't you move this ship?"
Dagmon asked Sigron.
"No. Not at all."
"It would be terrible if that waterspout came here."
"I've never seen anything like this in my life. Anyway, strange things always happen whenever Aaron is on board."
The column of water truly approached the Helon as if targeting it. However, it stopped a few meters away from the Helon. Suddenly, the column of water split with a 'whoosh,' and a person emerged from within. The person had dark gray hair, a stout build, and a face full of wrinkles, indicating she was quite old. As soon as she appeared, she suddenly threw back her stout body and began to cackle. Her appearance, as if standing on a large fountain, made one think less of fear than

It made him feel that something was strange.
“What? Who is that woman? Why is she laughing like a madwoman the moment she appears?”
Aron muttered. Suddenly, she stopped laughing and asked a question.
“Who is the Champion of Light?”
She asked, floating in the air.
“Looking for me again, huh… Tsk.”
Aron felt a headache coming on from the all-too-familiar situation.
“Is no one coming out? In that case.”
Her wrinkled lips twitched with a thoughtful expression, then she raised one hand. With a 'Paat!' sound, a blue light formed in her hand. Then she hurled that light towards the Hellon.
“This should make them come out, right?”
“That’s magic. Damn it.”
Without a second thought, Aron had to prevent that magic from hitting the Hellon. The Hellon wouldn't be completely destroyed, but if a large hole were to be accidentally blown in the ship, it would be a disaster. But just as Aron thought it was already too late for him to act,
the exact same magic flew in from somewhere, collided with a loud bang, and exploded in mid-air.
“Who was that?”
Aron looked in the direction the magic had come from. In that direction, only the merchant from before was huddled close to the deck, carrying a wooden box.
“Are you the Champion of Light?”
She pointed at the merchant. The merchant was greatly surprised to see himself being pointed at. She channeled her magic again. The merchant, startled, threw his box aside and dodged. With a 'Kwaang!' sound, the part of the deck where he had been was shattered, and the discarded box broke open, revealing a magic staff that rolled out haphazardly.
Seeing this, she clicked her tongue, her gray hair fluttering like a madwoman's.
“So the Champion of Light is nothing more than that… How disappointing. I’ll just finish you off along with the ship.”
In her hand, a blue light formed, incomparably larger than before. Following the 'Paat!' sound of magic being cast, the magical energy flew towards the merchant. Aron quickly blocked the merchant, deflecting the magic with his sword energy.
“You’re quite capable. Are you the one? The so-called Champion of Light?”
“What in the world are you doing?!”
“I was merely asked to kill the Champion of Light. Killing someone or sinking a ship is a delightful task. Hohoho.”
“What?!”
“Try to block this too!”
She channeled her magic again. Aron blocked that magic as well, then pointed his sword straight at her and shouted.
“Urr!”
With a 'Hwarr!' sound, flames shot out towards her, who was floating on a pillar of water.
“Ugh.”
She barely dodged, her expression one of panic, not the relaxed one from before. But there was more. Aron was firing multiple shots in quick succession. Her old, plump body seemed to struggle to move. It was clear she wasn't skilled at dodging. Moreover, it wasn't just Aron; Elron had now joined the fray. Soon, one shot hit her in mid-air.
“Aaaargh!”
She screamed in agony from the flames. But soon, she vanished into the water pillar, extinguishing the fire on her body.
“You brats! I won’t go easy on you now!”
“Go on, try it!”
Aron shouted and fired magic at her again.
“Buwa!”
As her eyes twitched and she chanted a spell, a tremendous wind blew. The magic Aron had fired was being blown back by the wind.
“Shiryon!”
With a 'Kwaang!' sound, the magic Aron had fired collided with a defensive spell and exploded in front of Aron.
“Ugh.”
It seemed Aron hadn't completely blocked it with his defensive magic. This time, Dagmon also joined in, firing a crossbow bolt, but she easily blocked his shot by creating a wall of water. She then climbed back onto the water pillar and chanted a spell with a terrifying expression.
“Shihon!”
When she chanted the spell again, Aron tensed, but nothing happened. However, clouds suddenly began to gather.
“Are you playing petty tricks?!”
“Don’t be so impatient; just wait a little. Hohoho.”
The old gray-haired woman replied with an unpleasant laugh, and soon dark clouds completely covered the sky, and the wind began to intensify.
“It seems like weather magic.”
Lishia said in an unusual voice, looking around. As the wind intensified, the Hebel began to sway, people grabbed onto the ship's structures, and unsecured cargo started rolling around.
Before long, the wind turned into a storm. Even the remaining people on deck hastily went into the cabins, leaving only Aron's group and the sailors needed to operate the ship on deck. The sailors began to struggle to right the ship, which seemed on the verge of sinking due to the wind, and Shikgron and Umma held onto the helm, shouting at them.
“Aron! Do something about that witch!”
Aron's group, too, was barely standing, clinging to the ship's structures.
“How do you like that, you brats! Hohohoho!”
The old gray-haired woman laughed confidently.
“That hag really is a weather witch, isn't she? Or should I say, a weather madwoman?”
Dagmon even joked amidst all this. Elron then said with a troubled expression.
“You’re still making jokes at a time like this? You’re wrong. Fighting a hag like that on a ship is impossible.”
Looking at the waves that seemed ready to swallow the ship at any moment, Aron said in a despondent voice.
“What do we do now? Is there no choice but to willingly give up my life for everyone?”
“That’s absurd!”
Lishia vehemently objected, horrified.
“She doesn’t seem like the kind of woman who would just let us go if one person sacrificed their life.”
Dagmon added with an incredulous expression, looking at the woman laughing like a madwoman in the storm.
“Then what do we do? If only Master Elleasar were here…”
Aron tried to think, but no good solution came to mind.
“Well… I don’t know either…”
Dagmon also seemed to be thinking hard, but couldn't come up with a good answer. Aron's group was helpless, the ship's rocking grew wilder like a madwoman's jump rope, and only the sailors were fighting against the weather witch's magic to right the ship.

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode 3
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
Aaron's group was on a ship that had departed from the port of Nigoboli, heading for Imra Port in the Seres Kingdom. The weather was clear, perfect for sailing, and the ship was cutting through the waves powerfully with a tailwind, advancing across the sea. Aaron had already started a drinking party on the ship's deck.
"Hey! Lysia! Let's have a drink!"
"What?! I'm underage!"
Lysia, leaning against the ship's railing, turned away from Aaron, looking displeased, and stared at the sea. Then she yelled at Aaron and looked back down at the sea.
"Tch. He's just in a good mood, but I'm so seasick... Ugh."
"What's going on? With Aaron?"
Dagmon approached Lysia and asked.
"Oh, he said it's an old friend or something."
"Who?"
"Sigron, the captain of this Hebel ship?"
"No. His son, Umma."
"He must be happy to see him after a long time."
"Happy? What's happy about it? I'm dizzy, and my stomach feels queasy."
"There's no cure for seasickness. You just have to wait until it passes."
"Still. This is... Ugh."
Lysia dry-heaved into the sea.
"Shall I pat your back?"
"No, it's fine. I haven't eaten anything anyway. I wish Aaron was more like Dagmon."
Dagmon just smiled at that answer.
"Um... Dagmon."
Someone spoke to Dagmon. Sera had approached at some point. Sera stood awkwardly, eyes cast down like a child about to be scolded.
"What is it?"
Dagmon asked, finding Sera's behavior strange.
"Because of Elon's scolding..."
Sera still answered reluctantly.
"What do you mean?"
Dagmon asked again, not understanding. Lysia also looked at Sera's face. Her white face, visible through her blonde hair, was as red as a beet. Lysia was more interested in Sera than in the seasickness that plagued her. Lysia cautiously observed Sera.
"Elon said..... I was wrong........"
"Huh?"
Dagmon, still not understanding Sera's sudden behavior, asked again.
"I was wrong all this time! Misunderstanding and all that!"
With that shout, Sera, her long blonde hair flying, stomped and ran down the ship's ladder to below deck.
"Pfft."
Lysia covered her mouth to stifle a laugh.
"Why did Princess Sera say that? Did I just receive an apology?"
Dagmon asked, puzzled by Sera's actions.
"She doesn't seem used to apologizing."
Lysia turned back, leaned against the railing, closed her eyes, and said.
"Huh?"
"Princess Sera, who is so proud, finally admitted her mistake to Prince Dagmon."
Lysia said that to Dagmon with a smile, then chased after Princess Sera, who had gone below deck.
Lysia opened the cabin door where Sera and Elon were and peeked her face in.
Inside, Sera was sitting on the bed, and Elon was standing, talking about something. Lysia called Sera.
"Princess Sera?"
Sera saw Lysia and, as if she had never been embarrassed, smiled and replied.
"Come in, Lysia. You're always welcome, Lysia."
Lysia entered the cabin.
"Your apology to Dagmon was well done."
"Just call me Sera comfortably, like you do Prince Dagmon."
Sera smiled and treated Lysia casually.
"Lysia seems so comfortable."
"Am I not too young to call you Sera?"
"Then you be the younger sister. I'll be the older sister."
"That would be better. Sister Sera... How's that?"
"That sounds much better."
Sera smiled brightly.
"Why is Aaron so cold to me?"
"He lost his parents to a Seres Kingdom soldier. And he doesn't think highly of the country. That's why he treats Princess Sera that way."
"Oh dear. How did that happen?"
"His parents died because of Anania."
"That wicked woman..."
Sera clenched her fist upon hearing that name.
"Oh! You might know Aaron's parents!"
Lysia said, clapping her hands as if she had just remembered.
"Who are they?"
"Princess Bidia, General Helen's granddaughter, and Halhas, who was a general of the Seres Kingdom."
"What did you say?"
Elon, startled by those words, interjected.
"Aaron's parents were Lady Bidia and General Halhas?"
"Who are they, Elon?"
"According to my grandfather, they were people who disappeared from Seres Castle when this war broke out. They were the ones who opposed this war until the very end. So, Lady Bidia would be Princess Sera's aunt. And General Halhas was even the commander-in-chief of the Seres Kingdom. To think that such people were Aaron's parents... I can't believe it. That stubborn fellow."
"Then, Aaron and I are cousins?"
Sera exclaimed in surprise.
"That's how it is."
"What? That guy? He has royal blood in him too, so who is he taking his anger out on?! I'll get him!"
Sera got excited upon hearing that. Then she jumped up and ran out, saying she would go to Aaron.
"Sister! Wait a minute!"
Before Lysia could even finish her sentence, Sera ran outside.
"He really does seem like Aaron's cousin..."
Lysia mumbled and followed Sera.
Outside, it was already night, and small lanterns hanging on the ship illuminated the ship and the sea. Aaron was thoroughly drunk.
"Cheers!"
Aaron clinked glasses with Umma.
"You're a great drinker. To be able to drink with a sailor like me."
"Alcohol is essential for a traveler!"
Aaron replied heartily.
"Hey! Aaron!"
Aaron heard his name being called and looked in the direction of the sound. Sera's figure, illuminated by the small lanterns of the night, was glaring down at Aaron, huffing.
"Oh? What? It's Princess Sera? Want to drink with us?"
Aaron mumbled with a slurred tongue, holding out a glass full of alcohol. There was still a hint of mockery in his voice. Umma tried to stop Aaron.
"Aaron. That's enough. What are you doing to the princess?"
"Tch. What... Look at how the world is going. The country is in this state, and what princess? Is being royalty everything? Ugh, dirty royal blood!"
Aaron spat on the ground as if disgusted.
"What?"
Sera, angered by Aaron's mocking demeanor, picked up a glass and splashed it on Aaron's face.
"Oh~ Look at this. Is it okay to do this just because you're a princess?"
Aaron, drenched in alcohol, mumbled in a drunken voice.
"How clean is your blood?! Wasn't Bidia royalty?"
As Sera shouted, Aaron's face instantly contorted.
"What?! You mentioned my mother's name!"
Aaron stood up abruptly. However, he was very drunk and seemed to have difficulty even standing steady.
"You wench!"
Umma quickly grabbed Aaron's arm.
"You're very drunk!"
"No, let go!"
Aaron shook off Umma with terrifying force. Umma had no choice but to fall back due to Aaron's immense strength.
"Damn princess! I'll kill you!"
Aaron swung his fist. But Aaron was very drunk. However, Sera was not so weak as to be defeated by a drunken Aaron. Sera dodged Aaron's swaying fist, grabbed his arm, and threw him into a corner of the ship where cargo was piled up. The cargo Aaron hit fell with a loud crash.
"What are you doing!"
Lysia, Elon, and even Dagmon rushed over, startled by the commotion, and others gathered to watch the scene. Aaron got up. But his body was still swaying violently. Suddenly, Aaron stared at Sera, then pointed a finger at her and chuckled.
"Look at that! That's a princess. Heh heh. One who easily throws a man... Hahaha! A princess who thinks she's the only great one in this foolish world! Hahaha!"
"You... really..."
Sera's lips trembled slightly, her fists clenched tight. Aaron's words were an unbearable humiliation and pain for Sera.
"Aaron!"
Lysia also shouted, as if she couldn't stand it anymore.
"Why, Lysia? I'm not drunk. I'm not drunk! I'm not drunk~ Hahahaha..."
Aaron laughed loudly, then for some reason, suddenly slumped down and continued to laugh. One or two drops of water began to fall from Aaron's shadowed face, which was bowed under the dim light of the lantern on the ship's ladder, wetting the deck. Soon, his hollow laughter gradually turned into sobs, and he began to cry loudly.
Sera watched Aaron for a moment, then turned away, covered her face, and ran down to below deck. Elon followed her. Sera ran into the cabin and locked the door.
"Princess! Princess!"
Elon knocked on the door and called Sera.
"Everyone, go! Just go away!"
Sera's cry was heard, and inside the cabin, Sera's faint sobs could be heard. Elon could do nothing more in front of the cabin. He could only stand there.
Aaron also continued to sit on the deck, crying loudly. Many people were looking at him, but the crying of a grown child, once started, did not stop easily. Lysia approached Aaron. Aaron stopped crying for a moment and looked at Lysia. Lysia's face, illuminated by the ship's dim light, was clearly angry as Aaron looked up at her.
"Lysia. Are you angry? Sometimes it's good to cry like this when you're traveling. When you feel depressed, you know."
The moment Aaron grinned and spoke with a slurred tongue, there was a 'smack' sound, and Lysia slapped Aaron hard on the cheek. That one slap from Lysia was enough to bring Aaron to his senses.
"Lysia..."
Aaron stared into Lysia's eyes. Lysia avoided Aaron's gaze, turned around, slowly walked through the gathered crowd, and went to the other side of the ship's railing. Aaron could do nothing but watch Lysia's retreating back.
Lysia leaned against the railing and looked at the sea.

She looked down. At its end was a dark blue sea.. a sea so black its end was unknown, and ceaseless waves rocked the Hebel. Lishia's dark hair fluttered in the sea breeze.
From her eyes, as she gazed down at the sea, something small and sparkling, like stars reflected in the sea, fell, and she uttered a single word in a voice so small only she could hear it.
“Aaron. You fool...”

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1, Episode
contentEn:
The torch Aaron was holding had already burned down quite a bit, and it grew dark. Dagmon, having discovered something, urgently called Aaron, so Aaron approached Dagmon. Dagmon was pressed close to the wall, examining something intently. On the wall he was pressed against, a square black hole was visible.
“What is it?”
“Look at that.”
“That’s...”
“There are animal carcasses laid out inside.”
In the wall was a small, window-like opening, barely large enough for a human head to pass through. The opening connected to another hall on the opposite side, where unknown animal carcasses lay neatly arranged.
“And, would you look at this?”
Dagmon knelt on one knee and pointed at the ground with his hand.
“These are footprints, aren’t they?”
“They’re not that old.”
“Then someone must have come in recently?”
“And those carcasses aren’t arranged randomly. It’s hard to see, but if you look closely, you can see lime powder sprinkled beneath them, right? They’re creating a magic circle. It seems they’re casting a spell for something.”
“Do you know what kind of spell it is?”
“Well, I don’t know anything about dark magic either...”
“Then wouldn’t it be better to destroy that circle and proceed? Especially if they’re doing something with dark magic.”
“Just because it’s dark magic doesn’t necessarily mean they’re doing evil. The tribes of darkness who hid in the mountains haven’t caused much trouble until now. More importantly, there’s no way for us to get in there right now. A rather strong barrier spell has been cast on this wall and window. It seems like if you apply a certain magic to this wall, it might open like a door, but breaking it would take a long time, even for a high-level mage.”
Aaron then said, as if resigned.
“In that case, there’s nothing we can do right now. The torch is almost out, so let’s go out and rethink this.”
“Yes. Unfortunately, we haven’t gained much for our efforts.”
Aaron and Dagmon began to head out of the cave again.
After walking for a while, something darted out of the darkness at incredible speed and crashed into Aaron. The object appeared so suddenly that Aaron didn't even have time to think about dodging, and he fell backward, landing on his bottom.
“Ouch. What was that?”
“Huh? Isn’t that Lishia?”
Dagmon exclaimed in surprise upon seeing the object that had rushed over.
“Lishia? You said you were scared. Why are you rushing in like this? And without a torch...”
Aaron said, dumbfounded. Lishia then cried out urgently, her voice on the verge of tears.
“Sob, sob, there’s something outside.”
Upon seeing Aaron and Dagmon, Lishia seemed to relax her tension and started crying again.
“Don’t cry, Lishia. Anyway, let’s go out and see.”
Aaron comforted Lishia, instinctively knowing that something was wrong outside. He drew his sword and took the lead, preparing for any eventuality. However, when Aaron and his companions emerged, there was nothing in front of the cave. Only the sky was heavily overcast with dark clouds, and the wind had grown strong, making the leaves rustle with an unsettling sound.
“What? There’s nothing here? What were you talking about? Were you just scared of the wind? Why were you so stubborn about not coming with us if you were scared?”
“It’s true! There really was something!”
Lishia cried out. Just then, Aaron also felt something.
“Wait a minute.”
As Aaron tensed up and drew attention to their surroundings, Lishia got scared again.
“Is there something?”
Dagmon asked Aaron. But Aaron didn't answer Dagmon's question; instead, he chanted an attack spell, and seeing this, Dagmon also drew his sword.
“Urr!”
Aaron unleashed the spell towards where he felt something strange. With a whooshing sound, the spot where Aaron cast the spell was engulfed in flames, and something pitch-black burst out from within the fire. The figure was human.
His clothes were entirely black. A long black cloak, and long hair that fell down his back, as black as pitch. However, in contrast, his face with its remarkably pale skin was impossible to miss. He stood lightly before the group, seemingly unharmed by Aaron's spell.
“Who are you!”
Aaron shouted. But instead of answering, he began to chant a low spell. Before Aaron's group could react, a loud sound was followed by an intense burst of heat around them. Yet, despite being caught off guard, no one in the group was harmed.
‘Whoa. That’s an incredible spell.’
“That was a return for the spell you cast, and a warning to you all.”
The black man’s voice was low.
“What? You black thing... so arrogant...”
Aaron provoked him.
“You talk big for someone who trespassed on another’s sacred ground! Do not defile this holy place.”
“Sacred ground? Are you talking about that cave?”
Aaron, understanding the reason for his anger, then changed his demeanor and asked again.
“Yes.”
“So there really are people who still serve darkness. What are those carcasses inside?”
“I have no obligation to tell you. If you wish to return alive, disappear now.”
He whistled, and large black wolves emerged, flanking him as if guarding him. They then began to snarl at Aaron’s group, ready to pounce at their master’s command.
“We merely came in search of the ruins of light.”
Aaron, somewhat intimidated by the large dogs’ ferocity, said in a slightly softened voice.
“This is a ruin of those who serve darkness. It is one of the few remaining ruins for us, whom you, who serve light, drove into the mountains. There is no ‘light something’ that you seek here. If you attempt to desecrate even this place, I will stop you, even if it costs my life.”
Dagmon then quickly defused the situation.
“Understood. It seems we misunderstood. We apologize if we were rude.”
Aaron also thought it best to avoid a meaningless fight with someone who wasn't a monster, in order to learn more about the dark ruins. He also judged that winning a fight against the dogs and the black man without any casualties would be impossible.
“We have no intention of fighting you. We haven’t desecrated the inside either. You merely appeared suddenly and cast a spell. If you remove those black dogs, we will simply withdraw.”
The black man whistled once more, and the black wolves stopped snarling and soon disappeared into the bushes.
“Get lost.”
Aaron and his companions left the spot as if fleeing.
“If we had destroyed the magic circle, we would have had to fight, no doubt. It’s a huge relief we didn’t break it. Luckily, he didn’t seem like a bad person.”
Dagmon replied, sounding relieved.
“But it didn’t feel good. The Dragon Elder once told me that Esbaal, a dark mage, was using dark magic to revive the dead and turn them into monsters. We came away because it was impossible to break the magic circle with our strength alone, but if it’s related to him, shouldn’t we have broken it before leaving?”
“What? You met the Dragon Elder?”
Dagmon asked, surprised.
“My sword master was also a dragon.”
“I understood that dragons don’t interfere with humans after the war, so it’s amazing that you met one, Aaron. You truly must be the legendary hero.”
Dagmon replied with admiration.
“Legendary hero, my foot. Thanks to that, I never have a day of peace. Do you think my stomach is lined with steel? It’s not like I can use incredible magic like an Archmage. Strange guys keep attacking me, calling me a hero or whatever, I wouldn’t have enough lives even if I had ten.”
“But the dragon acknowledged you, didn’t it?”
“Acknowledged, my ass... I couldn’t do anything when my master died. Could I have easily won if I fought that guy just now? There are many strong people in the world.”
“I also suspected that monsters were coming to life because of dark magic. But Esbaal... that’s the first I’ve heard of him.”
“The Dragon Elder told me to find the magic of light and fight him. And that’s my mission, and the only way to defeat him.”
“I see. So that was Aaron’s purpose. I know that light magic isn’t something just anyone can easily cast. And the fact that the dragonkin are involved means they’ve received some kind of oracle.”
“Forget about oracles and such. Wouldn’t it be possible for you to lead an army and capture the dark mage? Then I wouldn’t have to do this troublesome work, and the people wouldn’t be threatened by monsters, right?”
Dagmon then replied, thinking seriously.
“It might be possible. However, from the perspective of the Kingdom of Laodicea, monsters are not yet a military concern compared to the Kingdom of Ceres. Furthermore, we know too little about these enemies. My father would believe that if we withdraw troops from the front lines to subjugate monsters, the tense front with the Kingdom of Ceres would collapse. He knows it’s a problem, but he can’t act because he’s focused on the war. As things stand, I can only say it’s impossible.”
“But by the time they become a military threat, it might already be too late.”
“In that case, I need to get more information from Aaron. Only then can I get my father to act more quickly.”

Licia and Royce took shelter in a cave near Dabera Village, where they had previously sought refuge from the rain. Due to the attack on their group, they had to camp out again instead of staying at the village inn. They sat around a campfire in the cave, waiting for Aaron, and an awkward silence hung between them.

"Will Aaron be alright?" Royce broke the silence and asked Licia. But Licia still didn't answer. Royce gently looked at Licia's face. Licia was staring intently at the crackling campfire, her face filled with worry, almost on the verge of tears.

"Licia?" Royce asked.

"Huh?" Licia startled and finally seemed to snap out of it, answering.

"Are you worried about Aaron?"

"Why would I worry about that clumsy Aaron?" Licia turned her head sharply and replied primly. Royce felt a slight smile, but suppressed it, thinking it might be rude to Licia.

"By the way, who were those people who attacked us? They looked like soldiers. Aren't they the ones chasing Royce?" Licia asked.

"That... well, I don't really know why they're chasing me either."

Just then, someone's voice provided the answer.

"Who else? It's Sera, the princess of the Ceres Kingdom, and her escort knight, Elon." Licia immediately recognized the owner of the voice.

"Oh? Aaron?" Licia's face instantly brightened. Aaron entered the cave, his figure revealed by the campfire's light.

"Are you hurt again?" Licia fussed over Aaron's injured arm. Aaron plopped down next to the campfire.

"Thanks to you, we'll have to spend the night in a cave today. Right, Royce?" Licia felt a certain coldness in Aaron's voice.

"Yes." Royce replied with his usual smile.

"No, should I call you Dagmon? Prince Dagmon?" Aaron's voice was slightly agitated. Licia was surprised by Aaron's words. And a prince, no less...

"What are you talking about?"

"There's no one in the land of Dragonia who doesn't know Dagmon and Sera."

".........."

As if a huge secret had been exposed, Royce's face hardened, and he couldn't say a word.

"Dagmon, the youngest of King Laodicea's three sons. The prince most trusted by the king. However, burdened by his position, he left the palace to 'study the world' and has been on the run ever since. He was the only one of the three princes in Laodicea whom the people had hopes for, but because he's always running away, he's called the Cowardly Prince among the common folk.

Sera, the princess of the Ceres Kingdom. In a way, she's a pitiful woman. She's a princess in name only, with almost no power, all because of Anania. King Besse, who desires a son, is manipulated by the harlot sorceress Anania, and because of this, Sera decided to become a man from a young age and dresses like a tomboy. That's why her nickname among the people is the Tomboy Princess.

But when that tomboy princess turned 12, she had another younger brother. So that brother must have been like a jewel to her. Because he was the son her father wanted, and she must have thought he could neutralize Anania's power... However, that younger brother died when he was 5 years old. And she believes that Prince Dagmon of the Laodicea Kingdom killed her younger brother. That's why, ever since, Sera has been chasing Dagmon to avenge her brother. Most people in Dragonia know this much, but I never thought I'd see it firsthand. Wouldn't you agree, Your Royal Highness?"

"What? Then, Royce is Prince Dagmon?" Licia asked back, surprised.

"Prince, my foot. Would anyone even treat a prince of this kind of country with respect?" Aaron still grumbled in response. Royce, who had been silent, finally spoke.

"That's right. I am Dagmon."

Licia then said with a very surprised expression, "Then... ah... I should call you Your Royal Highness. I've been so rude all this time..." Licia's tone and attitude towards Dagmon had already changed.

"Hmph. I don't like either Laodicea or Ceres. My parents also died at the hands of soldiers. Moreover, their bloody cruelty, war... they suck the blood of the common people, and they're still shedding each other's blood."

"Ha. But I have nothing to do with that war." Dagmon said, as if making an excuse.

"A royal having nothing to do with war. Should I call you a truly cowardly prince? Or, as the rumors say, a timid prince? Then who is fighting this war!" Aaron stood up abruptly and shouted.

"Aaron. Stop it. Why are you so agitated?" Licia tried to calm Aaron.

"That is beyond my authority." But Dagmon's answer was brief.

"Hmph. Is it over if it's beyond your authority, irresponsibly? Do you wear the title of prince just for show?" Licia couldn't understand why Aaron was so agitated.

"Perhaps." Dagmon replied weakly, as if blaming himself.

"What do you plan to do by finding the magic of light? Annihilate the Ceres Kingdom with that power? And how many more common people will you kill in the process?"

"Don't talk like that! What do you know about me!" Dagmon finally couldn't take it anymore. He stood up abruptly, shouted, and ran out of the cave.

"Aaron! What on earth is wrong with you!" Licia screamed and chased after Dagmon, who had run out of the cave.

"Your Royal Highness! Your Royal Highness!" Licia searched the forest for Dagmon.

Dagmon was sitting on a rock in the not-too-distant forest. Licia slowly approached Dagmon, who was staring blankly at the star-studded night sky from the forest rock, as if it were about to pour down.

"Your Royal Highness. I'm sorry. Aaron's behavior..."

Dagmon glanced at Licia, who was standing behind him like a child being scolded. Then he spoke.

"Licia. Don't talk like that. Just call me Dagmon. If it's uncomfortable, you can call me Royce." Licia's face brightened, and she said,

"Can I really do that?"

"Of course, you've always done it that way..."

"Wow~ I'm so happy!" Licia plopped down next to Dagmon.

"What makes you so happy?"

"Is it common to be friends with a prince? I had no friends when I was little. Everyone shunned me because I was a sorcerer's daughter. But you're not just any friend, you're a prince. How proud is that? But you always use honorifics, don't you? Even to me, who's younger... No, it seems you use honorifics to almost everyone."

"Hehe. I'm happier to have a pretty friend like Licia." At the word "pretty," Licia's face turned red, even her ears.

"And everyone's attitude changes when they find out I'm a prince, but reactions like Aaron's or Licia's are actually uncommon. It's rather fortunate. The reason I use honorifics like this is simply because it's comfortable. An old man who taught me long ago said that if you change your way of speaking, your heart changes too. Even though I'm royalty, I disliked people who acted arrogant just because they were nobles."

"Were you upset because of Aaron?"

"No." Dagmon sighed, as if he couldn't help it.

"Aaron is right. I can't do anything. So many people are bleeding and dying, as numerous as the stars in the sky..."

"It's okay. It's not your fault, Dagmon."

"Have you been to a battlefield?" Dagmon asked abruptly, his voice laced with a sigh.

"No. I haven't."

"Then, have you seen the tragedies caused by war? No, perhaps you've already seen them. Dirsa's parents were also killed by soldiers, you said. And Aaron must have seen such things repeatedly. It's natural for him to speak that way."

"I grew up in one village since I was little. And my village disappeared because of monsters, not soldiers... But Aaron's village was apparently destroyed by the Ceres army. Perhaps that's why. Please understand Aaron." Dagmon's voice trailed off, and he continued.

"Understand him? I think the same way... Even now, many people are being driven to the battlefield. Death... there's only the shadow of death there. Nothing is meaningful, only life and death exist. People who laughed together suddenly die. Even though the Ceres Kingdom and the Laodicea Kingdom speak the same language, they have to kill each other. Death holds great meaning for ordinary people or individuals. But on the battlefield, it means nothing. Except that one person has died... No one grieves for him, no one prays for him. It's just something that always happens. What's important is how much land is taken. But I still don't know if that's really so important. However, someone who loved him will surely weep endlessly when they realize he's gone. And that's not all. War also causes suffering to many orphans like Dirsa... to children. The people are starving, losing their homes and loved ones, but this country is still waging war. My father and Besse don't seem to have any intention of a truce. It seems they won't stop until one side is dead and rotten." Dagmon's voice was calm and subdued.

"Dagmon, don't blame yourself too much. It's not something you can control with your power."

"Yet... I can't do anything for them. That's why... I hate it. That I can't do anything... They know that fact too. That's why I'm called the Cowardly Prince by the people."
"You're the third prince, aren't you? You have older brothers."
"My brothers? They are just fools who are only older. They don't try to see the people, only their own safety. Rather, they say they don't know. But I've always run away. Even when someone I loved was in danger, I ran."

"Anago even destroyed what he had. This country, too... it's the same. I really don't have the confidence to properly fulfill the role of a prince."
Dagmon gritted his teeth and continued.
"Please don't be like that. It's not like you, Dagmon."
"What *is* like me?"
"What's like Dagmon... well... it's smiling. Always cheerful... Isn't the name 'Royce' supposed to mean 'joyful'?"
"Is that so? Then, today must be the day I give up on being myself."
Only then did Dagmon grin, a smile truly like him.
"That's it. Dagmon looks cool when he smiles."
"Really? Thank you."
"And Dagmon, you're already a good prince. Last time, in Bergamo village, you treated so many injured people, didn't you? How many princes can heal their people?"
"If that's all it takes to be a good prince, that would be great."
"What do you mean, 'that's all'? By the way, can I ask you something?"
Lishia hesitated, unable to bring herself to say something, fidgeting.
"Ask away. What is it?"
Only then did Lishia ask.
"But did you really kill Princess Sera's younger brother, Dagmon?"
Dagmon waved his hand, as if to say it absolutely wasn't true, and replied.
"No, it's a complete misunderstanding. I encountered the royal carriage while traveling through the Kingdom of Ceres. At that time, I deliberately avoided the royal carriage in a hurry. Because I was a prince of an enemy nation. But right before my eyes, as I watched from hiding, that royal carriage was hit by a magic attack and exploded. I couldn't identify the person who attacked it. However, when I went through the shattered debris, I found a small boy barely clinging to life, so I took him to a nearby village and tried every method to save him. But there was nothing I could do. I only sent his body back to the Ceres royal palace via messenger. But Princess Sera, who vowed revenge, somehow found out about me and has been chasing me to kill me."
"Phew~ That's a relief."
Lishia replied with a relieved smile.
"What is?"
Puzzled by her reaction, Dagmon asked again.
"I was thinking, what if Dagmon really killed that child? A child who was only five years old... If that were the case, Dagmon would be a murderer, wouldn't he? I'm relieved you're not such a bad person. Wouldn't that make you a truly bad prince?"
"I..."
Dagmon was about to give some kind of excuse, but a memory from the past flashed through his mind, and he stopped speaking.
"Then, have you talked directly with Princess Sera?"
Lishia continued to ask, seemingly interested.
"Talk? She only tries to kill me."
"Then, as a prince, you don't fight Princess Sera?"
"Princess Sera is a pitiful person, if you think about it. There's no need for me to fight her too."
"I see. Dagmon, you really are a kind person. Let's go back now. Aaron will be waiting. Even though he seems gruff on the outside, that grumbler worries a lot about others."
Lishia brushed herself off and stood up, and Dagmon followed suit.
"Lishia?"
Dagmon suddenly called out to Lishia, who was walking ahead.
"Yes?"
Lishia heard the call and turned back towards Dagmon. Her hair shimmered beautifully with the starlight each time it swayed.
"Thank you. No one has ever said something like this to me before."
Dagmon awkwardly expressed his gratitude, feeling shy.
"Hehe. It's nothing."
Lishia's smile brightened even Dagmon's heart. Lishia and Dagmon began to walk back to the cave where Aaron was waiting, and in Dagmon's mind, as he followed, he was still recalling the war, his own weakness, and past events. Not that child, but he had committed murder without justification.
He hated his weak self, who only ever ran away from the position of a prince given by his father. He wanted to end this tiresome cycle now.
"A murderer..."
Dagmon murmured quietly. However, the sound of Dagmon and Lishia treading through the bushes drowned out Dagmon's small voice, and the darkness soon swallowed even the sound of their footsteps. Behind their shadows, only the starlight in the night sky seemed like a great roar.

titleEn: The Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode 2
contentEn:
Aaron was startled when Apollo tried to directly attack Lysia, who was unable to move. Judging that there was no time to lose, he lowered the nose of his glider without hesitation and charged at Apollo. Apollo, as if expecting it, deftly dodged and drew his sword, attacking Aaron. Aaron twisted his body to avoid the sword, but being strapped to the glider, it wasn't easy. Aaron ended up suffering a severe wound to his arm.
"Aargh! Damn it!"
Aaron screamed. Aaron, along with his glider, crashed into a corner of the temple.
"Ugh."
"Aaron!"
Lysia's desperate voice, worried about Aaron, was heard. Before Aaron could reply, Apollo immediately attacked again with a spell. Large pillars of fire were seen erupting towards Aaron. Aaron tried to roll to avoid them, but again, the glider held him back. He barely managed to twist his body and block the flames with the glider, and half of the glider was hit by the flames, burning away. Aaron, without time to free himself from the glider, forcibly broke it apart and detached himself, drawing his sword.
"Alright. Let's have a proper fight now. I won't hold back!"
Aaron charged at Apollo. As Aaron tried to vertically slash him with his sword, Apollo hastily used a defensive spell to block Aaron. Aaron, putting power and sword energy into another horizontal thrust, caused Apollo to fall while still maintaining his defensive spell. As a mage, Apollo was no match for Aaron in close combat. Just as Aaron was about to deliver a decisive blow, Apollo teleported to a nearby rock with a spell, creating distance from Aaron and unleashing more magic.
Aaron easily dodged those spells. A flustered Apollo began to chant another spell. Aaron leaped towards Apollo again to interrupt his spell. The moment Aaron jumped at Apollo, black things blocked his path.
"What is this!"
They were not strong, but with dozens of them attacking at once, they were not easy to deal with. Aaron struck down a few of them with his sword.
"Damn, what are these?"
Dozens of crows were blocking the space between Apollo and Aaron, attacking Aaron.
"Tch. Such a pathetic mage, resorting to petty tricks. Amasha!"
As Aaron swung his sword with a destruction spell, the crows blocking his path exploded and scattered into pieces. Crow blood splattered on Aaron's clothes.
"Tch. Disgusting."
Aaron looked for Apollo, but he had already disappeared. Then, Apollo's voice was heard from somewhere.
"Aaron! You are indeed just a strong fool. I will give you a suitable opponent. Darkness will cover the sun, and the Mother of Darkness shall appear. Even the god of this land cannot contend with her. Resurrect, Asherah!"
As Apollo's voice echoed from somewhere, a strong wind began to blow. It was a summoning spell. Judging by its scale, it was clearly a high-level summoning spell. Suddenly, the giant Asherah statue in the center of the temple began to glow.
"What is it?"
As the light from Asherah shone, the villagers' behavior became strange again. Royce's medicine didn't seem to be working, as the villagers were approaching Lysia.
'Is this the power of this Asherah?'
"Aargh ~ No ~"
Lysia's scream echoed, and she kicked at the approaching people, her face pale. Since the people were hypnotized, they couldn't avoid Lysia's kicks and fell back. However, they kept approaching like zombies, so it seemed she couldn't hold out forever. Aaron put away his sword and tried to run to save Lysia. At that moment, Aaron felt something chilling and rolled to the side. 'Boom!' An incredibly large stone spear pierced the spot where Aaron had been standing. If Aaron hadn't dodged that giant stone spear, he would have been shattered into pieces.
"What is that?"
The Asherah statue in front of the temple was moving its massive body as if alive. Asherah walked towards Aaron, and the giant stone spear attacked again with terrifying speed. The massive stone spear plunged into the hard ground as if piercing soft tofu, and when it struck rocks, they shattered with a loud noise.
"Oh. This is incredible. If I get hit by that, there won't be a second chance."
Aaron dodged the Asherah statue's attack, then climbed her arm and leaped towards Asherah's head. Aaron plunged his sword into the Asherah statue's head, and a 'clang' sound was heard as his sword struck the stone Asherah. The sword was precisely embedded an inch deep between Asherah's eyebrows.
'Got it.'
However, at that moment, Aaron felt Asherah's giant hand coming down on him from behind again.
"Damn it!"
Aaron tried to pull out the sword with force, but it wouldn't budge. Aaron gave up on the sword and dodged her hand. Once again, Asherah's spear targeted him and attacked. Aaron chanted a spell to use Iwa, dodging Asherah's stone spear and leaping up. But at the same time, Asherah's hand came down, and this time, he couldn't dodge it. Aaron was hit by an immense impact before he could finish chanting the spell and was thrown back.
"Aargh!"
As he fell, receiving a body-shattering impact, Lysia's scream was heard. It seemed impossible to save Lysia if he kept fighting Asherah like this. Moreover, with his sword gone, despair overwhelmed Aaron even more, and Asherah didn't seem like an opponent that could be defeated with one or two spells he could cast with his remaining stamina. So he looked for Apollo, who had summoned Asherah, but he was no longer visible, and the giant Asherah statue stood between Lysia, who was surrounded by the crowd, and Aaron.
'Oh no... This can't be... Damn it. What do I do?'
Lysia was crying and kicking them away, and her skirt was already badly torn. Aaron dodged Asherah's attacks a few more times and completed the Iwa spell.
"Iwa!"
Having already cast Amasha, a high-level destruction magic, the most powerful spell Aaron could use was Iwa, a mid-level destruction magic. Aaron unleashed the spell towards Asherah.
Boom! It exploded against Asherah with a loud sound. However, Asherah was only slightly damaged in form and suffered no actual injury.
"Iwa! Iwa!"
Aaron, with all his might, fired several more destruction spells in succession, but soon he could no longer use magic. Moreover, if he continued to use magic, he wouldn't have enough stamina left to dodge Asherah's attacks. Aaron's breath grew ragged, and his heart felt like it would burst. Now, there was truly no way to deal with Asherah. He desperately wanted to save at least Lysia, but he had no method.
Asherah, with her massive body, slowly approached Aaron, who was struggling even to stand. In the already dark night, Asherah's colossal figure, illuminated by torches, looked like a giant demon. Lysia's desperate resistance was still ongoing, and then one of them finally grabbed Lysia's leg.
"Lysia!"
Aaron saw that and called Lysia's name. As one person subdued Lysia, others quickly swarmed her.
"Aargh! Aaron! Help me!"
"Ugh. This is truly maddening."
All Aaron could do was dodge Asherah's attacks.
"Ugh!"
Eventually, Aaron didn't last long and was caught by Asherah's giant hand. Aaron felt his body being crushed within Asherah's hand. Aaron's mind was already fading. From afar, only Lysia's screams were heard, heartbreakingly.
Then, a familiar voice reached Aaron's ears.
"Brother Aaron!"
It was Dirsa. Dirsa appeared from the forest, where people were gathered, with a small dragon in her arms, her eyes wide with surprise.
"Dirsa! Don't come! Ugh!"
Asherah tightened her grip on Aaron. Dirsa was utterly shocked by the unfolding scene. Lysia was on the verge of being assaulted by the people, and Aaron was trapped in the hand of the giant statue. Dirsa didn't know what to do. Suddenly, Aaron heard a loud boom that made his mind reel from the shock and his ears ring. Stone dust began to pour from Asherah's body everywhere. Simultaneously, Dirsa made a decision and began to run towards Lysia.
"Aaron! I'm here!"
Aaron easily recognized the owner of that cheerful voice. Aaron looked towards the sound, and Royce was standing on a large rock, shouting at him. And Royce threw something forcefully at Asherah. The moment it touched Asherah's body, Asherah crumbled into pieces with another tremendous boom.
Dirsa cut through the hypnotized people and ran to Lysia. Occasionally, someone blocked Dirsa's path, but most were chased away by Shaga's fire breath. Dirsa squeezed through the chaos, further intensified by Royce's attack, and finally reached Lysia. The last person who tried to assault Lysia was scared out of their wits by Shaga's flames, and Dirsa quickly untied the ropes on Lysia's hands.
"Sister. Are you okay?"
"Thank you, Dirsa. Stay close to me."
Lysia's voice was still hoarse from being so startled, but she quickly regained her composure, kicked away one of the approaching people, and snatched someone's outer garment to cover her exposed parts. The people were so strongly hypnotized that they easily fell to Lysia's clumsy attacks. Asherah, unable to withstand Royce's attack any longer, knelt and released Aaron. Aaron quickly pulled out the sword embedded in Asherah's head. And he shouted at Royce.
"Royce. Stop it!"
Only after Aaron's words of dissuasion did Royce stop destroying the already shattered Asherah.
"Lysia! Can't you bring these people back to their senses?"
When Aaron shouted, Lysia, as if remembering, began to chant a spell.
"To control people with such trivial hypnosis spells, even if I'm not good at offensive magic, I'm confident in this kind of magic. Esdon!"
As Lysia's spell echoed through Hiddekel, everyone began to return to their senses. Lysia's spell had four

Perhaps imbued with a magical power that calms people's hearts, even those released from hypnosis weren't overly flustered, and it even brought peace to the minds of Aaron's party, who hadn't been hypnotized. Licia shouted through the Hiddegel magic.
"Everyone, you have been deceived by that false magician until now. I have already broken the spell you have feared until now, so now you don't need to forcibly believe in this strange religion."
People began to murmur. Some still seemed afraid and disbelieving. Then, this time, Aaron shouted.
"Avolo has already fled! What you need to do now is take care of the injured people next to you!"
"Who is fleeing?!"
But as if on cue, Avolo's shout was heard. At that voice, people began to scream in fear and confusion, and fled.
"Damn it! Where is he?"
At that moment, flames shot up from underground.
"What?"
"Underground!"
Avolo was already out of his mind. Avolo shot up from the ground and soared into the sky. Then he spewed fire magic everywhere, engulfing the entire forest in flames.
"All of you will die here now!"
The fire magic Avolo wildly shot from the air mercilessly burned the forest. With a half-mad look on his face, Avolo tried to cast yet another spell. The people watched the scene from below.
However, he couldn't finish the spell. With a 'thwack,' Avolo looked down at his chest. An arrowhead, having pierced him from the back, protruded through his chest. Avolo placed his hand on his chest, where red blood was gushing. Avolo let out a hollow, meaningless laugh. Avolo let out a loud, long scream. As that sound vibrated through the forest, as if it were a signal to begin, dozens of arrows left the bowstrings of the village youths. His body, riddled with arrows like a hedgehog, hung miserably in the sky. But that was only for a moment; Avolo's lifeless body fell helplessly and disappeared into the forest flames.
Licia once again used the psychological magic, Esdon, to calm the people, and the calmed villagers began to put out the mountain fire.

"Wow~ Sagya, are you really a dragon?"
Yusdo giggled, holding onto Sagya. Lishia, who had been sitting blankly staring at the lake, seemed to snap out of it at Yusdo's question, startled, then smiled and replied.
"Yes. A real dragon."
However, Sagya, held captive, coughed painfully but didn't act mean towards young Yusdo. Yusdo continued to laugh and play with Sagya, while Lishia once again stared at the lake, deep in thought. Lishia always felt a sense of peace when looking at the lake. It was probably due to her friendship with Anel. Dirsa approached Lishia, placing a hand on her shoulder, and said,
"Thinking about big brother Aron, aren't you?"
"Ah... no. Just..."
Lishia said, startled as if caught. Then Dirsa smiled and said in a playful voice,
"Oh~ It's written all over your face. He'll be fine. He's... strong."
"But what should we do now?"
Then Dirsa replied in a weak voice again,
"We should go back to the village."
"......... Right. Somehow... if Misa is there, we have to go for her sake."
"No! If you go there!"
Yusdo stopped playing with Sagya and shouted.
"Sister, you can't go there!"
"Yusdo!"
Dirsa yelled at Yusdo.
"He's right, Dirsa. You stay here with Yusdo."
"No. I'm going. How can I let you go into danger alone, unnie?"
"No. Leave it to me. If you come along, you'll only be a hindrance. I'm not that skilled, but I'm a mage... You saw my skills, didn't you? Don't worry."
Dirsa was speechless at being called a hindrance. Lishia left them there and headed for the village. Lishia honestly wasn't confident. She knew well that the offensive magic she could use was almost useless. But she resolved to herself that she had to be brave for Dirsa's sake and walked on. However, she also wished Aron was there. She thought, 'If it were him, he would surely act cool and confident in a situation like this...'
"Is this the right way? I think I teleported roughly east..."
Just then, a 'Kyaak' sound came from the sky. Sagya was circling in the air, showing her the way.
"Thank you, Sagya."
Lishia soon neared the village. The streets were quiet, as if all the villagers were inside their homes. Lishia quietly chanted a spell.
"Svanya. (Hiding magic)"
Lishia's body glowed white and then became invisible. Lishia walked, observing the village's situation. Then she entered a large building in the center of the village.
It was structured like a temple. In the front stood a wooden statue of a woman. At first glance, it felt captivating, but somehow lacked dignity. Several villagers were gathered in the temple, chatting and worshipping. Lishia quietly stood nearby, eavesdropping on their conversations. Lishia was overjoyed when she heard them talking about Aron.
'He escaped safely.'
Later, as they continued to spout lewd remarks, Lishia's face turned red with anger, and she kicked the butt of the person who was talking. Seeing the person's bewildered expression, Lishia couldn't help but laugh. Lishia covered her mouth and giggled.
Then, as if they heard Lishia's laughter, one of them shouted,
"Who's there!"
Lishia's heart sank instantly. She felt her own heartbeat loudly and her body trembled. Lishia carefully and stealthily moved away from them. Then, when she reached the building's door, she quickly ran out.
"Phew~"
Outside, Lishia sighed, clutching her chest. Lishia continued to walk around the village, observing. Then she saw a small girl in a small house, looking out of a window with iron bars, from a room locked from the outside, with an incredibly sad face.
Thinking the child might be Misa, Lishia opened the door and quietly entered. Fortunately, no one was home. Lishia opened the door to the room where the child was confined. The child heard the door open and shouted,
"Go! Just go!"
She shouted without turning her head.
"Shhh~ Be quiet. It'll be a big problem if we're caught. Are you Misa?"
The small girl was startled by the unexpectedly gentle voice and looked in the direction of the voice. However, she saw no one, only heard the voice.
"Kyaa~! Is it a ghost?"
The child screamed in surprise. Lishia's heart sank, fearing the scream would attract people.
"Shhh~! I told you to be quiet. I'm a mage who's hidden my appearance to rescue you. And I'm Dirsa's friend, okay?"
"What? Sister Dirsa?"
The child looked relieved at the mention of Dirsa's name.
"Yes. But where are you? I can't see you at all."
"I used a hiding spell to make myself invisible. I'm right in front of you."
Misa reached out her hand. When she touched Lishia, she was startled and pulled her hand back.
"Just a moment..."
As Lishia chanted a spell, she returned to her original form. Misa, seeing Lishia, looked overjoyed for a moment, then burst into tears and clung to Lishia. Lishia hugged Misa and comforted her, saying,
"Don't cry. It'll be a big problem if others hear you."
Lishia struggled for a long time to comfort Misa but eventually succeeded. Lishia hugged Misa and tried to go outside. However, when Lishia stepped out, she was startled. People had already surrounded and besieged the house.
"H-how did this happen?"
A person dressed as a mage approached. Misa, held in Lishia's arms, clung tightly to Lishia's neck, as if afraid.
"There's nowhere to run, young lady. You were lucky to escape the temple earlier. A magic circle has been cast here, so Elieser (escape magic) is impossible."
Lishia was dumbfounded.
'No choice, since it's come to this, I have to see it through to the end...'
Lishia put Misa down on the ground and hid her behind her.
'But what should I do? Do I have to use magic on people? What if they get hurt? Are they bad people, so it's okay? Ugh. I don't know. I'll just scare them. But what should I use? I can't use offensive magic.'
The mage suddenly raised his hand to the sky and shouted,
"Catch that girl!"
Then people began to rush forward.
Panicked, Lishia hastily swung her hand and chanted an offensive spell.
"Amasha!"
Then, the ground directly in front of the charging people exploded with an enormous cloud of dust and a loud roar. Not a single person was hit by the magic, but those nearby were thrown back by the force of the explosion. The villagers, surprised and frightened by its power, cautiously retreated, remaining in a circle but not moving, ready to flee at any moment.
'Ah. It worked.'
Lishia was secretly proud that she had used offensive magic.
"A powerful mage for such a young girl... but you didn't hit anyone. And it's too clumsy to be considered a threat. You've never hurt anyone, have you? Am I wrong?"
Abolo said with a sneer.
"Don't make me laugh! This time I'll really hit you."
Lishia wasn't confident but bluffed. His guess wasn't wrong, but it was also due to her inability to control it well.
"Everyone attack!"
However, despite Abolo's shout, the people only hesitated. After seeing the power of the magic earlier, no one dared to rush forward first.
Lishia felt relieved. She hoped they wouldn't attack. Even if she wasn't confident in hitting them, she hoped her magic wouldn't hurt anyone.
"Tsk. Cowards. No choice then."
Abolo began to chant a spell. Lishia felt the atmosphere among the people suddenly change.
'What's happening?'
"Now. It's Lady Asera's command. Quickly seize that woman!"
The people shouted 'Wah!' and rushed forward without an ounce of fear. Lishia still couldn't bring herself to use offensive magic on them. Lishia quickly hugged Misa, who was trembling with fear.
"Aswat! Dilon!"
Lishia continuously chanted escape magic and telekinesis magic spells. Instantly, a large light shone, blinding the people. Lishia, holding Misa, floated above the people's heads. She intended to temporarily blind them and then escape. However, Abolo was already floating in the air, blocking Lishia's path.
'Right, I can use magic on this guy.'
Lishia channeled her magic.
"Ur!"
However, the fire magic she intended to use on Abolo exploded in front of Lishia. Lishia hugged Misa tightly to prevent her from getting hurt. The shock of the magic was unleashed directly upon Lishia.
"Heh heh. Now I see your magic is clumsy too."
Saying this, Abolo instantly flew towards Lishia and struck her with his fist. Lishia screamed from the impact and fell to the ground.
Aron didn't know how long he had been unconscious. When he came to, he found himself absurdly tied up, hands and feet bound behind his back, inside a shed.
"What happened?"
Aron looked around. He found Royce similarly tied up next to him.
"Hey!"
"Mmm..."
Royce opened his eyes.
"Huh? What happened?"
"I don't know either. I remember falling, but..."
"Where are my glasses? I can't see well..."
"What are you looking for?"
"My glasses. My eyesight is bad."
"What are glasses?"
"They're made of ground glass, and if you wear them, you can correct your vision."
"Such a thing exists?"
"There are many strange things in the Eastern lands."
Aron strained his arms and said,
"Ugh. It's no use. They've tied me up really tight."
Just then, the shed door creaked open, and a person entered.
"Ah. You are?"
Aron shouted in an angry voice. The person was Abolo, the mage of Bergamo village.
"Well met, Aron. I am Abolo."
"Ugh. How do you know my name..."
"That's a secret. I thought you were quite strong and smart, but to think you'd fall from the sky on your own accord."
"That's not my fault."
Aron said, glaring at Royce.

“Heh... that, I made a mistake in my calculations...”
Lois said in a hushed voice. Avolo continued speaking.
“And, your cute girlfriend was also captured. While trying to rescue the little girl we had.”
More than anything, Aaron was furious at these words.
“Ugh, you bastard, Lishia! If you hurt Lishia, I'll kill you!”
“Huhu, worrying about others in this situation. Anyway, fine. You, tonight, as a burnt offering to the god Ashera, that Lishia, was it? That girl will be offered as our dancer. Farewell for now. Hero of Light. Hahahaha.”
Avolo laughed disgustingly and walked out of the barn, and the sound of the barn door locking with a thud was heard.
“Aargh..! You, that guy...”
Aaron shouted in anger. Then Lois said in a small voice.
“You're the Hero of Light?”
“What's the point of knowing something like that!”
“No. That is an ancient legend of light written in Dragonia. Saving the world... that is very important.”
“Tch. I'm sick of hearing such nonsense.”
“It is absolutely necessary in this land now. If the Hero of Light truly exists, that is. Many races are waiting for him. In this land, where bloody wars and dark magic run rampant, he would be much better than foolish royalty.”
“I don't have that much power!”
“No. You felt different. From the beginning.”
“If I can't even untie this damn rope, what good is being the Hero of Light or anything else...”
“I'll see what I can do about that.”
Lois pulled out a small bottle from his sleeve and poured the liquid inside onto the rope tied around Aaron's wrist. The rope soon corroded and broke easily.
“Is it magic?”
Lois then untied the rope on his own feet and said.
“It's just one of the chemicals I carry. These ropes are weak to acid.”
And then, he approached Aaron.
“What on earth is going on, anyway, hurry up and untie me.”
“Before that, tell me first. What exactly happened. You promised to tell me, didn't you?”
“What? Where's that coming from?”
“Then, I won't untie you.”
“Alright, fine. I'll tell you. Actually, I don't know the details either. I'll just tell you what I experienced.”
Aaron recounted what he had experienced. Lois then thought for a moment and said, untying Aaron's ropes.
“In that case, Dirsa must have been chosen as Ashera's dancer.”
“What? What's that?”
“Ashera's dancer means death. And by debauchery... that's just how the god Ashera is. There. You're all untied.”
Aaron rubbed his freed hands, which seemed to be numb, and said.
“Then, that's a big problem! Lishia was captured, and they said she'd be offered to Ashera as a dancer.”
“Then, it really is a big problem. But there's time. They said we'd be offered as a burnt offering tonight, didn't they? She'll probably be presented as a dancer for the first time with the ritual then.”
“In that case, I'd better go rescue her quickly.”
Aaron sprang to his feet.
“Wait a minute. We can't just go in blindly. That wizard has all the villagers under his command. It doesn't seem like it's just bound by faith; the wizard is probably controlling them. If we push through with brute force, the villagers will get hurt, and Lishia and Misal might get hurt too.”
“Then what do we do?” Aaron said, slumping down.
“First, let's wait until evening. The first ritual of the dancer will probably begin at the same time the burnt offering is made. Avolo will clearly be playing the role of the priest then, and if we just deal with Avolo at that time, it will be simple.”
“That's a good idea.”
Aaron soon grinned and agreed.
“Then, I guess we should pretend to be tied up and wait. But, Lois, you're really amazing. You seem to know everything without hesitation.”
“Oh, it's nothing.”
“It feels strange when you use such formal language, even though we don't seem to be that far apart in age. How about we speak informally?”
“I'm comfortable with this way of speaking.”
“It's because I feel like I'm constantly treating you like a subordinate. I'd like to treat you as a friend.”
“Do as you please.”
“Ugh. I told you to drop that way of speaking. From now on, I won't bother with formalities. I like that.”
Aaron said, looking at Lois as if he couldn't be helped. Aaron somehow felt that he got along well with Lois.
