Have we ever deeply considered how it developed after the Meiji Restoration, or why and how it invaded our country?
Regarding Ahn Jung-geun, how much do we know beyond him being the person who killed Itō Hirobumi and his palm print?

Japan's history of enlightenment was very similar to ours. Looking at what was written in "Today's Person"...

"During his time as Resident-General of the Korean Empire, Itō once tried to persuade Dosan [Ahn Chang-ho](http://people.naver.com/DetailView.nhn?frompage=nx_people&id=8344) to form a youth cabinet in Joseon. At that time, Dosan said, “If Americans had come and carried out Japan's Meiji Restoration, would you have stood by idly? We, too, intend to achieve independence with our own hands. So, you Japanese should withdraw.” Faced with the spirit of the young Korean independence activist Ahn Chang-ho, the seasoned politician Itō could not respond. This was because it was precisely what he himself had done as a Japanese politician."

There is a passage like the one above.
A figure who was patriotic for his own country, but in other countries, completely abandoned the values he championed.
Was it Korea's misfortune that a figure like Ahn Chang-ho, who could have been as influential as Itō Hirobumi, did not emerge earlier in Korea?

History is relative. However, universal values do exist.
According to what many Japanese claim, the Korean Peninsula was modernized and industrialized by Japan.
How should we respond to this? In some aspects, it is true. It's not a false statement.
If we respond without knowing anything, it's nothing more than stubborn insistence.
[Related Post ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70043259685](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70043259685))]

Can we simply insist, "Independence means our country should be left alone"?
If it hadn't been Japan, wouldn't Russia or China have taken similar actions?

We cannot criticize them solely in the name of nationalism without understanding imperialism.
Only by understanding imperialism can we criticize them.

If we cannot explain "development for exploitation and war," we will inevitably fall prey to their logic.
And these parts were never taught in textbooks, nor did we learn them.
Because we only received history education for college entrance exams.
In 5000 years of history, the period of Japan's annexation of Korea was only 36 years, and due to past governments not being able to be proud of it, there was almost no content taught about modern history.

Even if we simply recount the unfair stories our grandparents experienced, we will inevitably be met with demands for historical evidence.
Furthermore, there's no law saying that it couldn't be remembered as a beautiful time for some who sided with the Japanese government back then.

At the very least, information without subjective intervention cannot be good or evil. Moreover, it is effective in understanding necessary values and true patriotism.
Can Naver's story about Itō Hirobumi simply be seen as "As expected, Naver" and nothing more than bad?
How is simply enjoying the exaggerated lies written in a book like "Japan Doesn't Exist" any different from Japanese people enjoying reading "Ugly Koreans"?

Only recently has there been a re-examination of Dokdo.
What the song "Dokdo is Our Land" aims to teach is information about "Dokdo" that one needs to know for "Dokdo to be our land."
It is natural that to know Ahn Jung-geun, one must know Itō Hirobumi, and to know Dokdo, one must know Takeshima.
**Am I a traitor for believing that there is no more suitable figure for "World's Person" the day after the March 1st Movement than this?**

However, if I were to ask a bit more of Naver,
I think it would have been better if Ahn Jung-geun had also appeared in "Today's Korean."
The problem is that service seems to only feature living people.

I feel a bit disappointed that Korean historical figures are not covered separately.
To know the world's great figures, shouldn't we also know Korea's great figures?

*   I subscribe to Godowon's Morning Letter, and although I don't open it often, sometimes when I do, I feel like I've been hit by a hammer. I've been donating 20,000 won a month for a child, and I recently received a letter from that child. When I sponsored an Afghan child in the past, I regretted not being able to send a warm gift, so I resolved to send one this time, but I kept procrastinating until now. I missed Christmas, and this time I missed Seollal (Lunar New Year) too. Excuses like being busy with work, and feeling a bit burdened by tens of thousands of won. Sitting in a warm office, working, paying millions of won in tuition fees and studying, yet I, who only sent 240,000 won a year, couldn't even recall the child's name immediately, which filled me with unspeakable shame.

    Today, when I go home... I must look it up again. Even if I'm busy, I'll look at the child's name and photo again, and I will send a gift before March ends.

    Even if I'm busy, I should definitely open short letters of reflection like this.

titleEn: The Old Partner: A Story of Parents Like Oxen
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=50869

#### [Old Partner](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=50869)

Director Lee Chung-ryoul
Cast Choi Won-gyun, Lee Sam-soon, Old Man Choi's Ox
Release 2008 South Korea, 78 min
**Rating**

Perhaps because I had heard so much about how sad and touching it was, I started watching the movie prepared to be moved.
However, perhaps because it was a documentary-style film, it felt rather bland at first.
 
My initial impression of the film was like taking a break in a quiet countryside.
Throughout the movie, there were no bustling buildings or numerous cars obstructing the view, providing a comfortable screen.
 
In fact, the plot didn't have much grand content, but it was a film that provided a lot to think about.
 
**1. The Ox and the Old Man, Alike**
However, the life of the old ox resembled the life of the old man.
Perhaps that was the main theme.
The ending credit, dedicating this film to all fathers on this land, conveyed it well.
In this information age, a time when money has become the highest value in the world,
it was the story of someone spending their old age unable to adapt.
 

**2. Reality**
A somewhat uncomfortable point was our self-deprecating reflection on why we had to make them struggle until the very end.
Although it's said to be a politically neutral film, because it depicted the reality of rural areas, the "Korea-US FTA" topic came up.
I heard the president watched it... I imagine the mention of "mad cow" must have been quite uncomfortable.
In fact, no matter how favorably one views it, the FTA is not a good thing for rural areas. Especially not for those who farm such small plots of land.
(In my personal opinion... the FTA is necessary, but measures for the elderly should be prepared. They know nothing but the land. Anyway, once they pass away, small-scale tenant farming will no longer exist, so the damage won't be that great. Since some of the benefits of the Korea-US FTA come from their sacrifice, I hope the government will pay a little attention to them at least until they pass away.)
 
**3. Fathers' Hearts, the Ox's Thick Tears**
Ultimately, the old ox, which had worked its entire life, is pushed aside by younger oxen, and the grandfather's heartache at being offered 1 million won is like the hearts of our fathers.
Having worked hard their entire lives, they must have been upset to suddenly be treated as obsolete.
 
**4. The Calf Following the Old Ox**
Furthermore, the old man's stubbornness reminded us of what we have lost today.
The young calf's constant desire to go to the old ox also signified that our children need the unconditional love and the lesson of living slowly that they can learn from their grandparents. However, we, too, were forcing our children into a busy way of life with academies and other things.
 
**5. Unconditional Parental Love**
Until the very end, the ox worked silently and laboriously, and eventually passed away.
At the end, when the grandmother said the ox had gathered a lot of firewood so it wouldn't be cold, and I saw the pile of wood, a lump formed in my throat and my eyes welled up.
'What was the ox thinking while carrying all that firewood?'
The ox, which worked silently for the old man without complaining about its heavy, aching body, was the story of our fathers who don't complain about hardship.
 
**6. The Young Ox and Us**
In these times when working oxen no longer exist, are we living as well as our fathers did?

titleEn: Revisiting the Green New Deal Initiative
contentEn:
[http://www.seri.org/db/dbReptV.html?menu=db02&pubkey=db20090211001&pgsd](http://www.seri.org/db/dbReptV.html?menu=db02&pubkey=db20090211001&pgsd)=

Re-examining the Green New Deal Project
No. 691, 2009.02.11 [Do Geon-woo](https://blog.naver.com/javascript%3Cx/%3E:viewProf('209535','2');) [Lee Ji-hoon](https://blog.naver.com/javascript%3Cx/%3E:viewProf('959146','2');) [Shin Chang-mok](https://blog.naver.com/javascript%3Cx/%3E:viewProf('168440','2');)

| Summary | The 'Green New Deal,' which proposes economic stimulus through sustainable new methods, is rapidly emerging as a solution to overcome the triple crises of economic downturn, employment crisis, and environmental crisis. The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has highlighted the Green New Deal as a solution to overcome the economic crisis, proposing five priority areas including clean energy and clean technology. Countries worldwide are also engaging in a 'Green New Deal competition' to overcome the crisis. |
| --- | --- |
| Table of Contents | Ⅰ. Economic Crisis and New Deal Projects Ⅱ. Global Green New Deal Competition Ⅲ. Characteristics of the Korean-style Green New Deal Ⅳ. Implications and Suggestions |

Overseas, it's clear that 'green' is the motto. For example, they've built 'railroads' instead of 'roads.' Our current problem is that while we've adopted 'green' as our motto, targeting roads, which have the highest carbon emissions, and waterways, which are not far behind, seems to be going in the wrong direction, doesn't it?
While I support the government's renewable energy projects and believe they should be given more impetus, it seems problematic if this leads to utilizing the Four Major Rivers. I believe it would be more 'green' to focus on maintaining the Four Major Rivers and enhancing their function as urban lungs.
At the very least, the proposed utilization of the Four Major Rivers as an industrial means appears likely to increase carbon emissions. Furthermore, in Korea's case, I believe that addressing inefficient carbon emissions from haphazard development and existing cities first would yield greater actual benefits in terms of reduction.
Of course, new cities should also reduce carbon emissions, but even with reductions, building new ones still implies an increase.
While green initiatives can generate new growth engines and opportunities, we should not overlook the fact that they can also incur costs for businesses.
Moreover, even if Korea's current fiscal health is good, whether there are sufficient funds to prepare for future ongoing problems is also a subject for discussion. Shouldn't we, at the very least, keep some 'bullets' for extreme defense?
While 'green' that benefits the environment and humanity is always welcome, if it's 'green' that merely aims for short-term growth driven by development issues, I believe it will eventually become a cost for the entire nation and boomerang back.
I acknowledge the necessity of the Green New Deal. My hope is that its detailed plans are well-executed. If development issues prematurely cause real estate speculation, it will lead to increased development costs. Furthermore, I believe the Green New Deal should prioritize transportation and IT infrastructure, which have high carbon emission costs, rather than construction. Investing in operation and management rather than production might also lead to more sustainable employment effects.

While studying, I was surprised to find so many in-house knowledge-sharing sites.
I couldn't believe there were so many great resources.

Because I've been so focused solely on my team's work,
I forgot that this workplace I'm at is truly sensitive to the latest technology,
and is a company that does everything.

I've been too indifferent to the company's systems all this time.

I realized anew that I myself was a prime example of users failing to utilize
the integrated system built for knowledge sharing. ㅜㅜ

Studying is one thing, but somehow my data collection has only increased...
If I had just paid a little attention, it would have been so good for studying; I guess I've been too lazy all this time.

Although the company faced difficulties this year and salaries were frozen, I feel that working at a place like this is a blessing, if anything.
I should frequently check out what other teams are doing.
It seems all that's left is my will and ability.

http://book.naver.com/bookdb/book_detail.php?bid=4475016

[Haak Haak](http://book.naver.com/bookdb/book_detail.php?bid=4475016)

Lee Oi-soo
Haenam (Neobook) 2008.03.30.
Lee Oi-soo's Haak Haak.
I would like to call him a convergence intellectual of this era.
His position, bridging the present and the past, is authentic.

Although he expresses sincere thoughts using netizens' language, his inner self holds the value of a literary figure and an intellectual.
I could feel that what was contained within was the truth, and the means of expression were nothing.
If I were to put it that way, someone might bring up Gwiyeoni, but the difference was that only entertainment existed within that, not value.

Isn't what makes Lee Oi-soo so great the fact that he doesn't speak of truth in difficult terms, but rather tells sincere stories at the eye level of this era?
Although he was not welcomed by the literary establishment from the beginning,
he, who is without pretense and always expresses himself honestly, might have been chosen as the most respected literary figure by university students for that very reason.

It was a good book that allowed me to dip my toes, even if just a little, into his depth.

titleEn: There She Is!! - The Green Muffler, A
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
 
It seems like a long time ago that I first encountered this animation.
When I first watched episode 1, I became a fan because I loved the "Love is all you need!" vibe.
Upon searching, I found it's a work by Amalloc from the creative group Sambakza.
Visiting their website, I saw they accept small donations, and these works have become famous overseas, gaining many international fans.
What was most unfamiliar and impressive was that they created and screened animations via the internet, not traditional media, and operated through donations and sponsorships.
 
For now, I'll skip this background and begin the review of the animation.
**** 
**Episode 1: There she is**
In a world where cats and rabbits should never date, Doki the rabbit falls for Nabi.
And that love disregards all conditions and procedures.
The story is about how her pure love even moves Nabi's heart.
The story, which began that way, was very enjoyable.
At first, I thought it was just Doki's love story, simply "Love is all you need!"
 
**Episode 2: Cake Dance**
However, as it moved to Episode 2 (subtitled Cake Dance), new friends appeared, and the worldview suddenly expanded rapidly.
The content of Episode 2 expands beyond just their relationship to relationships with the world.
Doki, who is loved by many and loves everyone and everything, was waiting above all for the cake from the one she truly loved.
However, Nabi's delivery of the cake is not easy.
Perhaps this was a foreshadowing of the conflict and resolution that would begin from Episode 3?
And at the end, by helping a small rabbit child deliver a cake, it hints at that small love growing.
 
**Episode 3: Doki & Nabi**
Doki and Nabi's first date began.
Nabi still finds Doki a bit bothersome and is conscious of the world's gaze.
But Doki doesn't care about such things. Nabi opens his heart to the cute Doki, awkwardly promises a second date, and their love grows.
However, the final scene ends with a window breaking and a stone flying in, hinting at an unusual conflict in their romantic relationship.
 
**Episode 4: Paradise**
This episode, ironically titled Paradise, is the first to feature a melancholic song (Taboo) as its background.
The cold reception their love faces from the world is directly depicted, and their love throws a hot issue into the society where cats and rabbits live.
Amidst this, Doki gets hurt by those who oppose their love, and a friend, worried about her, advises them to leave for Paradise, where their love is accepted.
Doki considers leaving for overseas/Paradise with Nabi to get their love recognized, but Nabi, thinking Doki got hurt because of him, cuts off contact with Doki. Ilho, who liked Doki but acknowledged Nabi, gets angry and beats Nabi. In the midst of this, they get caught in a fight between those who support their love and those who oppose it.
Doki eventually goes to the airport to go to Paradise alone.
Episode 4 was an episode with much to ponder. It was completely different from the bright stories before it. Although I didn't realize it well through episodes 1, 2, and 3, that society actually already had many elements of conflict. And perhaps the author, by naming escaping that society "Paradise," viewed that society as a reality rife with conflict, or even hell.
**** 
**Episode 5: Imagine**
I'm not sure why the title is Imagine. Perhaps my English skills are lacking...
Nabi, who was caught in the fight, comes out of the police station and follows a yellow chick, symbolizing hope, to a place where he finds green ribbons she had tied to a tree.
That color was initially like the scarf around Nabi's neck, and later, it was tied around the necks of various animals, big and small, that Doki had brought.
And Nabi, seeing those ribbons, realizes that he can be happy even if the world doesn't change. He realizes that the big answer isn't some grand solution, but Doki herself, that her love is Paradise. So, he starts chasing her to the airport with all his might. On the way, he receives a Paradise ticket from Ilho, but Nabi tears it up, vowing to bravely face his love, and Ilho also helps Nabi get to the airport. The obstacles in front of Nabi as he runs after her were trivial, and his friends were by his side, cheering them on, and eventually, they end with a touching reunion.
In an epilogue-like segment, the romantic relationships of other friend characters also turn out well.
Perhaps there will still be obstacles ahead for them. But they will be in Paradise. It ends with such a pleasant conclusion.
 
**Overall Review**
Somehow, it feels similar to today's world. Whether they support or oppose their love, both sides believe they are right, but neither side lives in Paradise.
Those who supported their love sometimes hailed them as heroes, but then pointed fingers at Doki, calling her a "Looser" as she left the airport. In reality, just as they were divided into rabbits and cats, they simply drew another line between those who supported love and those who didn't. Ultimately, Nabi and Doki were the ones hurt in that rift.
However, Doki changed the world. But she didn't love to change the world. If they could only be happy if the world changed, they should have left.
The method she practiced was simply caring for abandoned animals and tying green scarves around their necks. With that, she was living in Paradise.
Perhaps Doki was truly a Messiah in the true sense for Nabi.
 
In a society like today's, where the country is fiercely divided into East, West, Left, Right, progressive, and conservative... this animation made me ponder what it means to live happily.
In conclusion... this is an animation I keep replaying in frustrating times like these. I wish this animation were reality, not just Imagine.

titleEn: It seems the internet is indeed harmful.
contentEn:
Looking at the comments on Naver's articles about the Yongsan protest deaths,

Would people react this way even if a dog died?
The way they tear into someone else's death makes me even think they're like hyenas.

Both the deceased police officer and the protesters were someone's family.
How truly heartbreaking must these comments be for their families to see?

Malicious comments truly exist.

No one admits fault. Everyone is slandering each other,
and merely tearing into the deceased.

Although I believe in the positive functions of the internet and that humans are inherently capable of trusting and caring for one another,
every time I see this side of society, it frightens me deeply.

Why, instead of feeling sorrow for someone's death...
are they tearing into it like this, revealing their lack of humanity and shallowness?
How lamentable, Republic of Korea.

It's not an economic crisis or a lack of leadership that's the problem; this is a disease that will ruin the nation.
May the deceased rest in peace.

Reflecting on the Minerva incident... it leaves a truly bitter taste.

Many people were shocked that he was an unemployed man in his 30s, and those who opposed Minerva are ultimately pushing him to be seen as nothing more than an unemployed 30-something internet cafe addict. I, too, was concerned about his hero complex and extreme predictions, but I believed his writings had value. If someone had a grasp of the economy and the world to some extent, and possessed that level of analytical ability, I believed they would at least be a practitioner well-versed in economics or a degree holder. Indeed, Minerva himself introduced himself as a successful figure in a foreign company. It also seems that many people are more shocked by this incident because of that, and the opposing side seems to be mocking him.

But then. Thinking about it a bit more... I realized that I, too, was a narrow-minded person. Dr. Park Kyung-chul, whom I often referred to as "the country doctor," is also not an economics major, and he doesn't even directly engage in stock investment. Why did I trust him? Although I said I was drawn to his extensive knowledge and character, wasn't it partly the authority of him being a successful doctor that made me trust him with ease? I, too, felt a slight disappointment when Minerva was caught by the prosecution and revealed to be unemployed. This is because I had agreed with the notion that he was a (successful or practical) economic expert.
[http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70040096980](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70040096980)

Looking at how things are unfolding these days, I get the feeling that the value of Minerva's writings is drifting in a strange direction. His extreme predictions certainly deserve criticism, but whether that warrants arrest... or whether it's important that he's an unemployed person, not an economic expert... something about the world is strange. From the outset, there's a strong sense that the government and media are also participating in this petty game, focusing on making him out to be an internet cafe addict. However, according to a certain lawmaker, even one point of contention has been revealed to involve foreign exchange intervention, giving a strong impression that the game is becoming increasingly petty.

The petty game of petty people. That seems to be a reflection of our distorted selves. The admiration I had for Ahn Cheol-soo when I was young was because he was both a computer expert and a doctor. And wasn't it the title of Dr. Park Kyung-chul being a doctor, along with his extensive economic knowledge and excellent writing skills, that made me trust him so much? It seems even Minerva himself was not free from this vanity. Why did he portray himself as such a figure? Isn't it a story that shows even those who criticize a distorted society are themselves members of that distorted society? And I, too, seem to be clinging to those prestigious degrees and jobs, hesitating to focus on what's important and broaden my own horizons.

Recently, I borrowed a book by Lee Oi-soo.

My boundaries and capacity are far too small.

titleEn: It seems the media's clickbait has started again
contentEn:
Arresting and interrogating a Minerva who is in his 30s and unemployed?
No matter how I look at it, it's hard to see him as Minerva. Unemployed in his 30s?
Even mainstream analysts said he was extreme but had practical experience in exchange rates...
It's hard to believe he was in his 20s during the IMF crisis.
Moreover, the atmosphere has been quite good these past few days... The government has no reason to stir up Minerva.
Yesterday, most conservative and progressive newscasts were talking about Minerva...
Is the media just trying to bait people?

Minerva supporters or opponents, flapping around after being baited here, are rather making Minerva into a hero, and the flustered government is also playing a part.

Recently, there hasn't been anything for Minerva to become an issue about, and isn't it the media that keeps making people curious about who he is? I'm not very interested in who he is. Though I've heard a bit, he's nothing more or less than an ordinary netizen who spouts extreme predictions and is a bit puffed up with a sense of heroism. And that kind of person could be any one of us; he's not a particularly special individual.

However, what's frustrating is... whether he is Minerva or not...
The very belief that "spreading false information" can be applied to economic predictions is quite absurd.

Many cite the Lee Myung-bak 3000 analogy, but that's not President Lee Myung-bak's fault.
Even mainstream analysts don't know what tomorrow will bring, and they make wrong predictions every day.

Even those at the very top don't have a 100% accuracy rate.
Fortune tellers are good at predicting the past, but not the future.
Are we going to arrest all of them?
I thought the law was equal before all and meant to protect the weak...
But I'm realizing anew that it can also be used by those in power to arrest people they dislike.
I also went around repeating the words of mainstream analysts that the first quarter would be in a 900-1300 range. If I'm wrong, am I going to jail? Haha, what a funny world.

Whether intentionally or unintentionally... Due to this incident, driven by the media, public sentiment will further turn away.

titleEn: Even Conservatives and Progressives Can Compromise and Talk
contentEn:
The only ones cursing it as a political deal or whatever are supporters of the Democratic Party and the Grand National Party. Have you actually taken a close look at the manifestos they both presented during the presidential election?

Excluding North Korea policy, their political lines were mostly similar, leaning towards social democracy. Strictly speaking, by international standards, Moon Kook-hyun and Roh Moo-hyun are conservatives. Progressivism in Korea doesn't exist outside of the Democratic Labor Party.

It's rather strange that Korea divides itself into conservative and progressive camps based solely on North Korea policy, and compromise between conservatives and progressives is possible.

Roh Moo-hyun also proposed a grand coalition. Perhaps it was a proposal made out of frustration, and seemed impossible and absurd, but at least his mindset was very much to my liking.

Moon Kook-hyun and Lee Hoi-chang also eventually achieved something similar. A political deal. It might be true. However, the agreement to take turns as floor leader would have been a losing proposition for the Liberty Forward Party (Seonjin Party), which had more seats, and Lee Hoi-chang also seems to be a magnanimous figure. Moon Kook-hyun's unwavering approval rating of 5-8% must have been regrettable for the Liberty Forward Party. Moreover, both parties similarly campaigned on the slogan of a 'clean image'.

But at least, it's better than seeing the Democratic Party and the Grand National Party carrying chainsaws and setting up barricades. Conservatives and progressives can compromise and converse as much as they want.

Even Obama in another country became president with that approach. With the slogan 'A Strong America, One America,' he garnered support that encompassed both conservatives and progressives. It's a stark contrast to someone who became president by dividing both sides.

I hope the Grand National Party and the Democratic Party would learn from this, and I hope our voters would also throw away those 'leftist commie,' 'die-hard conservative' Gyeongsang-do and Jeolla-do labels into the Sea of Japan and reclaim the concept of the East Sea.

titleEn: Future Impact of Opencast and Newscast
contentEn:
**1. The Impact of Outlinks**
 - As I've mentioned in previous posts, the change regarding outlinks is a very significant one for users.
 Some predict that many users will flee to other portals because of this.

** 1) Existing service users feel inconvenience and disappear (?)**
 However, personally, the truth is that "we don't know yet."
 Given that detailed links are provided to access existing services, I don't think there will be a significant exodus of users.
 Those who like Naver's news comments will click the [News Home] button at the top of News Cast,
 and [Trending Stories] is also exposed by default due to user demand.
 The fact that [Trending Stories] is still the #1 subscription with 6,381 subscribers shows the inclination of Naver users.
 
 Furthermore, the navigation tab, which used to be only on the left side of Open Cast, has now moved into the Open Cast content area,
 reflecting the voices of users during the beta test who were accustomed to the existing Naver interface.
 
** 2) Media outlets lining up (?)**
[http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&sid1=101&oid=018&aid=0002056412](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&sid1=101&oid=018&aid=0002056412)
 The "lining up" of media outlets, as some newspapers claim.
 I don't understand who is supposedly doing the lining up. They increased the number from a dozen to over thirty.
 Did Naver say it would arbitrarily select the rankings of these thirty-something outlets? It clearly stated that they would be automatically selected based on user preference.
 Now, the popularity ranking of media outlets will be displayed according to subscription numbers, so perhaps "lining up" might be true.
 However, this is not done by Naver, but by the users.
 And this is a natural outcome in a capitalist society, and it is also the duty of media outlets to reflect public opinion.
 
** 3) Naver's relinquishment of editorial rights**
 No one denies that Naver's previous filtering system had its own problems.
 No matter how well it tries, a main page edited by a few is dangerous.
 This has been transferred to the system and fundamentally handed over to each media outlet. This is because Naver has no intention of claiming to be a media organization.
 Naver's target is Google (whether it has the capability or not), not Daum.
 Selection and concentration. I believe they have correctly identified the target they need to focus on and invest resources in for future success.
 If they intended to play the role of a media organization, they would need to hire close to 30% journalists rather than nearly 50% developers.
 To an extreme, the "News Clustering" system recently opened in Naver Labs (a system that automatically organizes news issues).
 This might be the goal for Naver's news page.
 [http://news.search.naver.com/newscluster/](http://news.search.naver.com/newscluster/)
 
** 4) Increased responsibility of media outlets**
 Many users complain that when they click on a News Cast article, a news page filled with provocative advertisements appears.
 This is currently true, and many users are angry at Naver.
 While this is entirely the responsibility of the media outlets, users are criticizing Naver simply because it exposes these articles on its main page.
 However, this is an excessive demand on Naver.
 Media outlets are fundamentally just entities that want to tell their own stories, just like netizens.
 Intervening in that would be nothing short of violence, like forcing netizens' edits. Along with their own self-purification efforts,
 they now bear the responsibility of directly facing netizens' criticism and participating as agents to further improve the internet world.
 Since the page has been opened to those who used to post provocative articles with only changed titles, trying to grab more attention from behind the portal, they must make self-purification efforts themselves. After the opening, I've seen that the news being cast actually has an overwhelmingly large number of comments compared to other news pages, and some pages seem to have traffic issues as predicted.
 Now the ball is in the court of the media outlets. The reason is simple: portals have no desire to be media organizations, nor do they have the capability.
 If netizens still expect portals to do something, how is that different from agreeing with the Grand National Party's "digital evil laws"?
 We must believe in the power of self-purification on the internet. And that power rightly belongs to netizens, not portals.
 
**5) Increased rights and responsibilities of netizens**
 The stage is already set. It's time for netizens' voices to grow louder.
 The opening of such a portal's main page seems to be Korea's first attempt to create such a diverse web environment.
 Whether this will bring a new web paradigm or become just another page overflowing with spam depends on the voices and actions of netizens.

Aaron walked for about half a day. Suddenly, a sense of unease began to creep in. It was already the Forest of Spirits, yet the trees were still losing their lush green. The Forest of Spirits should never lose its natural vibrancy. Aaron began to feel anxious, fearing his worries might come true.

Before he knew it, a village came into view. Aaron slowly walked towards it. The closer he got, the more the village looked different from before. As Aaron entered the village, the first thing he felt was the smell of death. Human skulls and bones lay scattered everywhere, and houses were broken or burned. He pushed open the door of one house, and it fell off weakly.

Inside, a skeleton lay slumped against the wall, still holding a plow. Aaron approached to examine the skeleton more closely. It seemed to have died fighting hard, and there was a large tooth mark on its skull.

"Ugh... This far... What on earth happened? Could it be, Auntie and Lishia too?"

Aaron left that house and went to Dina's house, where he had lived with Elleasal.
The house was already burned down to its bare frame, as if it had never been a clean home.
Aaron felt hollow. First, the place he had lived in for years was like this, and second, his last glimmer of hope of finding light magic had vanished. Aaron anxiously rummaged through the burned remains, hoping to find at least a skeleton. He searched until evening, but only found a few familiar household items. Aaron found a small comfort in the fact that no skeletons were found. In Aaron's memory, Dina was certainly strong enough.

By then, the evening sun was setting over the western mountains, and the sunset was painting the sky.
Aaron soon dusted himself off and decided to move. At night, the village was open on all sides, making it a bad place for Aaron to camp alone due to the risk of being ambushed. Aaron walked for a while, entered the forest, and chose a spot surrounded by rocks as his campsite. Aaron first lit a fire. With a fire burning, at least lower-level monsters would not approach. After lighting the fire, Aaron set up a makeshift tent with the equipment he had. The small one-person tent barely protected him from the wind and dew.

After setting up camp, Aaron, with the skilled hands of a hunter's son, caught a pheasant and placed it over the fire. Aaron took out a book he carried and opened it. The book contained records of all the investigations Aaron had conducted so far.

Aaron was now at a loss as to where to go. There was nowhere left to investigate. As Aaron continued to compare his records and maps, the pheasant meat he had placed over the fire was cooking, and the sun had set behind the mountains. As it was now dark and he couldn't see the book well, Aaron put it aside and picked up the pheasant. The moment he took a joyful bite, he heard a strange sound.

'Is it a monster again? Did the monsters from yesterday follow me?'

Aaron grabbed his sword and stealthily investigated. Aaron walked towards the sound.
'Rustle.' There was definitely another movement.
Aaron's hunter's instinct told him it wasn't a small animal based on the sound. Aaron approached the wooded area where something was clearly moving. Discovering something large crouching in the trees, Aaron leaped in, striking down with his sword.

"Hiyah!"

The moment Aaron brought his sword down to strike what was there, the target that appeared in his sight was not a monster, but a person.

"Kyaaak!"

Aaron's sword, which rarely missed its target, seemed to react to the target's scream and stopped right in front of it. Aaron confirmed it was a person and was surprised again to find it was a girl. Aaron's sword stopped right above her, and she had her arms raised as if to block the sharp blade, her head turned, eyes tightly shut, trembling like a frightened rabbit. Aaron and the girl remained in that posture for a moment. Soon, Aaron bowed his head deeply and sighed. Then, sheathing his sword, he said,

"Whew~ It was a person? That was close."

"Are you alright? There was no sign of anyone, so I thought it was a monster."

Aaron said to her in a worried voice as he sheathed his sword.
She looked up and stared intently at Aaron.
The campfire Aaron had lit a little distance away allowed him to see her face and appearance. She had a pretty face, but her clothes and face looked a bit dirty, as if she had been through some hardship recently. When their eyes met, Aaron felt somehow embarrassed. Her eyes were glistening with tears, perhaps from the shock earlier. Aaron felt very sorry for having startled her.

"Ah... I'm... sorry about earlier. I really didn't know it was a person..."

Aaron apologized and approached her.
But just as Aaron got close enough to touch her, the girl suddenly called Aaron's name and leaped into his arms, hugging him.
Aaron was enveloped by the soft scent of a grown woman.
Aaron was startled by the girl's actions. Although he was old enough to know women, having wandered around, he still didn't know them. He knew no women other than a few barmaids who were information sources in villages.
Or perhaps he didn't want to know them. Including a woman in his destiny was a burden for him, who had lived the destiny of the Warrior of Light until now.
The girl hugged Aaron and began to sob.
Aaron couldn't help but be flustered by a grown lady he didn't know suddenly hugging him like this.

"Sniff. Aaron... You're back. Sniff, sniff."
"H-hey. Who are you...?"

As Aaron, bewildered, spoke to her, she finally pulled away from his embrace.
"Ah... Aaron... Don't you know me? Did you forget so soon? You said you'd come back."

Aaron looked at her closely.
Long, straight black hair, a red ribbon, and eyes still glistening with unshed tears. Only then did a child come to Aaron's mind.

"Oh? Lishia?"
"Yes, that's right."

Only then did she smile.
Until now, even as he came to Nahaliel, Aaron's memories of Lishia and Dina were exactly as they were when he left. Aaron now realized how foolish he had been. Lishia had grown up. She was no longer the little girl from before, but had suddenly appeared before him as a grown woman.

"I cried again. I said I wouldn't cry."
Lishia said, wiping her tears.
"Let's go to the camp first."

Aaron took Lishia to his camp. Aaron sat Lishia near the fire and tore off some pheasant meat to give to her. Lishia took it and, perhaps hungry, began to eat it quickly.

"Eat slowly, Lishia. You'll get indigestion."
Aaron gave Lishia his water skin. Lishia looked at Aaron shyly, smiled gently, and took the water to drink.

"What do you mean you said you wouldn't cry?"
"I promised Mom I wouldn't cry... but I keep crying."
"Pfft~ It would be strange if you, a crybaby, didn't cry. I recognized you by your eyes."
"What? My eyes?"
"Your eyes that are always crying."
"Hmph. I'm really not going to cry."
Lishia still spoke in a childish tone.

"But what happened to the village?"
Then Lishia spoke quietly and slowly.
"It was a month ago. Mom suddenly gave me two small books and some food and told me to practice magic in the cave on that mountain over there. She said it was training... First, I took one book and faithfully followed Mom's instructions. It had one light magic spell written in it. But the other book didn't have any stories about magic. It was just full of strange records..."

"What? Light magic?"
"Oh. Aaron, do you know about light magic? Most people don't know about it, they say."
"Yes. Will you teach me what kind of magic it is later?"
"Whew~ Okay. Later...
So, after learning that one magic spell, I came home and found the village like this... The house was burned down, and all I found in the house was this necklace of Mom's... What happened to her... I cried so much... Now I'm tired of crying..."
Lishia fiddled with the black stone hexagonal star-shaped necklace around her neck.
"What do you think happened to my mom?"
Lishia said this and started sniffling again. Aaron comforted Lishia. Then Lishia grabbed Aaron again and started crying. Aaron, even though it was Lishia, felt a little embarrassed.

"Stop crying. She's probably fine. Auntie is strong, isn't she?"
Lishia wiped her tears and said,
"Yes, I promised Mom too, I shouldn't cry."
"But do you just hug any man like that?"
When Aaron chided her, Lishia was startled, let go of Aaron, and pouted.
"It's not like that, really."
Aaron looked at Lishia, who had grown up but was still like a child.
"Then how have you been since then? What about food?"
Lishia doodled on the ground and replied,
"I ate mountain berries, slept in the cave, and so on. There were still animal friends left in that forest over there... I had someone to talk to."
"Why didn't you go to another village?"
"You said you'd come."
"Huh~ What made you believe me and wait?"
"You came anyway..."
After saying that, she was silent for a moment, then Lishia replied again.
"Actually, it's not that, I just don't know at all. I've never been to another village... and I haven't seen many other people..."
Aaron was surprised.
"What? You've never been anywhere else?"
It was natural for Lishia to be naive. She had been stuck in this village without friends her age.
"Whew~ So, what are you going to do now?"
Lishia kept drawing and erasing something on the ground.
"I don't know. I'll just follow Aaron."
Lishia replied simply.
"What on earth should I do? Ugh~ I don't know. First, we need to get out of here."
Aaron suddenly saw what Lishia had drawn.
"Oh? What's that?"
Lishia was drawing something small. The drawing was a pattern symbolizing light, and it was an essential pattern for a light magic circle.
"It's the Emblem of Light, isn't it?"
"That's right."
"Where did you find it? Is it part of the magic circle for the magic you learned?"
"It is, in a way."

"This is just the cover of this book."
Lishia pulled a small book from her skirt pocket.
"It's a book Mom gave me... No magic is written in it, and it's full of strange words."
"Let me see it."
Aaron took the book. He opened it. It was clearly written in the Light Script. Aaron began to decipher the book, word by word.
"God... bestowed... Light... and..."
"Darkness is the strongest power in this world."
Lishia continued Aaron's words, rattling them off.
"Huh? How did you do that?"
"Why can't you even read that?"
"How do you know the Light Script? Where did you learn it?"
"Learn it? I've never learned letters from anyone. Don't letters just read themselves from the beginning?"
"What?"
Aaron was dumbfounded.
"Writing is something you learn."
"That's strange. It just reads itself to me..."
"Don't lie. You must have learned it sometime. Anyway, can you read this for me?"
"Hmph~ Who's a liar? Why should I read this for Aaron?"
Lishia bristled at being called a liar and spoke coldly to Aaron.
Aaron was flustered.
"Ah... right, right. You're not a liar. So please read this."
"Hmph~ No."
Lishia kept pouting until Aaron practically begged her, and she reluctantly began to read.
The content was an introduction to the Civilization of Light and a story about its legends.
Lishia began to read the book.
"In the beginning, the Civilization of Light emerged. They possessed immense power, and with that power, they developed towards a peaceful utopia, according to the will of the Creator God. However, a great war broke out among the Civilizations of Light. In that war, a Civilization of Darkness, which rebelled against them, eventually arose. This civilization began to create a culture of conflict and destruction, and they worshipped things that opposed God. The two civilizations clashed, and the Civilization of Darkness, which only brought about destruction, emerged victorious. The Civilization of Darkness annihilated all Civilizations of Light and covered the entire world in darkness and evil.
Thereafter, evil ruled the world. The sun lost its light, and the sky was no longer blue. The land also ceased to bestow its fruits upon humans, and the denizens of darkness worshipped corruption, pleasure, chaos, and the products of evil, and they consumed them. They summoned the Dark Lord, and with the power these entities granted, they dominated the world and other races.
Other races were forced to live underground to avoid the denizens of the Civilization of Darkness, and they earnestly called upon the names of God. Eventually, God intervened and sent down the power of Light. However, that power found it difficult to completely eradicate the power of Darkness. The power, which possessed its own will, ultimately sealed the Dark Lord and restored light to the world.
But that light expended all its power in sealing the Dark Lord. Eventually, that light also lost its will, and its power was divided and permeated this world.
The Dark Lord is not completely gone. Whenever evil exists in the world, and its power grows, he will be resurrected.
God knew this and planned that whenever the power of Light, which had permeated the world, was needed, He would designate one person as the Warrior of Light and save the world through him. This conflict between darkness and light is the origin of all magic, and this legend will repeat eternally, balancing the world as long as the power of magic exists in this world.
This is conveyed to future generations: Darkness will not appear unless the power of darkness grows in the world. The power of darkness is ultimately self-inflicted. That power will destroy everything.
Our ancestors committed foolish acts. They created the Civilization of Darkness amidst a great war, killing and fighting each other. Forgetting their purpose... Ultimately, that responsibility fell upon our ancestors, and now, neither the Civilization of Light nor the Civilization of Darkness remains. "
Lishia read it all the way through in a clear, resonant voice. Aaron, listening, nodded and replied.
"I think I can finally synthesize all the fragmented knowledge I've had until now."
Aaron mumbled.
"Hold on. There's still a lot... Hmm... There's something interesting drawn here. It looks like a map. A temple, a village, a church... Where is this map from?"
"Huh? What? A map?"
Aaron snatched the book.
"Hmph~ What the heck, Aaron! You asked me to read it!"
"This is a map of Dragonia. And an ancient one... from the era of the Civilization of Light... I might finally be able to find the temple."
"So what about it?!"
Lishia said indifferently.
"Oh? Are you sulking again?"
"I don't know."
Aaron continued to flip through the book. After a bit of searching, Aaron suddenly opened a page and his hand stopped.
"Lishia. Do you know who wrote this?"
"I don't know."
Lishia was still sitting turned away, looking indifferent.
"Your father wrote it." "........."
At that, Lishia said nothing.
"Lishia?" Aaron called again.
She spoke in a small, trembling voice.
"I don't know. Really... I can't remember Dad's face... He seemed like a kind person... but not since I was four..."
Aaron approached Lishia. He showed her a page in the book. Faintly etched there was the Pangaea script 'Eldge'.
"I had forgotten... even Father's name... Mother kept waiting for Father..."
Lishia replied, her voice trembling again. Aaron comforted her and then said,
"Phew~ That's enough. Stop now. Your mother will be fine. Eat this, and sleep over there."
Aaron pointed to a small tent. Lishia gobbled down the pheasant meat and then collapsed weakly into the tent. It seemed she hadn't had a proper place to sleep or food to eat before meeting Aaron. Aaron felt pity for Lishia.
Aaron used a rock as a pillow, spread leaves on the ground, lay down, and covered himself with his cloak. Then he closed his tired eyes.
Just then, Lishia's voice was heard. It came from across the tent.
"Aaron, if you're sleeping outside, let's sleep together."
Aaron, with his eyes closed, was flustered.
'What on earth is she thinking?'
Aaron still felt sorry for Lishia, who was like a child. She had never been anywhere else, nor had she ever talked to anyone else...
"You don't even know about boys and girls, you really are a fool, just like Anel said."
"What does that mean?"
"When boys and girls grow up, they shouldn't sleep together."
".........."
After a long silence, Lishia spoke softly in a gentle voice.
"Aaron... thank you..."
"I told you to call me Oppa..."
Lishia seemed to have fallen asleep, as no reply came.

Year 26 of the Dragonia Calendar
Throughout the deep forests of Dragonia lay abandoned cities. Most of these neglected ruins, symbolizing the glory of a bygone era, boasted magnificent appearances and grand scales. However, today, they were eroded by wind and rain, losing their form, and overgrown with weeds, making their locations difficult to find. These ruins, said to have been built by a civilization that suddenly vanished long ago, were shunned by ordinary travelers who believed the dead souls of the city resided there, and were instead used as hideouts by bandits and animals. In one such ruin, amidst the piles of rubble that still preserved a fraction of its former splendor, two young men were diligently searching for something.

"Phew~ Teacher, it seems it's not here either."
Ellezar, who was examining the ruins from a distance, called out.
"Aaron! Come here for a moment."
Aaron ran over and saw Ellezar holding a broken stone tablet.
"Look at this. It's the emblem of light, isn't it?"
"Hmm... it is. After searching for two years, I've become an expert on it."
"It seems this is definitely a remnant civilization of the People of Light too..."
"Isn't there a temple somewhere around here?"
"Well, phew~ we've found seven ruins of light already, but we haven't discovered a temple yet. If only Eldge, that friend, were here..."
"He was a wizard who could use light magic?"
"That's right. And Lisia's father... Thanks to him, we were able to defeat the Dark Tribe who used dark magic. He would have known. If we find a temple, there would be records of magic there."
"I suppose so. All the light magic we've found in ancient texts so far has only been enough to summon light spirits. And even if we summon them, we can't control them, so it's useless."
"First, let's decipher this stone tablet."
Aaron pulled out a small book and began deciphering it, comparing it to the tablet. After deciphering for a while, Aaron spoke with a resigned tone.
"Tsk... it's probably useless to decipher this."
"I see. This is probably just a phrase praising the god of light..."
Just then, something wrapped around Aaron's foot and tripped him.
"Ack! What is this!"
Aaron was lifted into the air, hanging upside down. A giant plant held his foot high with its vine-like tendrils. As Aaron tried to cast a spell, the carnivorous plant quickly wrapped its other tendrils around his entire body. It was dragging him towards the large red flower at the center of the plant. Aaron tried to move, but being upside down and completely enveloped, he couldn't even cast a simple spell.
"How did this thing get behind us? I didn't feel anything..."
No sooner had Ellezar expressed his surprise than the plant attacked Ellezar as well. The plant's tendrils persistently tried to grab Ellezar, sometimes even trying to stab him like a knife. Ellezar dodged the attacks, jumped towards Aaron, and cut the tendril holding Aaron.
Aaron instantly felt his body loosen, and as the tendrils wrapped around him disappeared, he could see again. The moment he thought he had landed lightly, his feet felt strange. He had landed in the center of the red flower. A burning sensation spread from his feet, and the petals were closing. As soon as Aaron noticed his shoes melting, he lunged and barely managed to escape before the petals closed completely. Ellezar was cutting off the monster flower's tendrils one by one.
"Ah... it's hot... Damn it. These shoes are ruined, and I just bought them!"
"What are you talking about? You almost got eaten. Hurry up and weed."
Aaron then grumbled continuously about his shoes and joined in attacking the carnivorous plant. After cutting for a while, Aaron got annoyed and shouted.
"Teacher! Get out of the way!"
As Ellezar retreated from the plant, Aaron quickly drew a magic circle on the ground with his sword, stood on it, and shouted.
"Uriel!"
The plant let out a pathetic shriek and collapsed, engulfed in flames.
"Aaron, are you alright?"
Ellezar asked Aaron, who was standing in the middle of the magic circle, breathing heavily.
Aaron replied in a weak voice.
"Huff, huff, I'm alright... Such a big spell is tiring."
"You idiot. You used such an energy-draining spell just because you were annoyed? And you're not even good at magic..."
"Still, I can fight a few more. Though I won't be able to use magic..."
"You fool. What if there were really a few more?"
No sooner had Ellezar finished speaking than he somersaulted sideways, dodging an attack. A monstrous earthworm had suddenly lunged. In an instant, monstrous earthworms appeared everywhere.
"Ugh... my mouth is always getting me into trouble... After pulling out weeds, now it's pest extermination. This isn't farming or anything."
Ellezar said that and fought the earthworms. Aaron, though a bit tired from the previous spell, drew his sword and fought them. They weren't particularly difficult opponents. After killing about 10 of them, Aaron's stamina was running out. To avoid being attacked from behind, Aaron moved towards Ellezar and fought with Ellezar behind him.
After fighting for a while, Ellezar and Aaron stood back to back.
"Teacher, don't you have any stamina potions?"
"We used them all last time. And unless it's magic, relying on such drugs too much will lead to addiction."
"I wouldn't mind being addicted if I had some now. It seems like it'll be hard to last if we keep going like this..."
"Then, there's no choice. I'm not very good at healing magic, but..."
Ellezar cast a spell on Aaron, restoring some of his stamina.
"Still, with this much, I think I can keep fighting."
Aaron jumped up and cut down several of them at once.
"It's strange! I can't believe we didn't notice so many monsters coming near us..."
Ellezar said, shattering the body of the last one he was fighting with magic-infused sword. Soon, Aaron also finished off his last one.
"Phew~ We finally got rid of them all. Huff, huff."
Both Aaron and Ellezar seemed quite exhausted.
"Ugh... I'm definitely tired now. We should head to a nearby village quickly."
Ellezar said, his face strained and breathless. Ellezar and Aaron gathered their belongings.
Just as they were about to leave, a tremendous wind blew. Aaron and Ellezar crouched low.
"Ugh... what now? It's one thing after another... Aaron! If anything happens, we run!"
However, as Ellezar said this, he instinctively sensed that this was no ordinary enemy. The unsettling feeling flowing through Ellezar's body was completely different from when he faced monsters. The immense wind obscured their vision with a dusty yellow loess.
'What on earth is it?'
The moment Aaron thought this, something large emerged from the dust storm. And he saw a fireball shooting towards him. The event was so sudden that Aaron was struck squarely in the chest by the fireball, and the force sent him crashing into the piles of ruins.
"Are you alright? Aaron!"
Ellezar approached Aaron, wary of the object in the dust storm. Aaron struggled out of the rubble, stumbled, and coughed a few times.
"Cough, I'm alright... Ugh, it's hot..."
The clothes on his chest, including the thick leather armor he wore underneath, were burnt black, exposing his chest, and he seemed to have suffered burns.
"What is that?"
"Ugh... I couldn't see it clearly. In my current state, I don't think I can defeat that thing. The injury seems quite severe."
The dust storm was gradually subsiding. Within it, something large and black began to reveal its outline. Ellezar and Aaron were instantly surprised.
"A dragon? What? How did this happen? A dragon attacking me..."
Ellezar recognized the dragon.
"Th-that's the Dragon of Envy?"
"Huh? Isn't that the dragon my father killed?"
"Yes. That's right. How did this happen?"
The black dragon let out a roar. It seemed its teleportation had just ended. The dragon turned its massive head towards Ellezar and grinned with a hideous smile.
"So, it was you, Dragon of Courage, who was with the Champion of Light. Remarkable, both of you. To have so cleanly dispatched the monsters I sent..."
Its rough, booming voice echoed.
"You, who abandoned your racial duty, cursed by the elders to never return to your original form and exiled, what business do you have with me!"
Ellezar scoffed.
The Dragon of Envy then laughed loudly and said,
"Hmph. Racial duty? Why should I uphold such a thing? For whom? To pledge loyalty to those esteemed gods and elders? Are you saying we should continue to be played by the gods' game called 'oracle,' without thinking about the future of our race? Throw away such ideals! We are far superior to humans, so why do we have even less self-respect than humans? And, the elders, who feared my power, ultimately couldn't kill me. Look. Even in this state, I survived, didn't I?"
Ellezar clenched his fists and observed the Dragon of Envy. A large scar on the Dragon of Envy's neck... that was clearly left by Halhas when he killed the Dragon of Envy. Ellezar had clearly seen a tremendous amount of blood gush out and its head fall off at that time.
"Don't provoke my anger! Why are you here? And how did you survive!"

.

Aaron traveled with Eleazar, meeting many people and seeing many things. Aaron's eyes welled up as he passed near his lost old hometown, and he also fought monsters.
As he did so, Aaron gradually began to forget about his destiny. Or perhaps he hadn't cared about it from the start. At least, not for a wanderer like him. After every tense battle, fatigue would set in, leaving little time to think about anything else. Thus, another two long years were spent traveling to the land of Caledonia. Aaron, now nineteen, had grown so much that he looked like an adult.
The weather was getting colder. Not because it was winter, but because they were heading further north. Aaron had arrived at Lagis Village, the northernmost point in Dragonia. Most of the villagers, who spent the majority of the year in the snow, were people who had lived there long before the Pangaea people arrived. To the north of the village, Mount Suria stood as a barrier. They held the mountain sacred, and because of it, no one dared to venture further north. It was said that the Dragon Temple lay beyond the mountain. Only a few curious travelers and well-trained soldiers had ever attempted to cross the mountain, but very few had actually claimed to have reached the Dragon Temple, and it was rumored that only a more desolate snowfield stretched out on the other side.
Aaron bought winter clothing at the village general store to climb Mount Suria.
This heavy winter clothing, made of several layers of wool and waterproofed with leather and glue, felt like walking wrapped in a blanket. He entered the tavern where Eleazar was waiting. Aaron looked around for a seat, found Eleazar's, and approached.
Just then, he felt a strange gaze. After a long journey, his sense of others' gazes had become extraordinary. Aaron looked in the direction of the gaze and saw a boy staring intently at him. However, sensing no malice or anything unusual, Aaron soon ignored it and went to Eleazar's seat.
“Teacher. I bought it here.”
Aaron came to Eleazar, who was sitting in the tavern, carrying the thick fur clothes.
“How much did you pay?” “300 shekels.”
“You got it cheap.”
“I haggled a bit.”
“Alright, let's go.”
Aaron and Eleazar stood up from their seats. Just then, the boy who had been staring at Aaron earlier approached as if he had been waiting.
“Brother, wait a moment. I've been watching you from the side. Are you going up Mount Suria?”
“Uh... yes.”
“Then please take me with you.”
“What?”
Aaron asked with a bewildered expression.
“What are you going to do up there?”
“I'm going to get the Flower of Life on the mountaintop.”
“What? The Flower of Life? What's that?”
“They say it can save anyone who's sick.”
“What do you need it for?”
The boy hesitated, unable to answer, then clenched his fists and replied in a slightly trembling voice.
“To save my sick mother. No doctor can save her.”
Just then, Eleazar interjected.
“Do you know that flower is Rimmon's flower?”
“Yes. I know.”
Aaron, wondering what they were talking about, asked.
“Wait. Just a moment. Teacher, what is Rimmon?”
“He's a spirit who claims to be the deity of Mount Suria. He's very nasty. If you get caught by him, you'll be in trouble.”
The boy pleaded with earnest eyes. Eleazar asked again.
“How exactly do you plan to find it alone? We're just crossing the mountain pass, not climbing to the summit.”
“Just take me there. The adults at the village entrance stop people from going up the mountain.”
“But we can't help you find your flower, can we? That's not a place for a child to go alone.”
Eleazar asked.
“Just let me pass through there. I'll take care of the rest myself.”
Aaron looked into the boy's eyes. Eyes that seemed to hold a terrifying resolve... Aaron envied the boy. The boy who could do something for his mother... What could he have done for his own mother? He recalled his birth mother, brutally murdered right before his eyes, and his adoptive mother, burned to death.
“Shall we take him?”
Aaron, seeing the boy's eyes, couldn't bring himself to refuse.
“What are you talking about?”
“This child is serious.”
“Serious or not, it's no place for a child to go alone. And I have no intention of helping.”
“I'll take responsibility.”
“Aaron. Can you take responsibility for that?”
“Yes.”
Aaron didn't want to make the boy's resolve futile.
“You might get the child killed.”
“I don't care! I won't die. Absolutely.”
The boy answered before Aaron did. Then, Eleazar retorted.
“Even a child must take responsibility for his words.”
So, in the end, they took the boy and passed through the village entrance. The villagers tried to stop them from going up, but after Eleazar spoke with the village chief, the people readily let them go.
Once they were on the mountain path, the atmosphere was completely different from the village. An intense cold bit at their skin, as if it were some kind of boundary. Aaron pulled his thick clothes tighter. The path was narrow, so they walked in single file, with the boy in front of Aaron, and Eleazar leading. Normally, they would have talked, but perhaps due to the cold, they said nothing. They had to cover every part of their faces as much as possible.
After a short while, the path forked. One path led to the summit, and the other crossed the mountain pass. Eleazar, who was leading, unhesitatingly took the path to the pass and ascended. The boy, who was following, watched Eleazar's retreating figure for a moment, then chose the path leading to the summit and went up. Aaron saw the two of them take different paths.
Aaron watched the boy's retreating figure. The small child steadfastly walked his own path even in the intense cold. Aaron felt that Eleazar was a bit heartless. If left alone, the boy might die. No matter how strong a child's resolve, a child is still a child...
Aaron wanted to help the boy. After a moment's thought, Aaron followed the boy up. The boy had already entered a narrow path along a cliff. The path looked very slippery. The boy hesitated for a moment, then carefully took another step. After walking a bit, the boy turned around, saw Aaron, and then strode towards him and spoke.
“Why are you following me?”
“I just want to help... and besides, you're still a child, aren't you?”
“I don't need help. I've lived like this all my life...”
The boy turned sharply and continued up the mountain. Aaron found himself smiling, as the boy's demeanor somehow reminded him of his own childhood. Aaron leisurely whistled and followed closely behind this time.
Just then, a thunderous roar echoed through the mountain from somewhere. The boy, walking on the narrow path, was startled and almost fell off the cliff, but Aaron quickly grabbed him, narrowly saving him from falling.
“What in the world was that sound?”
Aaron said, pulling the boy up.
“Th-thank you.”
The boy replied, blushing at having received help.
“But I still don't know your name. What is it?”
“Isaac. And you, brother?”
“I'm Aaron.”
Isaac said thank you and continued up the mountain. The boy seemed unaccustomed to saying thank you. Aaron felt sorry for the boy, thinking he must not be used to kindness from others due to a lack of parental care. Yet, the small child's steps looked so brave, making him feel proud at the same time.
After a while, the cliff path ended and the road widened a bit, with a large wooden house by the side of the road.
“What's that?”
The boy discovered it first and asked.
“I don't know. Looks like a log cabin?”
The size of the house was enormous. The door was twice a person's height, and everything was abnormally large. The boy looked at the house with curiosity, while Aaron, thinking that whatever lived there must be very large, became wary of his surroundings.
‘Do giants live here?’
Just then, Isaac screamed.
A huge bear was coming down the path from the other side. Its body was so large that it looked twice the size of a normal bear. Isaac was terrified.
“Is everything in this area this big?!”
Aaron stepped in front of Isaac and drew his sword, and the bear charged even more fiercely towards Aaron. Just as he thought the bear was attacking, he heard something cut through the wind. With that loud whooshing sound, the bear collapsed lifelessly with a loud thud right in front of Aaron's feet. Aaron was puzzled.
Aaron cautiously approached the bear and saw a massive double-bladed axe embedded in its back, staining the white snow crimson with blood.
Just then, the ground rumbled with heavy thuds. Something else was rapidly leaping down from higher up the mountain. It looked human-like but was much larger and covered in fur. Its speed was also incredible. Aaron immediately sensed that this creature was more dangerous than the bear.
The monster was armed. Recently, intelligent monsters had begun to appear. They were more malicious and much harder to deal with because they were armed.
Because of this, Aaron thought it would be better to face a dim-witted bear. However, the monster did not attack Aaron; instead, it stopped running in front of the fallen bear's corpse. Then, it slung the bear over its shoulder and looked towards Aaron. As the furry monster's large eyes glinted and stared at Isaac, the terrified Isaac hid behind Aaron, and Aaron tightened his grip on his sword.

“Am I small? I think you’re just excessively big!”
Aaron shouted.
“Is that so? Hahahaha.”
The mountain echoed as the monster let out a loud, booming laugh. The sound was so immense that the entire mountain reverberated, threatening to cause an avalanche at any moment.
“Hey! Stop it! What if there’s an avalanche? That loud noise earlier was you too, wasn’t it?”
“Follow me. I’ll invite you to my house.”
Aaron was flustered by the sudden invitation, but he also found it amusing.
“Brother. Let’s go. He doesn’t seem like a bad monster.”
The child, seemingly amused by the monster, pestered them to go.
Aaron was worried that Eleazar might be waiting, but sensing that Isaac was a little tired, he decided to rest for a while before continuing and accepted the invitation. The enormous wooden house was the monster’s home.
Inside the house were huge chairs, a bed, a table, and even chairs of normal human size, perhaps made for guests. The house was very warm and, surprisingly, decorated with charming little trinkets.
The furry monster, despite his size, brewed tea and brought it over.
“What’s your name, mister?”
The little boy asked the monster.
“Bedrabah.”
“How long have you lived here alone?”
Aaron asked.
“I don’t know. Three years since I came back to life. I was dead. And when I woke up, I was on this mountain.”
“What on earth do you mean? Dead?”
Aaron flinched in surprise. The monster then picked up a teacup that looked incredibly small in his huge hand, sipped his tea, and said,
“Hmm… I don’t know how it happened… I think I died 2000 years ago… Based on conversations with passersby. Of course, they were surprised and ran away. Haha.”
Bedrabah was formidable in size and strength, but surprisingly simple-minded. His speech was also childlike. Then, he suddenly spoke with a gloomy expression.
“I was born a giant and did many bad things in my life. I killed people… I was the greatest demon of that era. But because of my mother, I became good. Still, the villagers killed me…”
Bedrabah briefly recalled his past.
His mother, 2000 years ago, lived with the dishonor of being raped by a Nephilim giant while still a virgin. She was an object of scorn in the village and relied solely on Bedrabah, having no one else to depend on. As he grew up, he began to think of revenge on people for his mother. With immense power, he was a filial son to his mother, but as a twisted young man, he became a demon to the world. Later, at his mother’s earnest request, he changed his ways, but the world did not acknowledge it. While he was sleeping at home, he was tied up in the village square by the villagers. His mother tried to defend and protect him until the end, but the people, with devilish faces, dragged him away. At that moment, though he was big and strong, the faces of those small people were truly terrifying. He wondered if his own face had looked like that when he committed evil deeds. And then, the last thing he saw and felt was people throwing stones at him with all sorts of insults, and their spears and swords piercing his body. He screamed in a terrible pain he had never experienced before. After that, 2000 years passed without him remembering anything.
“Did you have a mother?”
Isaac asked Bedrabah, who was lost in thought and staring blankly.
Bedrabah was startled, came to his senses, and replied,
“…Yes. She was the one who truly loved me… Someone like me… I wonder what happened to her after I died… But it’s the first time a little kid like you has climbed this mountain. Sometimes adventurers climb this mountain, but…”
“Because of my mother. To find the Flower of Life…”
“Really? You’re truly a filial son.”
At those words, the image of his mother was once again imprinted on Bedrabah’s mind.
“I have to go now. Thank you very much. I’m in a bit of a hurry.”
Aaron was worried that if he didn’t resolve this quickly and leave, he would fall behind Eleazar, so he wanted to hurry.
“Oh? In that case, why don’t I help you? I want to help Isaac for his mother.”
Seeing the child, Bedrabah was reminded of his mother and wanted to help.
“I’d be grateful for your help. You seem to know this mountain well.”
At that, Bedrabah rejoiced like a child at the prospect of being able to help Isaac.
Aaron, Isaac, and Bedrabah climbed the mountain together. Bedrabah, who had lived on this mountain for a long time, led the way with a large double-bladed axe on his back, striding purposefully, and Isaac followed behind him.
As the snow deepened, the distance between the three gradually widened. When Isaac found it difficult to walk, Bedrabah turned back, lifted Isaac up, and carried him on his shoulders.
“Wow~ It’s really high! I can see the village where I used to live.”
They were already quite high up the mountain, but for Isaac, perched on Bedrabah’s neck, it felt like he had climbed even higher than the mountain itself, and laughter, like the meaning of his name, never left him.
“Haha. That ridge over there is where I hunt. There are many wild goats there, and do you know how funny it is when I herd them and they leap and bound?”
Bedrabah seemed incredibly strong, but also innocent. Perhaps because of this, he seemed to connect well with the young Isaac. Isaac and Bedrabah continued to chatter as they climbed the mountain, and Aaron watched them fondly, thinking they looked like a father and son. However, as the snow deepened, Aaron also found it difficult to walk, and he felt it was hard to keep up with Bedrabah’s pace.
“Go a little slower!”
Aaron shouted, wiping sweat from his brow, towards Bedrabah. Keeping up with them became so strenuous that he didn’t feel cold at all.
“Brother Aaron, do you want a ride too?”
“No thanks. I’m past the age for piggyback rides.”
Then Bedrabah stomped back towards Aaron and suddenly lifted him up.
“Aargh!”
With immense strength, Aaron was lifted and placed on his shoulder.
“Hahaha. Don’t be shy. There’s plenty of room.”
Aaron felt a little embarrassed for a grown young man to be riding on someone’s shoulder, but thinking this way was much faster, he reluctantly replied,
“Well… if that’s the case, please.”
