Aaron was excited when the wizard from the fairy tale appeared before his eyes.
'A righteous wizard... Now she will defeat them all.'
Aaron looked at her with awe.
Halhas was jolted awake by the pain of an injury he hadn't felt in a long time, and memories of the past resurfaced. The sensation of the one wielding the sword once again stirred tension in his mind.
"Anania! You wicked thing! What is this outrage!"
Vidia's angry shout at the wizard cut through the air.
Aaron was puzzled.
'Why is Mom stepping in? And does Mom know that wizard?'
Too many things Aaron couldn't understand were happening.
Anania, upon seeing Vidia and Halhas, spoke with surprise in her eyes.
"Hoho, how interesting. My subordinate, who went to get provisions, called me, and it turns out Princess Vidia of Ceres and General Halhas, the Commander-in-Chief of Ceres, were here. I couldn't find you no matter how much I searched..."
Vidia, not to be outdone, also spoke with an angry voice.
"Go away, now!"
"This is the first time something so amusing has happened, isn't it? Who would have imagined that a princess exiled from the kingdom and a traitorous commander-in-chief would marry and live happily ever after?"
Anania sneered and laughed heartily. Then Halhas shouted.
"Ridiculous. All the Ceres soldiers have become fools. They weren't this incompetent when I was around... And furthermore, they never plundered!
And I am no longer a general, and Vidia is no longer a princess! I don't want to be involved in your bloody war!"
"Anyway, you two will die here. If you're alive, my position will be in danger..."
Anania lightly descended to the ground.
As Anania shouted "Sysmae!", a fireball formed in her hand.
"You talk too much. I have to get rid of you two anyway..."
Anania smiled slightly, looked at the fireball in her hand, and threw it at Vidia. Halhas instantly pushed Vidia aside and took the fireball.
As Halhas swung his sword, the sword's power dispersed the fireball, and Halhas immediately cast Ur (a flame spell), causing a red flame to extend from his sword like a living snake.
Anania easily dodged it. The soldier behind Anania was hit by the stream of fire, writhed in pain from the burns, trembled, and collapsed.
The moment Anania thought she had dodged, she saw Halhas's icy blue sword blade aimed at her. Anania, startled, stretched out her hand and, casting a spell, emitted a blue light. The light grazed Halhas's right shoulder, and Halhas's sword wounded Anania's chest. "Kyaak!" Anania cried out in surprise.
Halhas seemed to have been grazed by Anania's magic, but his right shoulder was completely frozen. Red blood seeped into the golden clothes covering Anania's chest.
"Damn it... To be hit by your magic... Age really shows."
Halhas said, looking at his right shoulder. As his right shoulder froze, he felt the nerves in his right arm dying, accompanied by extreme pain and cold. He knew that if he didn't take action quickly, his right arm would soon feel like nothing more than a cumbersome lump of flesh, beyond recovery.
"Oh... As expected, you're not someone to be underestimated. The Archmage of Ceres in such a state... Come out! Sargon!"
"It seems all the Ceres mages are dead. What kind of Archmage are you!"
Halhas shouted, gritting his teeth. Although he shouted with such vigor, he already felt like dropping his sword and rolling around due to the numerous large and small wounds all over his body and the pain in his shoulder. However, he knew well that if he did, everything would be over. He had too much to protect for that. Halhas took a ragged breath and gripped his sword tightly.
As Anania began to chant a summoning spell, a chilling wind began to blow.
Soon, with a roar, a red dragon appeared in the air with a white light.
Halhas clutched his frozen right shoulder and muttered in a low, angry voice.
"Damn woman, how could she summon a Dragon of Wrath..."
Halhas felt his cells dying due to the effects of Gora (ice magic) he had taken earlier. His right arm was already almost useless.
Smoke billowed from the red dragon's mouth, and its size was like three elephants stacked together. Its roar echoed through the mountains and forests.
Halhas calmly assessed the situation. No matter how painful, that was how Halhas had always done things in the past, and what he had learned to survive.
'The situation is utterly unfavorable. It's impossible to defeat a dragon alone. My body is already wounded beyond recovery, and I have no comrades to help. Furthermore, there's no retreat because of Vidia and Aaron. I must make a final stand here, no matter if my body breaks... I must resolve this as quickly as possible. The longer it drags on, the more disadvantageous it becomes. What I can do is...'
Halhas quickly racked his brain.
The dragon spewed immense flames. Halhas cast an ice magic spell and hurled it at the dragon. However, Halhas's ice magic only slightly weakened the dragon's fire and had little effect. Halhas seemed to dodge slightly, but he failed to move his right arm out of the way.
"Aargh~" Halhas's scream echoed.
"Hohoho" Anania laughed cruelly.
Halhas's right arm was horribly burned and became unsightly. It looked difficult for him to even hold a sword.
Despite this, Halhas suddenly leaped towards Anania, attempting close combat. Anania, as a mage, was weak in close combat. A flustered Anania hastily formed a defensive spell and then used a teleportation spell, Eliezer (spatial movement spell), to move a short distance away, escaping. Anania gasped for breath. Spatial movement seemed to be a difficult spell for Anania. Halhas did not miss that moment. To deliver a fatal blow, he imbued his sword with flame magic and flew at Anania.
However, the dragon instantly blocked Halhas's path. The dragon was faster than Halhas expected. The moment Halhas flinched in surprise, its massive tail struck Halhas. Having taken a direct hit without any defense while attacking Anania, he was brutally slammed into the ground, and another wave of pain engulfed Halhas. Halhas tried to stand up despite the pain, but he collapsed due to the excruciating pain rising from his leg. His leg seemed to be broken. He tried to survey the situation, but his eyes were already dimming, and all external sounds seemed to come from far away.
"Oh, you cunning one. Using the dragon's fire to move your arm, and putting me in this state... Hmph, you truly are a wonderful man. It would have been good if you had remained a general of Ceres..."
"Now, this is the end! Iwa (destruction spell)!" As Anania clasped her hands and chanted the spell, magic glowed in her hands.
Halhas no longer had the strength to move. He tried to lift his head to look at Anania, but his vision was blurry, and blood flowing from his forehead kept his eyes closing, and the thought of death began to surface. At this moment, if he could protect Vidia and Aaron, he would even sell his soul to the devil. He continuously called out God's name inwardly, but it felt somehow futile.
- Who do you pray for? -
A girl's question came to mind. His past flashed by like a continuous series of pictures.
His mother's face in his early childhood during the pioneering days, his own young self begging like a beggar and being ridiculed, his time as General Helon's confidant... the battle with the dragon... General of Ceres... his opposition to war... his affectionate times with Vidia and Aaron...
He recalled a young girl praying in a church. Kneeling demurely, she looked silently pure and beautiful in the light scattered through the church's stained glass. But she was a dignified princess of a nation. The boy watching her knew well that their social statuses were incomparable.
"I don't pray. There is no God on the battlefield. It would be truly dramatic if there were a God on the battlefield, but I am also saddened that it's not the case."
The boy answered the girl's question, toying with the sword at his waist. Then, the girl, as if greatly disappointed, continued.
"At this time, I pray for the people I know. I recall each person's face. The priest told me that if you put your earnest wish into it, it will come true, and that wish becomes strength and protects that person."
Then, she paused for a moment, seemed to hesitate, and asked again.
"May I pray for you?"
At that question, the boy's face showed embarrassment and confusion.
"Oh. No. Someone as insignificant as me..."
"Insignificant? You are special. My grandfather also said he liked you. And... I also..."
The girl trailed off.
"Huh?"
The boy asked back, surprised.
"Oh. No. I also... like you. Because you have outstanding skills at a young age. You're a good officer, more than capable, a sufficient force beyond expectation..."
The girl stammered, flustered, but her face was already flushed.
Halhas continuously called out to God. The pain throughout his body was already exceeding his sensory capacity. Then, amidst that painful sensation, he felt a warm touch. He felt someone with a warm body temperature embracing him as he lay collapsed. His eyes were already so swollen and messed up that he couldn't see. But he could feel her scent. He could never forget her, his first and last love.
"Vidia... No. Run away." The brave Halhas spoke in a piteous voice.
He had never felt so weak. He had always won, no matter how difficult it was...
"How amusing. I was going to kill you anyway..." Anania sneered.
Vidia whispered to him in a small, trembling, beautiful voice.
"No. If you die, I die too. How can you defeat that dragon alone... You know better. Because you fought those dragons... You..."

"I was only eighteen. I fell for you when I saw you enter like a triumphant general. You smiled at me."
"Heh heh, back then, you were just a fifteen-year-old girl."
Halhas coughed as if in pain.
Holding such a Halhas, tears welled up in Vidia's eyes as she recalled the past.
"Don't say such things. I was once a princess of a nation... But what about Aaron?"
"God will take care of that. We have to believe in the legend. We have no choice but to trust the words of that wise dragon... He inherited both your blood and mine. You are wise, and I am brave... And he was born on the Day of Yesrahiya. You don't need to worry. We'll be able to see the General soon... Anyway, how did I end up being defeated by *that woman*? This is truly absurd."
"You were stronger than anyone. It's just time for you to rest after that long struggle."
"Tha-nk... you. The happiest moments of my life... were all related to you. I feel like I've only ever received... I've done something terrible..."
Halhas barely managed to continue speaking.
"No. What you've done for me is immeasurable. Do you know how grateful I was to God just for you being by my side? When you returned wounded, how sad I was... Even as a child, I prayed to curse our enemies for the first time. And then, having Aaron... the happy moments we shared in this village... they can't compare to the tedious life in the castle. All of this, you gave me.
I love you. Until death... I'm happy to die with you."
Vidia hugged Halhas tightly and kissed him. Vidia felt pity for him. His rough life... the scars etched all over his body and mind... they were greater than the wounds that now led to his death. No, it felt as if those very scars had driven him to this point. As if he had always anticipated such an end...
"Tch~ How sickening, I can't watch. Farewell, Princess Vidia!"
Anania expressionlessly cast her magic. With a blinding flash, they were... torn apart. Halhas and Vidia vanished, becoming one until the very end. They, who had promised to be together forever...
Their heroic tales, their adventures, their love, all vanished with them. Dark clouds began to gather in the sky. As if to cover their deaths...
Only the chilling wind and Anania's unpleasant laughter enveloped the ruined village and Aaron's heart.
Aaron watched his parents die until the very end. The mage, whom he had always believed to be on the side of justice, brutally murdered his father and mother. At first, Aaron's shoulders trembled, and he made low, pained groans, but then he screamed, "Mom! Dad!" and burst into tears, filled with hatred and sorrow...
Anania looked up at the upper floor of the hut from where the child's cries came. When her cold gaze met Aaron's, Aaron felt a shiver run down his spine.
"Hohoho, interesting, there was one dirty seed. Sargon, drag that one out!"
The dragon stretched its long neck towards the room where Aaron was. Aaron, startled, tried to move away from the window and into the corner of the room, but the dragon was faster. The dragon bit Aaron's clothes and pulled him out.
"Put me down! You demon!" "Hoho, I'll put him down. Put him down, Sargon!"
Aaron was dragged out of the window and fell from the second-story height.
Aaron felt extreme pain, but he neither screamed nor groaned. He thought it would only please that demon... He endured the pain and stood up.
"What a stubborn brat. Capture him alive!"
As the soldiers tried to seize Aaron, he drew his small dagger.
"Heh heh, a cheeky little brat."
The soldiers drew their swords.
"I said keep him alive!"
Anania yelled irritably. The soldiers looked disheartened. Even though he was a child, he held a knife and charged desperately.
Aaron's body was very agile. One light infantryman, who had underestimated him, suffered a severe leg injury from a knife, rendering him unable to use it. However, as the soldiers attacked, Aaron seemed to dodge once or twice but sustained injuries here and there. Still, he miraculously avoided all vital spots. Anania watched him with a curious expression.
Aaron, feigning evasion, lunged and picked up his father's sword.
Even though the sword hadn't been maintained for a long time, its sharpness was vastly different from the dagger Aaron had been holding. Even with Aaron's clumsy movements, it could inflict a fatal blow if mishandled.
As Aaron inflicted a large wound on one soldier and was about to swing his sword at another, he felt a burning pain in his back. Flames flickered at Anania's fingertips. Then a series of attacks followed. At that moment, the spells his father had shouted during their earlier fight flashed through Aaron's mind.
With the thought of "it's worth a try, whether it works or not," he simply raised his sword and shouted at Anania, "Ur! (Flame spell)!" To his surprise, flames erupted from the sword. The flames poured over Anania, who, having been complacent and watching as if it were a show, was hit squarely and writhed in pain amidst the fire. "Sargon, Aaargh! Sargon!"
The dragon then looked at Anania, as if questioning how she could have been defeated by such a mere child. Disfigured by burns, she irritably screamed.
"That child, such a spell... Sargon, kill that brat!"
The dragon flapped its wings towards Aaron. A tremendous gust of wind arose, blowing Aaron and the surrounding soldiers against the wall. Aaron felt as if his bones were shattering in agony. Nevertheless, he did not let go of the sword.
"Just like his parents. What a stubborn one. Sargon! Make that child drop his sword!"
The dragon toyed with Aaron. Aaron's consciousness gradually faded.
Seeing Aaron's body go completely limp after losing consciousness, it said to Anania.
"Isn't that too much? Even for a child. Burns can be healed with Irbuel, can't they?"
"I said until he drops the sword. He still hasn't dropped it. It's an order! Kill him! Have you forgotten our contract!"
The dragon then twitched and breathed fire at Aaron.
It was dark. Nothing could be seen. Suddenly, a ray of light shone, as if a spotlight had turned on. The figures of his mother and father appeared in the distance. Aaron ran towards them but they vanished. Anania's laughter echoed. A huge dragon approached Aaron. In Aaron's hand, somehow, was his father's sword. It was stained with blood. Horrifying blood. His own face was reflected in that blood. Aaron, startled, dropped the sword. The sword shattered like glass. The dragon held the corpses of his father and mother in its mouth. It chewed them with crunching sounds. "No! Mom! Dad!" The dragon sneered at Aaron. Anania pointed at Aaron. And then, she chanted an unpleasant spell. At that moment, a bright light approached, blocking Anania's path. It swallowed all darkness. That dazzling light seemed to have been known for a long time. An old friend...
The dragon stopped breathing fire. The fallen Aaron remained as he was. Despite the temperature being hot enough to melt everything around him. A white light enveloped Aaron's body, and his eyes were glowing.
"What is that?" The moment Anania spoke, Aaron leaped into the sky.
For some reason, Anania felt a shiver run down her spine at the sight. She instinctively realized that something extraordinary had happened.
"That's... damn it!"
The dragon, seeing the sight, muttered as if it knew something.
Aaron glanced

He quietly disappeared into the forest, dragging his father's greatsword.
All that remained was a small hut amidst the sound of rain and corpses scattered here and there.
The rain showed no sign of stopping. The rainy season had begun in Caledonia, Northern Draconia, once the land of dragons.

titleEn: Naver Open Beta: New Main Page
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

http://open.www.naver.com/

[http://open.www.naver.com/](http://open.www.naver.com/)
As of the 15th, the open beta has finally begun.
 
**1. Clean**
First of all, the impression is clean. At first, I thought it was similar to Yahoo, but the big difference from Yahoo is that there are no trivial navigators at all.
**Only the services that are truly well-used are placed.** Honestly... how many people would have clicked on those anyway? Haha.
**As someone who absolutely hates scrolling, I really like that the page has become shorter.**
 
**2. Outlinks**
The biggest changes are NewsCast and OpenCast...
Watching these, I lose track of time.
The surprising thing is that most of them are **outlinks**.
 
This is an action completely opposite to what traditional portals aimed for, which was to increase user dwell time.
News from media outlets via outlinks has started to be placed in the tens of millions of won per hour advertising space on Naver's main page.
Was it 34 media companies?? If you calculate... 800 million / 34... an enormous amount of PV is now starting to pour into these media companies...
I'm also curious if smaller media companies will have the equipment to handle that PV.
 
OpenCast has completely handed over the meta-blog format to users.
It seems much cleaner and better to look at than registering RSS.
 
**3. Development Potential of OpenCast**
OpenCast, for now, has the potential for abuse.
In fact, one of Naver's revenue sources and the biggest drawback of its monopoly was that it consumed most of the internet's PV.
However... opening this up to users means, in other words, distributing that PV.
Therefore, if power casters with many subscribers start to emerge, just as power bloggers and large cafes moved towards connecting to revenue,
there is a possibility that power casters will connect to revenue.
Power casters could collect useful data, create outlinks, or build pages to earn advertising revenue like Google AdSense.
From Naver's perspective, rather than taking the risk of implementing AdSense like Cyworld, it seems they aimed for another business model by distributing the PV, which was the foundation of their revenue, externally.
Of course, it's predictable that OpenCasts with severe abuse and excessive advertising will naturally lose popularity among users, and I wonder if there will even be casts consisting solely of advertisements, leading to subscribers of those casts or sites that distribute revenue.
While it's difficult to predict user behavior yet, it's clear that as a service within a major portal, it holds many possibilities.
 
**4. MySpace?**
I like that the personal information space, like MySpace on the right, has expanded. It's a bit different from Cyworld's,
and the direction it pursues is somewhat different, so it just looks like a summary.
For me, who frequently uses SMS services with Naver Mail mileage,
sending texts is a bit inconvenient as it requires moving to another page... In the past, I could send them directly with Flash...
It would be nice if cafes were also listed within the page, like Cyworld.
 
**5. Ads getting bigger?**
There's a lot of talk about ads getting bigger... **While they are bigger, they seem less intrusive than when they were in the middle.**
The proportion of shopping has relatively increased. This is inevitable because the page area itself has become smaller due to reduced scrolling.
Will prices in this area go up?
 
**6. Naver Cast, well-organized by category**
Naver Cast has become clean for each genre. What I barely knew existed before is now clearly organized.
 
**7. Smart Finder**
Something I hadn't seen before appeared right below the search bar, the so-called Smart Finder.
It seems they've named the feature that shows a specific page for a specific search query as Smart Finder.
It seems like one of the most 'Naver-like' services, which received both criticism and praise for directly editing search results.
It completely guides the desired query, making it easy for users to find what they want.
[Disease] Smart Finder... I'm surprised. So this existed.
Was there originally a [Health] category? (Is this new too?)
 
**8. Naver Lab**
Naver Lab has moved right below the search bar. In fact, general users weren't very interested,
but a service that was considered quite good by developers has moved to the most visible spot.
It seems like a clear indication of the direction Naver wants to go.
 
**9. Naver's distinct color, different from Daum**
It was definitely a revamp that strongly conveyed a different direction from Daum, whether for better or worse.
Daum emphasized being a media company, while Naver has emphasized being an information platform since 2008.
 
**10. End of News Editorial Fairness Controversy (?)**
A lot of thought and effort to shake off the fairness controversy itself is visible.
Now, it remains to be seen what impact these changes will have on consumers and the overall web market.
Will the talk about Naver being political... or editing... or whatever... diminish now?
It was obvious that Naver would die the moment it took on a political color.
This was because Naver's market share would clearly decrease if it lost either conservative or progressive users.
Daum, on the other hand, seemed to have tried to create a bit of that color, as there were areas where it could gain an advantage...
(And that strategy was actually effective, dealing a blow to Naver.)
Even when cursing the regionalism in politics, it's not just the Grand National Party that benefits from regional sentiment.
I wonder if the reason Korean politics cannot develop today is also because it's based on a dichotomy.
 
**11. Hoping for better portals**
Now, I believe we need to see how these actions by Naver will change the Korean web.
In particular, making half of the page outlinks was shocking.
Can this model work in Korea?
Now, I'm quite curious about what actions SK Communications and Daum will take.
Will Daum, which used to follow Naver's shadow, now realize that their directions are completely different,
and strengthen its media-centric identity to compete with Naver,
or will it introduce services similar in nature to Naver's? It remains to be seen.
Anyway... new changes will certainly exist, and I hope they are positive for everyone who uses the internet.

titleEn: Ugh, Why Is This So Hard?
contentEn:
It's difficult.
I didn't mean for it to turn out this way...

In the end, just grumbling.
Hurting and getting hurt...
It's foolish.

titleEn: Life often doesn't go as planned
contentEn:
That's how everything is.
Making big and small mistakes...

Often, I'm flustered, unable to handle things like a child.

Although I try to live with a clear conscience,
there are times I become selfish, and times I get annoyed.

Though there are many times the world seems completely askew,
I often forget that I am, in fact, one of the people who receive many benefits in this world.

The words, "Let's live with a sense of urgency"...
I seem to have forgotten them at some point.

Over the thirty years that have somehow just dragged on,
I only see a weak and lazy me.

I find it ridiculous.
And I also feel utterly insignificant.

With a vague expectation that I might have achieved something by this time,
I started my twenties, but ten years passed too quickly,
leaving only scars, and I barely managed to start a family.

But... am I even doing that properly?
When I ask myself that... I feel like a fool.

Didn't Kang Mae say something like this recently in 'Beethoven Virus'?
That he respected Hyuk-kwon, who protected his family and was faithful...
Compared to him, who was naive and even gave up his own dreams for his family, I look even more pathetic.

I built this out of love, but I'm not doing it well,
and I keep settling... I'm a fool....
I'm not proud of myself like that.

I'm depressed.

I don't know. Why am I suddenly feeling down again...?
As soon as the rush of work, which passed like a sudden shower, ended and a brief moment of calm appeared, a deep depression washed over me.
Today, I can't focus on work at all.
At times like this, I just want to immerse myself in my sadness and draw.

This 100-minute debate also left me deeply disappointed with the government.

The topic was the Internet Special Act, but I can only conclude that the government's remarks constituted a debate with [insult] and [punishment], but no [internet].
Whenever I talk about internet culture, I inevitably bring up the topic of PC communication again.
At that time, most users were so-called university students, and they were people who were bound to be more left-leaning than now.
In that environment, where there wasn't even an Information and Communication Network Act, were netiquette rules better observed than they are today?

At that time, there was a Korean language movement to use 'mureunmo' instead of the term S/W (software), and the 'Warm Band' movement to create a warm network.
Why can't we find such movements these days?

The reason is simple. Many people with insufficient character education have gathered, and both media and users are amplifying and reproducing provocative information.
And, once such an atmosphere takes root within the scope of any network space, it becomes a place where people can speak and curse in the same tone without feeling any guilt.

Whose responsibility is this?
The first responsibility lies in the historical development of the internet, which has pursued sensationalism.
If you were to rank tabloid-like internet newspapers, regardless of political stance, those filled with celebrity gossip and speculative articles would likely top the list.
Have you ever carefully observed where the portals that place such newspapers at the top rank in market share?
Clickbait articles are rampant, and beneath them are comments that match their tone.
A significant portion of the internet operates by chasing sensationalism. And this is linked to profit.

The government side claimed that there were sufficient laws, such as the Newspaper Act, but everyone knows how irresponsible they have been.
A single apology in a correction article tucked away in a corner makes everything 'OK.' Has anyone truly held them legally accountable for that?

Unlike in other countries, Korea's internet did not develop primarily by users.
That is a fact users should clearly understand. It developed through a few portals and content providers (CPs) that produced information.
While internet companies have grown massive and their influence has expanded, increasing the impact of portals, fundamentally, the CPs for news and information production were
traditional offline media, namely journalism and publishing, and it's no exaggeration to say that they have, in fact, exerted a dominant influence over portals.

The second responsibility lies with the portals.
I also work for an internet service provider, but it's the fault of not having timely mechanisms to prevent the spread of a problematic culture, especially with the explosive increase in users.
Currently, portals have 'like' and 'blind' systems. These are such mechanisms, but the problem is that they are not performing satisfactorily.
It's a 'sin, but not a sin' of portals that important and good information doesn't rise to the top, unnecessary or emotional posts aren't automatically filtered, and users aren't shown only the information they want.
However, as someone in the industry, I know well that no country or company has fully succeeded in this, and Korean portals are among those putting in the most effort.
When discussing Web 2.0, mechanisms for its ripple effects and negative functions are clearly necessary.
Simply put, personal information uploaded to P2P should be blocked. It cannot be said that the company operating the P2P server bears no responsibility to some extent.
However... it is technically impossible at present. But when discussing the meaning of Web 3.0's Semantic Web, the problem of having to distinguish the meaning of data will inevitably arise anyway,
and efforts for this are currently underway. Technology lagging behind the market – as a business operator, one cannot say there is no responsibility for this.

The third responsibility lies with our society, that is, with us.
In fact, we ourselves are the ones who have dirtied the internet. And the fact that we've become accustomed to speaking however we want means that others have also become accustomed to it.
In the past, one's ID was a source of pride, akin to one's name. Because of that, certain actions were perceived as bad or foolish.
The remark I liked most during the debate was the suggestion to create an [Internet Ethics] course in schools.
I truly empathized with that. What we lack is not [law]. It is [ethics].
Even if an utterance is legally valid, it can still be ethically unacceptable.
Furthermore, the reason why [ethics], not [law], is important in the cyber world lies in its [real-time nature].

Interestingly, both sides seemed to be ignoring this aspect.
Comments, by nature, are not [announcements] or [assertions], but rather [conversations].
However, the problem is that they exist as [text] and possess permanence.

And the power that fostered Korea's internet was precisely that [conversation], not actually [text].
[Text] is certainly very likely to contain better information. However, most information produced on the internet is [conversation], and since search engines are designed to judge its meaning and value, this aspect has the potential to be reproduced and cause problems.
After all, text is mostly less emotional and more logical, like the article I'm writing now.

However, so-called comments are just conversations.
If a law were made to arrest people for swearing on the street, what would people think?
Clearly, both uttering and hearing insults can already be punished under defamation laws and various other statutes, depending on the case, as you mentioned.
I was actually surprised to learn how strict the [Information and Communication Network Act] was after hearing the Democratic Party representative speak.
A characteristic of the internet is that all these conversations are recorded.
Therefore, it possesses real-time nature, and it is virtually impossible to regulate it.
It's easy to speak carelessly with inaccurate logic when driven by emotion.

I wholeheartedly agree with the statement, 'What's important is the victim.'
And for news comments and certain highly influential bulletin boards, I lean towards preferring a real-name system.
However, I am absolutely against any law that affects the entire internet space, or the entire portal space.
How could anyone write comfortably then...?

If you leave an inappropriate comment about someone else even on a friend's guestbook, others can see it, and since it's an internet space, couldn't that also become cyber defamation?

Finally, my suspicion regarding the government's push for legislation is nothing unusual.
It's simply indignation and suspicion that their words, always championing ideals, have never matched their actions.

If the Choi Jin-sil Act is truly a law for victims...
Rather than just thinking, 'Let's punish malicious commenters,' we should first consider who these malicious commenters are, why malicious comments have increased, and what the distribution structure is.
Malicious commenters are often, from a societal perspective, vulnerable individuals under stress.
Before punishing them, I believe it's a priority to consider why they post malicious comments and why the service has become one where they can do so.

As I always say, it's not about 'let's not punish what is clearly excessive.'
There is already 'punishment.' The problem is why they are simply and ignorantly contemplating 'punishment' again, without considering the underlying structure, system, or service.

Punishing problematic internet users is sufficient for portals. They are already entities that harm profits. It's also excessive to solely pass on the responsibility for them to portals again.

What's regrettable about the government... why do I feel like they're a bad service company that doesn't understand [users]?
When they brought up the Democratic Party's website, I almost died laughing. I got so angry at that point that I turned off the TV.
I didn't stay up late watching TV to see you two fight.

And for me, who had posted advice and policy critiques, not insults, on President Lee Myung-bak's blog,
and even registered with my real name on the Grand National Party's bulletin board only to have my posts deleted and even blinded, it was quite amusing.
It's just one episode, but for me, distrust might have already been sown from that moment.
Is the government truly... pursuing this legislation with a proper objective?

Another thing I'm curious about these days is why comedians don't imitate politicians anymore.
During the Roh Moo-hyun era, it was fun to watch that... he also got criticized a lot.

In conclusion...
It's about 'What is the true nature of that law?'
If they're going to do it, I wish they'd be more specific. That way, those in power can't control information as they please.
Either only arrest people who genuinely use abusive language, or arrest them after the scale of damage is proven...
And it must absolutely not be made into a one-sided law.

Oh. Also, a user's complaint that the portal only deleted the content after 4 days – that does seem like the portal's fault for a slow response.
However, blinding a specific post is not an easy task. And since such incidents weren't frequent, it's possible those functions were absent.
I am in favor of expanding such functions and creating systems.
However, the legislation must be realistically feasible, and I hope they refrain from making absurd demands to extort money from portals.
The technology for processing large amounts of data is not a vending machine.
I remember a certain J-member of a certain party brazenly claiming that 100% real-time filtering is possible on portals.
I wanted to ask that person,
'How would you design and implement that to make it possible?'
If that were possible, Korean portals would have already surpassed Google.

Technology has begun to threaten reality, and it seems we've entered an era where reality demands an absurd level of technology.
And unless we acknowledge the characteristics of technology, we are bound to go down the wrong path.
That is the era we live in today, and I wish those who lead the country in this era would also understand that fact.

I have many thoughts, but I couldn't consolidate them into one, resulting in this sprawling article.
The internet is not a one-way medium, but a two-way medium. This current government still doesn't seem to understand this point.
Above all, the biggest problem is that the government continuously fails to give the impression that it is 'listening to the people.'
Isn't the reason this law, regardless of its rightness or wrongness, is drawing suspicion, stemming from that very point?

More than anything else, what I most want to ask of the current government is... instead of always talking about 'misunderstandings' or whatever,
I wish to see [actions] that demonstrate 'listening to the people, including criticism.'
The reason the market is fluctuating is partly due to Mansu-hyeong's (a nickname for a political figure, likely referring to Lee Myung-bak) mistakes, but it's also clear that Mansu-hyeong's actions ultimately led to a loss of trust.

Even now, releasing something proper isn't working out well.

When will the [communication] and [restoring trust] that they claimed to have felt after seeing the candlelight vigil actually happen?
Will it happen around the same time stock prices rebound next year or the year after?

I always feel this, but Korea, an internet powerhouse, is incredibly dynamic. Seeing it always being put on new experimental stages...
As someone working in such an industry, I don't know whether to laugh or cry.

Rather, among the people there, Hong Seok-cheon seemed to have the highest understanding of the internet at a user level. ㅡㅡ

titleEn: Game Novels... Are They Still Being Written?
contentEn:
After seeing an article titled, "Cosplay... do people still do that?", I'm writing down some of my personal thoughts. You even said that BL (Boys' Love) is trash. Do you know why the scale of Korea's cultural industry is small? Or how Korea's internet industry grew so large? I'll briefly talk about the internet, which is my field of expertise.

The internet is a treasure trove of information, and you might say Google is the best for searching. But what is the most searched information on Google? It's not great academic papers, but the sex industry. There's a lot of controversy about portal sites filtering real-time search terms, but one of the elements of that filtering is precisely the sex industry. At night, adult terms invariably climb to the top. However, all portals block them.

In other words, the scale of the sex industry within the overall internet industry is enormous. And it's also true that this has brought about technological advancements along with the quantitative expansion of the internet. The internet exists because people gather and there's something to search for.

Looking at the early development of the internet in Korea, the primary goal was to gather people. In an era where there was no information, and services like Hitel and Nownuri had more information, what internet companies could do was directly produce information. From then on, portals like Daum and Naver began producing their own information, and that's why they grew differently from Google, creating Korea's internet.

Naver Knowledge iN also grew in a similar way. People gathered, and useful information emerged from within.

Now, let's briefly talk about the Japanese manga market. Have you heard the story of a professional Korean cartoonist earning 600,000 won a month? However, in Japan, there are people who make a living and succeed through doujinshi (fan-made manga). How can this be? It means that the market size is large enough for people to consume and participate. Furthermore, it's not taboo, and in the process, excellent works emerge and encroach upon the Korean market. Quite a few famous Japanese manga artists also came from the doujinshi market.

People say that because Korean sports are elite sports, they achieve excellent results in a small sports market. However, to some extent, it's not something to be proud of. It means that if it develops into a popular sport and expands its scale, it can achieve even better results. China also has elite sports, but because its population is so large, it has as many elites as Korea's entire population. What about the Korean manga market? The truth is, it's a market where even elites struggle to make a living.

Since I titled this "Game Novels," I'll talk about that again. People say that with the flood of game novels and mass-produced fantasy, there's nothing left to read. Or that it contributed to lowering the quality, but would people who read game novels suddenly start reading Park Kyung-ni's "Toji"? If a market doesn't exist in the first place, neither high-quality nor low-quality works can emerge.

The reason why Japan, with its cosplay and doujinshi markets, is enviable is that these serve as a solid foundation. In Korea's case, the market is so easily shaken that the failure of just one animation, "Armageddon," brought about a recession for the entire animation industry.

The biggest problem with the Korean music scene is also its thin layer compared to Japanese music, and this has led to the current situation. Disliking a specific genre is a personal preference. Frankly, I don't like the genre you mentioned either.

However, I believe that such a perspective itself contributes to lowering the competitiveness of our cultural industry. Eventually, groups who claim that comics like "Haedori's Adventure" from the 1970s are the most wholesome will reappear.

If viewed from such a perspective, even major broadcasts, anime, and comics have already become as low-quality as they can get. It's not for no reason that famous Korean cartoonists, finding it hard to make a living, advance into Japan. Mr. Park was also a truly regrettable case. Caught between ideals and reality...

titleEn: Naver Firefox: Random IT Thoughts / IT Stories
contentEn:
[http://t.lab.naver.com/firefox/](http://t.lab.naver.com/firefox/)
Naver Lab, which introduces Naver's new technologies, has created a Naver-exclusive Firefox. It seems like they just applied a Naver theme to Firefox... I'm not entirely sure what's different.

After using it, it's good. When needed, I mix it with IE Tab, and there are no other issues, and the perceived speed is definitely fast. If there's a problem, the code to remove the frame border doesn't work, making it look a bit messy. Was `frameborder` a non-standard tag...?

In places heavily reliant on scripts, there seem to be some differences from IE, causing issues, but otherwise, it looks fine. There's a lot of talk about ActiveX not working, but in practice, the places that use ActiveX are mostly government and financial institutions... Most importantly, public certificates don't work.

The speed, especially on image-heavy sites, definitely feels better than IE. The difference is significant, especially on sites with extensive scrolling, like shopping malls. However, I haven't tested if payments work well. I'd say there's a 90% chance they won't. Using IE Tab would solve it, though.. haha.

When installing plugins, Cyworld also runs without any particular issues. Naver Blog runs without any special effort. As for Chrome, I haven't tested it yet, but given that it's Safari-based, the speed should be good, but compatibility might not be great yet. Since a big company like Google is behind it, something even better will surely come out soon.

After using browsers other than IE... the biggest problem is not ActiveX, but rather the more serious issue of layouts breaking on general websites that haven't even been tested with other browsers. Portals, in general, are satisfactory.

A few days ago, I saw a nonsensical article, I think in PC World, claiming that 'a certain browser runs well on various platforms because it adheres to web standards.' ㅡㅡ;
Does Java run on various platforms because it adheres to web standards? Web standards mean consistent rendering across various browsers, and multi-platform support is merely an issue of whether that browser has been ported to various platforms.

The topic of web standards, which has been a hot potato for years, seems to have gained more attention recently, even among the general public, due to MS's web OS plans and Google's browser development. Worrying about Korea using a lot of ActiveX is an unnecessary concern.
The reason Korea used a lot of ActiveX was because IE was widely used, not because the goal was to violate web standards. If general users move away from IE in large numbers, websites will eventually be built to support other browsers.

The government, which always lags behind the market, is probably the biggest problem, though.

Instead of idealism detached from the market, like 'MS is unconditionally the axis of evil,' I'm linking a post that objectively explains the current situation and discusses it constructively. (However, developers are advised to click only if possible..)
[http://channy.tistory.com/136](http://channy.tistory.com/136)

Anyway, just changing the browser improved the speed, so it feels like an upgrade. haha. Sometimes IE7 would freeze, which was annoying... but there are no such problems now... Even IE Tab, which should be IE internally, doesn't show those issues. (Is it a problem with my PC?)

And here's a reflection from the developer.
[http://kldp.org/node/97601](http://kldp.org/node/97601)

titleEn: Eclipse CDT Installation Guide with SVN on Centos
contentEn:
**Let's set up an IDE environment in Linux (CentOS)!**
**Eclipse CDT Installation Guide using SVN on CentOS**
**** 
 : This document is the result of my own struggles to run a C++ project, originally developed on Windows, on Linux.
While VC++ setup methods were easy to find everywhere, setting up a Linux IDE tool in Korean was hard to find. Oh, these unfriendly Linux users...
 
Author: 숲속얘기 [fstory97@naver.com](mailto:fstory97@naver.com)
Original Author's Blog: [http://blog.naver.com/fstory97](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
 
**1. Eclipse Installation**
 1) **CentOS should be fully installed**: This saves the effort of installing Java and various libraries.
  : Test Environment (CentOS 4.6 64bit)

 2) **EasyEclipse**: Just extract the archive. (Other programs were not easy to install.)
   Reference: [http://www.easyeclipse.org/site/home/](http://www.easyeclipse.org/site/home/)
   Download URL: 
[http://sourceforge.net/project/downloading.php?group_id=131065&filename=easyeclipse-cplusplus-1.3.1.1.tar.gz](http://sourceforge.net/project/downloading.php?group_id=131065&filename=easyeclipse-cplusplus-1.3.1.1.tar.gz)
 
 3) Copy **SubClipse** plugin: A plugin for using Subversion
  Download: [http://www.easyeclipse.org/site/plugins/subclipse.html](http://www.easyeclipse.org/site/plugins/subclipse.html)
    Extract the archive and copy it into the same folder as EasyEclipse.
 
**2. Project Creation**
 : Project information will be stored in a folder named .metadata within the project directory.
(This folder is hidden, so you need to enable 'show hidden files' to see it.)
** Menu Click: File - New - Project - SVN**
  (Because we will be working with SVN)
 
**3. SVN Configuration** (If you are not using SVN, you can skip steps 3 and 5.)
 1) Checkout Projects from SVN - Create a new repository location
 2) Enter URL: Enter the URL of the SVN repository
 3) Select the URL - Finish
 
**4. Project Selection**
 - After SVN configuration is complete, the source project selection will automatically appear.
 1) C++ - C++ Project
 2) Executable - Select LinuxGCC (You must select Linux GCC for it to compile with that compiler; this is a compiler setting option.)
 3) Project name: Enter nhnOCR (An nhnOCR folder will be created under the workspace, and the project will be created.)
 4) Finish
 
**5. Files will be automatically checked out and downloaded from the SVN repository.**
 
**6. Project Name Setting**
  Uncheck 'Use default location' and set the folder where you want the project information to be located.
  Next
  Finish
** * When adding a new project, select File-New-Project and follow steps 4 and 6.**
 
**7. Project Settings**
 : Right-click on the project in the Project Explorer and click Properties.
** 1) Source, Include, Library Location Settings**
**    **: This is the same concept as setting paths in VC++.
  C/C++ General - Path and Symbols 
   - Includes: include folder
   - Library paths: library folder
   - Source Location: Set source location. If not set, the project folder becomes the default source folder.
                                           (Use this if the build folder and source location are different.)

** 2) Define Settings and Additional Path Settings**
  GCC C++ Build - Settings
 - GCC Preprocessor: Add Define 
                      Add compile options like _LINUX_.
 - GCC C++ Compiler - Directories: Add the required Include Path.
  OcrModule/Src Add (Relative paths are still unclear: I assume the base is the project path)
  When using FileBrowsing, absolute paths are entered.
 - GCC C++ Linker: Libraries - Add required libraries.
   If the library filename is LibModule.a, the library name should be 'Module', excluding 'Lib' and the extension.
 
**8. Build**
 Press Ctrl + B to build, and errors will appear in the Console window.
 * If 'Project - Build Automatically' is unchecked, automatic builds are disabled.
 
**9. Debug**
 Press F11 to debug.
 It's similar to VC++, so it's not difficult, and breakpoints can be set using the mouse or hotkeys.
 
**10. Add Created Project and New Source to Subversion**
 In the Project Explorer window, navigate to the path you created, and changed folders/files will be displayed.
 Right-click and select Team - Commit to reflect the changes.

 
**P.S. If you've followed these steps, even a VC++ user will have a working environment.**
**If anything was missed during the installation process, please contact me. I decline questions as I don't know much.**

Cyworld Malmi, Hyunshinong

Never have I wished I wasn't an NHN employee as much as I do these days.
It's not because Naver is being criticized.
I'm itching to say something, but as an employee, anything I say will obviously sound like an excuse or a defense, so I've even started wishing I weren't an employee at all.

Many of those who championed 'Anti-Naver' were based on groundless slander.
Initially, I thought the main proponents were power bloggers with open minds about web platforms, but as the company's explanations and positions were released, even if not fully comprehensive, their claims became quite controversial.
(What is true neutrality? How far does personal information protection extend? Honestly, it's not easy for anyone – bloggers, the government, Daum – to give a definitive answer to such questions.)
And what has emerged and remained are not users seeking discussion and communication, but rather those simply urging people to leave Naver, or engaging in collective actions of slander.

The Anti-Naver group has, at some point, started focusing on the closed nature of search and the possibility of subjective intervention in some systems.
Rather than questioning these fundamental functions of the web, it feels like they are throwing a tantrum with a much more political stance, unaware that their actions constitute aggressive abuse.

I have no intention of disparaging competitors like Daum, Yahoo, Cyworld, or other internet companies.
On the contrary, I commend the services of our competitors for making excellent attempts in their own ways and for engaging in fair competition to find their respective positions, considering them key players who have led Korean IT.

However, the claims of the Anti-Naver group are entirely different.
They completely disregard the revenue structure and development history of Korean internet companies, and it feels as if they are demanding money simply because they might be a fundamental source of Naver's revenue.
It's like saying, 'Many people pass by your store, so isn't your store doing well? Therefore, pay us taxes.' It just feels like extortion. (Are they gangsters?)

If they say Google returns income to netizens, I'd rather ask why Cyworld's similar revenue structure failed. Such ventures are not easy.
Furthermore, unlike Google, Naver offers many services beyond search. Does Google provide blog hosting space? Of course, Google *can* do it, it's not that they *can't*. In fact, everyone knows that Google is the world's top dog when it comes to abusing its monopolistic market position.

When I hear talk about Naver's utilization of its monopolistic position... it's almost absurd.
Rather, I'd like to ask if they've ever done business with SKT or Samsung Electronics. Naver employees might have become arrogant when they were in a position of power, depending on the individual. If such attitudes exist among employees, then any criticism would be deserved, and there would be nothing to say. This is a matter of individual rudeness before it is a company problem.
However, looking at the overall market structure, I have never seen any evidence to support claims of Naver abusing its monopolistic position.

What the government is saying as a reason for monopoly is that not putting ads before videos is for market monopolization... It's preposterous.

It's easy to say they're on the side of Chosun, JoongAng, and DongA (major conservative newspapers), but open your eyes again and check if Chosun, JoongAng, and DongA have ever spoken favorably about Naver. Compared to Daum... aside from saying it's 'neutral,' they are all very wary of the media function of portals.

What does this mean?
Offline media would naturally not welcome online media.
That's a fact everyone knows without having to think deeply.
Isn't it obvious that the entity they dislike even more than Daum is Naver, which occupies a significant portion of the internet? This is how the market structure is, regardless of whether it's progressive or conservative, Hankyoreh or Chosun/JoongAng/DongA.
Of course, even if Naver were to suddenly challenge offline media, it would be like hitting a rock with an egg until the day comes when the entire nation uses the internet more than TV.

If there are complaints, it's right to raise objections, and if still unsatisfied, to leave.
I, too, fundamentally like Agor's system. I also like DC (DC Inside).
However, the Anti-Naver movement by some users currently underway is not only difficult to understand but is also becoming so radicalized that it's hard to believe these are the same people who participated in non-violent candlelight vigils.

This is, in fact, empowering the voices of the government and media that advocate for indiscriminate regulation of the internet.

If we look at it that way, could Anti-Naver actually be government agents or another dark force from a competitor?
I indulge in some useless speculation.

While Naver is being criticized, looking at it from the opposite perspective, it seems to have taken on a bigger, new challenge: creating a system and atmosphere that can quell these aggressive tendencies and amplify the right voices among users.
This is not just a problem for Naver, but for the entire Korean internet.

Since this government came into power...
The IT industry is becoming tiresome, with only government regulations and users' political voices growing louder, rather than new technology issues.
Even though his ideals might have been a bit ahead of their time, I actually miss Jin Dae-je. ㅜㅜ

Is this also because of 2MB (Lee Myung-bak)?
With the entire nation angry right now, it seems absolutely nothing is going right in this country.

titleEn: Is the New Right Holding a Prayer Meeting
contentEn:
Oh my god.. This is insane..
As a Christian, I'm genuinely appalled.

I admit that conservatives can defend the president and oppose the candlelight vigils.
But.. what kind of prayer meeting is this?

Do you think all Christians oppose the candlelight vigils?
In a situation where Christians are already equated with conservatives,
Why are you dragging God into politics?

I really tried not to say anything, but this is just too much.
Go ahead and ignite anti-Christian sentiment.

God only wishes for His kingdom to come.
God doesn't care whether this nation is dominated by conservatives or progressives.
If you think beef imports are related to God's kingdom, then pray boldly.
Who are you praying for?

Will there be American beef in heaven? Or not?
If you have time for that, pray that the president and the people act according to God's will and goodness, not for political issues.
Absolutely, political good has absolutely no relation to God's good!

titleEn: Advice for the Hacked Grand National Party
contentEn:
[http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LPOD&mid=etc&oid=047&aid=0001942369](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LPOD&mid=etc&oid=047&aid=0001942369)
 
Seeing the news about the Grand National Party being hacked, I'm reminded of what an instructor once said: "The best security solution is not to make enemies."

Previously, a certain company advertised that their company's security was excellent, and then countless hackers attacked and breached it. The security company in charge reportedly found their advertisement to be a very embarrassing act.

Fundamentally, the best security solution is not about implementing an ironclad security solution, but rather, it's about not making enemies.

This is what I want to tell the Grand National Party right now.
If you make 40 million people your enemies...
No matter how ironclad your security is, or how many police surround you, what can't be done, can't be done.

titleEn: I'm Going Back to Using Cy
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

http://www.cyworld.com/fstory

It's already been about two years since I joined NHN, opened this blog, and started my activities.
During that time, my blog has accumulated 76,147 hits and 101 blog neighbors.
Considering it took over 5 years for my mini-hompy, which was featured on Best Minihompy and Cyworld Main, to reach 50,000 hits, this is an incredibly rapid increase in numbers.
During that time, my animation reviews were also featured on Naver's blog main page once.
There were people who occasionally left comments, but most of them weren't people I knew. It seemed they were mostly focused on the informational posts I uploaded. Especially when my personal thoughts on current affairs became hot topics, it sometimes even led to arguments.
But... the more I blog, the lonelier I feel.

I found myself lacking the confidence to click the 'Write Post' button and fill that wide page.
And I started to miss sharing affection and connection with many people while using Cyworld. Since Cyworld is centered around real names and focuses on personal stories, it seems the level of intimacy is naturally higher.
Moreover, after getting married and focusing on work, my social circle rapidly narrowed, and I sometimes found myself missing people.

Therefore, I'm crawling back to Cyworld.
I feel a bit like I'm betraying the company, but since search is the main thing anyway, there will probably be a day when mini-hompies are also searchable. ^^;
Meanwhile, Cyworld's features have changed a bit, so I'm re-adapting.
However, the fact that it's still paid and I really miss Naver's Smart Editor. OTL. (Blogs are all free...)

Hiding away on Cyworld to interact only with people I know,
I'll leave the blog for scrapbooking, testing, and QA purposes.

#### [A Country Doctor's Beautiful Journey](http://book.naver.com/bookdb/book_detail.php?bid=1532192)

By Park Kyung-chul
Leadersbook 2005.04.01
View Text
**Rating**

Recently, there was a book I was reading on the company shuttle, which even made me stop writing the fantasy novel I had been working on, putting everything else aside.
"A Country Doctor's Beautiful Journey"

The author, Park Kyung-chul, is a doctor who practices in the countryside. I came to know him when someone recommended his blog while we were talking about financial investment.
[http://blog.naver.com/donodonsu](http://blog.naver.com/donodonsu)
At first, reading his posts, I was amazed by his foresight and insight. What surprised me even more was reading his essay-like writings afterward. That's why the first book I bought by him wasn't a financial investment book, but this one, which is like his memoir as a doctor.

First, as someone who has recently started writing again, I couldn't help but admire his literary prowess. When I read his writing, I feel as if I am directly putting my hand into a patient's abdomen in a surgery room where warm blood is splattering, and I feel deeply moved by the many different types of people encountered at the scene of life and death. He doesn't achieve such writing skill by using flashy modifiers or by writing simply.
It's not like a fantasy novel where a grand event unfolds, nor is he a "munchkin" like Doctor K who can save anyone. Rather, he often lists specialized knowledge in his writing, which might make first-time readers wonder what he's talking about.
However, there is something different about his writing.
It is "sincerity." In his writing, he aptly points out the emotions of others through his own perspective and descriptions of people and situations, sometimes as an observer, sometimes as someone who grieves alongside them.

He is an "economic expert," a "skilled surgeon," a "columnist." Looking at his titles, he is clearly an "intellectual." But there is one more crucial thing. What emanates from his writing is not merely that of a "successful person" or a "knowledgeable person," but the "sincerity" that comes from his experiences as a doctor, witnessing countless lives and deaths.

Instead of artificially evoking emotions while looking at patients in desperate situations, like in some dramas, he sharply dissects situations and social injustices that our neighbors and family members might have experienced at some point.

I heard from someone that the reason he practices medicine in the countryside was due to a promise with a friend. (I haven't found that part yet.) In that way, he makes us reflect on what a true "intellectual" is, not just an expert, but as a human being.
And, on the other hand... no, he is a very enviable person. He has everything, but for him, these are merely means to pursue something higher. And even what he possesses makes me so envious that I feel jealous, but the very person who pursues that higher ideal is so admirable that it makes me bow my head in reverence.

In a world that only rushes towards success, he is a true intellectual who steps back and participates in the world. He is still alive.
Below, at a time when the debate between humanities and science is slowly resurfacing, I think this offers something to consider. Humanities is not "human." What science needs is not humanities, but "humanity." Although it is a field that explores "humanity," I believe that when it becomes an academic discipline, it yields the same results as science that has become an academic discipline. It's not something grand; it can be learned in relationships with colleagues, family, and seniors/juniors. The development of humanities does not restore broken families, nor does it suddenly make those who chase money pursue noble ideals.
And I don't think it's something that can simply be taught and known as an academic subject. "Humanity" is something to be experienced, to be felt, and it is necessary for all academic fields.

Gunslinger Girl Season 2, which I had been looking forward to, ended with episode 13, not long after it began airing. T_T
(Ah~ What do I watch now...) The quality has improved compared to Season 1. The depiction also seems to have become more detailed, to the point where you can feel the gunpowder scattering when a pistol is fired.
 
Even while writing my own novel recently, I've been listening to Season 2's OPENING on repeat.
And in the middle, Scarborough Fair... I even included it in the novel I'm serializing on Munpia.
 
Anyway, returning to the anime, regardless of the novel,
The title "Il Teatrino," as you can see, means "The Bad Girl with a Pistol."
If Gunslinger Girl Season 1 ended by hinting at Ange (Angelica)'s death,
Season 2 unfolds centering on the fight between Pinocchio and Triela. Is that around volume 6 of the manga?
 
Pinocchio and Triela are actually similar characters...
The final episode 13 is titled "Pinocchio as a Human..."
As episode 13 is the final episode, it seems to be the overarching theme of Season 2.
 
In the end, Pinocchio connects with the father who made him a killer.
And Triela also asks to be praised for defeating Pinocchio,
but her handler, Hilshire, embraces her without a word.
 
The title of Season 2, "The Bad Girl," ultimately refers to Triela, doesn't it?
Due to brainwashing called "conditioning," they kill people without any emotion, and rather, confirm their own existence through it.
Although this setting was also present in Season 1, this heavy atmosphere weighs down the entire Gunslinger Girl series.
And the sight of them killing people without emotion makes the scene even more melancholic and sad.
 
The father who made Pinocchio a killer is also the same setup for Pinocchio.
Also, the boss of the organization who saved Pinocchio and then made him a killer, perhaps not knowing how to express affection,
and Hilshire, who rescued a girl on the brink of death, inevitably made her a cyborg, and took on the role of her handler, are also similar characters.
 
That's why, in the end, when Rico asked, she said she wasn't happy even if she won.
From the outset, their battles, regardless of victory or defeat, are inherently melancholic and joyless simply because they are "girls with guns."
 
I also looked into the Fifth Republic Faction, which is the background for Gunslinger Girl. It's not a real organization, but the North-South issues actually exist. They gathered such circumstantial evidence to create a more serious background, like Palestine. Somehow, it reminded me of the fictional history in Ghost in the Shell, where Korea's North-South issues were made more severe, ultimately turning North Koreans into refugees. However, as it deals with real-world issues to that extent, the author's concerns do not seem to have been simple. In reality, it is said that about 1 million children worldwide, mainly in the Third World, participate in wars.
(It's truly amazing and enviable that they can use such a setting.)
 
Anyway, at least the story after this anime has already been released up to volume 8 in manga form, so I'll take comfort in that.

titleEn: President Yamada Creates a Salaryman's Paradise - The
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

http://book.naver.com/bookdb/book_detail.php?bid=4303605

#### [President Yamada Creates a Salaryman's Paradise - (Mirai Industry: The Myth of Human-Centered Utopian Management)](http://book.naver.com/bookdb/book_detail.php?bid=4303605)

Written by Akio Yamada | Translated by Kim Hyun-hee
21st Century Books
**Rating**

Can such a company really exist? A company that makes you wonder.
However, I was surprised that such a company exists in Japan, especially in manufacturing, where authoritarian companies are even more prevalent than in Korea.

However, calling it a "salaryman's paradise" in the title is a bait.
Infinite freedom, along with responsibility.
And leadership that fosters autonomous motivation was President Yamada's core.

His policies were reminiscent of cutting-edge IT companies like Google.
However, strict seniority and non-discriminatory treatment are, conversely, policies completely opposite to the American style.

Some people look to Samsung for Korea's growth engine.
But is that method unique to Samsung?
The large corporation and leader-centric approach, already adopted from Japanese general trading companies, has hit its limits.
One genius is powerful, but cannot defeat many diligent people.
Because a company is an organization formed by many, not just one.

A person is healthy only when their cells are healthy.
Many managers forget such a simple truth.
Humans are not machines.

That seems to be President Yamada's biggest principle.
However, that doesn't mean he sacrifices profit as a businessman.
In some ways, it might seem contradictory.

However, while many office workers today are actually doing it,
the higher one goes, the less people are seen and only numbers are visible, which might be the biggest mistake of today's business leaders and
leaders.

No matter how much I evaluate this and that, I am not a company leader.
However, as President Yamada wished, I personally desire strong motivation and passion.
Act like an employee, think like a president. Didn't someone say that? (I don't remember the source)

**0. Introduction**
First off, I didn't enjoy KartRider. {{IMG:1}}

Despite not being good at it, I enjoyed Need for Speed and Gotham Racing, {{IMG:2}}
and was a game user who insisted that real racing was better.

However, isn't casual gaming the trend these days? {{IMG:3}}
Anyway, I was tempted by an event at work that offered something if I played GogoSing and wrote a review on my blog, so I'll play it briefly and share my thoughts.

**1. Characters**
{{IMG:4}}
This is what GogoSing's characters look like. {{IMG:5}}
Cyber-style SD design characters... Honestly, I wanted to change to a more niche design, but I don't have enough items yet.
The big-eyed SD design is generally safe.
It seems like a good basic foundation for niche designs like glasses and aprons, similar to Paper Man.

Perhaps these kinds of characters will be racing soon.
{{IMG:6}}
(Just thinking about it makes me happy... {{IMG:7}} )

**2. Game Entry Screen**
{{IMG:8}}
This is the game screen.
It has a familiar layout.
Single missions and club features seem to be unimplemented yet.

**3. Drift**
{{IMG:9}}
The image above shows two drift missions. In actual gameplay, I just use them without really knowing which one I'm doing.
And I don't know which one is faster. {{IMG:10}}
It just feels like the more you slide, the faster your exit speed. {{IMG:11}}
What annoyed me most in racing games like KartRider and City Racer was that pressing Ctrl always triggered a drift. {{IMG:12}}
However, GogoSing is similar in that pressing Shift and an arrow key triggers a drift, but
releasing Shift and the acceleration given upon exiting a corner, when cornering,
very simply implements the thrill of attempting a drift with braking and then pressing the accelerator again to exit the corner.

However, compared to real games, the shortcomings are that there's no slip, no braking input, and speed doesn't decrease significantly during drift maneuvers.
If slip were to occur, the difficulty would become extremely high, so it seems they didn't consider it, given it's a casual game.

**2. Booster**
To play GogoSing well, cornering and boosting are important.
It feels like the game leans more towards maintaining top speed using boosters rather than relying on machine performance differences.
However, there's no mention of boosters in the game's missions. {{IMG:13}}
The fact that pressing the 'Z' button activates the booster
I only learned after reaching level 2, through a promotional video,
and there were even quite high-level players (LV3 or above) who didn't know.
Also, the popping sound when pressing the forward button right before starting
was a good effect for building tension before the start.
(Dokkang Turbo??)

**3. Machines**
I liked that this game is casual yet doesn't rely heavily on machine power.
Though it might change if paid items are released later...
There are Formula machines, Jet machines, and basic machines.
I don't really know the difference. {{IMG:14}}

The free Perry machine, available from Level 3...
{{IMG:15}}
This is what it originally looks like...
{{IMG:16}}
Some people usually mistake this for a kart...
Looking at the machine's shape, it's not a kart-type machine.
What came to mind when I first saw GogoSing was the Asurada design from Cyber Formula.

{{IMG:17}} ◀ [Asurada from Cyber Formula ]{{IMG:18}}
▲ [GogoSing's Trident]
The booster's appearance is similar.
In Asurada's case, it's a machine with an absurd speed of 700km/h (at this point, it's a rocket, not a car).
GogoSing's illustrations look even more similar. However, GogoSing seems to have a better design score.
This is partly because Cyber Formula's design is old, and while it's sleek, perhaps only minimally considering fluid dynamics,
GogoSing's design might be better because it has parts stuck on like a spaceship or a robot.
* Just as the **booster** was impressive in Cyber Formula, the booster is also the most crucial factor for victory or defeat in GogoSing.
(If you don't consider boosters, you're likely to keep leading only to lose at the last minute.)

**4. Theme Song**
Lastly... Jang Nara sang GogoSing's theme song... it's more addictive than I expected.
It's closer to an anime theme song, reminiscent of "Dodgeball King Tongki."
(Some even said it sounded like "Bbo Bbo Bbo" ㅡㅡ;)
{{IMG:19}}

titleEn: Let's Dig In: My Diary / Personal Stories
contentEn:
[This file does not support direct playback. Click to play in a pop-up window.](http://blog.naver.com/EmbedHttpView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=70027796511&hashKey=6c9f68e04bb2b4a7563401623097f4ba)
 
**Title: "I'll Eat Well :D"**
**** 
**Production Year**: 2005
**** 
**Screenplay.Direction.Cinematography**.-Heo Hye-yoon.
**** 
**Art Director.Animator**.-Kim Jin-young.Kim Ji-yoon.
 
**Sound**.-Elder. :)
**** 
**Running Time**. 4 minutes
**** 
**Filming.** nikon. D-70s.
**** 
**Synopsis:**
The story of a poor lizard family.
With a bad harvest,
Mother lizard
has no food to feed her children.
 
The children grow rapidly day by day,
and as it becomes harder and harder to find food,
 
when food is scarce,
her heart aches and tears fall every time she sees her once good-natured children becoming increasingly violent and fighting over food.
 
The children grow more and more violent,
trying to eat even a little more.
 
The mother grows thinner and thinner, sad and in pain.
As the children continue to grow,
no matter how much food she divides,
it is woefully insufficient.
The more so, the children only scream and fight each other.
So, the mother
prepares the last supper.....
 
 
 
:)
 
 
 
**Production Intention.:**
 
Thoughts on parental devotion.
This is the story of our parents,
who spare nothing for their children.
 
For their rapidly growing children,
she finally begins to cook and offer her own flesh.

But for the children who grow too quickly,
even that is always insufficient.

If a lizard's tail is cut, it grows back.
Therefore,
to feed her children,
she begins to cut off her own tail.
 
However, before a new tail can grow,
the children grow too quickly.
The mother lizard
grows thinner and thinner...
Eventually...
 
Even if she eventually loses her life due to such repetition,
regretting not being able to give more, she prepares the last supper and then
the lonely, quiet death of a parent,
and their desperate love.
 
We also wanted to reflect on our own reality, where we grow up eating our parents' bones and flesh,
yet live without knowing their sacrifice and love.
:)
 
 
**Main Materials:** Jovi clay, stone powder clay, wire, wood, gesso, acrylic paint,
           illustration board, aluminum, lacquer, fabric, cotton...
 
.-----------------------------------------------
 
Compared to other teams,
we started filming several months late,
so we had to push ourselves almost to death at the last minute.
:(
 
If I had planned the schedule better,
they wouldn't have had to suffer so much... *sob*.
 
Nevertheless, -
 
thanks to the talent and perseverance of Jiyoon unnie and Jinyoung,
and their affection and effort,
and
empowered by the encouragement of our beloved Professor Girin, -
we were able to finish safely.
Those miraculous days. :)
 
 
Source: [http://www.cyworld.com/nunmulsponge](http://www.cyworld.com/nunmulsponge) Heo Hye-yoon's mini-homepage
 
Heo Hye-yoon's mini-homepage, a good place to visit when feeling down...
I visited after a long time, and it didn't disappoint; she made something even more depressing with a short film...

{{IMG:1}}

http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=65991

			
				

#### [Forever the Moment](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=65991)

				Director Im Soon-rye
				Production 2007 Korea, 0 min
				**Rating** 
			
		

	
	

 
		
		
		
	
Their small rebellion in an unpopular sport.
The film immediately opens with a scene from a domestic handball final.
The excessively sparse audience.
 
After their victory, fireworks go off, but there's no one to congratulate them.
Just their small sense of accomplishment and
the fact that even if they win, they can't join a professional team.
 
In some ways, it feels like a feminist film.
As 'ajummas' (middle-aged women), they are pushed aside by younger players and are likely to be cast out simply for being married.
Just when it seems to highlight the unreasonable position of women,
it ultimately shows a stronger bond with the younger players within the shared framework of being women.
 
Anyway, if one were to analyze it too much in that way, it might become an overly provocative film.
Furthermore, in their social role as mothers,
 
they cannot give up that position, nor can they give up their dreams.
Perhaps the warm image of not abandoning the traditional female role of a mother and thinking of their indebted husbands
might be considered by feminists as a model that should never appear in media.
So, it might be better to exclude that aspect a bit from a feminist film perspective.
 
And above all, the position of these ordinary 'ajummas' in an unpopular sport
is compelling because it's a drama about people who are socially disadvantaged but do their best.
 
In the end, they didn't win the gold medal.
However, they did their best in their lives, and they say that is beautiful.
 
Somehow, I was reminded of Superstar Gam Sa-yong.
I recalled the lump in my throat when I saw him pitch for just one win.
The rebellion of the weak is always enjoyable for us, and their small achievements are more moving than the great achievements of geniuses.
 
And, at least in sports, the reason we cheer for the underdog is that such a drama
is precisely the hope of us ordinary people, who have always been socially disadvantaged, isn't it?
 
Anyway, Go, Korean Ajummas!
It made me think that I must watch the women's handball match at the next Olympics.

titleEn: Fantasy-Style Illustration After a Long Time / Original Work
A Conversation in the Dark / My Diary / Personal
contentEn:
When was it... The company had a few tickets, so I participated in an exhibition event called 'Dialogue in the Dark' with Eunhye.
A unique experience in a place where nothing could be seen.

It reminded me of an SF novel I read a long time ago.
A meteor shower fell from the sky, and one day everyone lost their sight.
Strange plant monsters appeared, and the protagonist, who had injured their eyes that day and was bandaged, could see the world, but...
The premise was, how should I put it...?

Everyone lives by seeing and judging many things with their eyes.
But how many people can truly see?

Eyes are rather a means to deceive us,
And now, in this information age, isn't an enormous amount of information pouring in through our eyes?

Sometimes, a world where everyone is blind seems wonderful.

What I felt in 'Dialogue in the Dark' was that while eyesight is something to be grateful for,
it also made me think that it's a fog that obscures our minds.
